name: Intellectual Developmental Disorder
symptoms: Deficits in general mental abilities (reasoning, problem-solving, abstract thinking, judgment, academic learning) and impairment in adaptive functioning resulting in failure to meet developmental and sociocultural standards for personal independence.

differentials.overlap: Profound cognitive developmental delay, delayed motor milestones, lethargy.
differentials.physical_signs: Macroglossia, coarse facial features, umbilical hernia, hypotonia, prolonged neonatal jaundice, dry skin, delayed epiphyseal closure.
differentials.workup: Newborn bloodspot TSH/Free T4 screening; Serum TSH (> 20-40 mIU/L confirms primary); Thyroid scintigraphy (technetium-99m or I-123) / ultrasound for thyroid dysgenesis.

differentials.overlap: Severe developmental arrest, microcephaly, behavioral irritability, hyperactivity.
differentials.physical_signs: Hypopigmentation (fair skin, blonde hair, blue eyes relative to family), eczematous rash, brisk deep tendon reflexes, musty/mousy odor to urine and sweat.
differentials.workup: Newborn tandem mass spectrometry; Quantitative plasma amino acid analysis (plasma phenylalanine > 360-600 umol/L with Phe/Tyr ratio > 3:1); PAH gene molecular testing.

differentials.overlap: Moderate-to-severe intellectual disability, hand-flapping, poor eye contact, ADHD-like hyperactivity.
differentials.physical_signs: Post-pubertal macroorchidism (testicular volume > 25 mL), long narrow face, prominent ears, high-arched palate, joint hypermobility (hyperextensible fingers).
differentials.workup: FMR1 DNA triplet repeat primed PCR and Southern blot analysis (> 200 CGG trinucleotide repeats confirms full mutation; abnormal methylation status).

differentials.overlap: Global developmental delay, speech and cognitive impairments across conceptual and practical domains.
differentials.physical_signs: Upslanting palpebral fissures, epicanthal folds, flat nasal bridge, Brushfield spots on iris, single transverse palmar crease (simian crease), sandal gap toe deformity.
differentials.workup: Chromosomal karyotyping / chromosomal microarray analysis confirming Trisomy 21 (47,XX,+21 or 47,XY,+21) or Robertsonian translocation.

differentials.overlap: Executive cognitive deficits, memory impairment, impulse control failure, poor social judgment.
differentials.physical_signs: Smooth philtrum (grades 4-5 on Lip-Philtrum Guide), thin vermilion border of upper lip, small palpebral fissures, microcephaly (< 10th percentile), prenatal/postnatal growth restriction.
differentials.workup: Standardized 4-digit diagnostic code assessment; Brain MRI (microcephaly, agenesis/dysgenesis of corpus callosum, reduced cerebellar/caudate volume); Documented maternal alcohol history.

red_flags: Coarse facial features, organomegaly, or skeletal dysostosis (suggesting lysosomal storage disease).
Loss of previously acquired developmental milestones (regression suggests neurometabolic degeneration, Rett syndrome, or epileptic encephalopathy).
Focal neurological deficits, asymmetric hyperreflexia, or persistent abnormal posturing.
Recurrent episodes of acute encephalopathy, vomiting, or lethargy precipitated by intercurrent illness or protein feeding.

name: Global Developmental Delay
symptoms: Diagnosed in children under age 5 who fail to meet expected developmental milestones in two or more domains (motor, speech/language, cognition, social/personal, activities of daily living) where standardized testing cannot be reliably conducted.

differentials.overlap: Developmental plateau followed by severe milestone regression after 6-18 months of normal development.
differentials.physical_signs: Deceleration of head growth (acquired microcephaly), loss of purposeful hand skills, stereotyped midline hand-wringing/washing movements, gait ataxia, episodic hyperventilation.
differentials.workup: MECP2 gene sequencing and deletion/duplication testing (mutations found in > 95% of classic Rett syndrome); Video-EEG monitoring.

differentials.overlap: Severe early developmental delay, delayed motor milestones, speech delay.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe neonatal hypotonia ('floppy infant' with feeding difficulty and poor suck), followed by hyperphagia and rapid development of morbid obesity after age 2; almond-shaped eyes, hypogonadism.
differentials.workup: DNA methylation analysis of chromosome 15q11-q13 (detects > 99% of cases, demonstrating absence of paternal active alleles); FISH or chromosomal microarray.

differentials.overlap: Sudden developmental arrest or regression, loss of social smile, visual inattention.
differentials.physical_signs: Clusters of sudden myoclonic flexion or extension spasms occurring upon waking (jackknife seizures), irritability.
differentials.workup: Urgent Video-EEG demonstrating pathognomonic *hypsarrhythmia* (chaotic, high-voltage, disorganized background with multifocal spikes); Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Profound motor and cognitive developmental delay, microcephaly.
differentials.physical_signs: Petechial 'blueberry muffin' rash at birth, hepatosplenomegaly, sensorineural hearing loss, chorioretinitis, microcephaly.
differentials.workup: Urine or saliva CMV PCR within first 21 days of life (gold standard); Brain CT/MRI demonstrating pathognomonic *periventricular intracranial calcifications* and polymicrogyria.

red_flags: Episodic muscle spasm clusters or sudden head drops upon waking.
Developmental regression (loss of previously mastered words, hand skills, or motor milestones).
Severe neonatal hypotonia with poor suck and failure to thrive.
Periventricular calcifications or dysmorphic structural features on neuroimaging.

name: Unspecified Intellectual Disability
symptoms: Presumed intellectual disability in individuals older than 5 years when standardized diagnostic psychometric testing is precluded by sensory/motor impairments, severe physical disability, or severe behavioral disturbance.

differentials.overlap: Unresponsiveness to verbal and visual stimuli, apparent severe cognitive deficit.
differentials.physical_signs: Absence of visual tracking, lack of auditory startle, tactile seeking behaviors; cognitive architecture and receptive cortex may be preserved.
differentials.workup: Visual Evoked Potentials (VEP); Auditory Brainstem Response (ABR); Specialized tactile-based psychological assessment.

differentials.overlap: Absence of expressive spoken communication, total dependence in activities of daily living.
differentials.physical_signs: Pseudobulbar palsy, severe spasticity, hypertonia, scissoring gait, contractures; receptive cognitive abilities often far exceed expressive motor capabilities.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (periventricular leukomalacia, cortical/subcortical watershed injury); Specialized nonverbal augmentative assistive communication evaluation.

differentials.mimic: Severe Traumatic Brain Injury / Locked-In State (G81.9, G83.5)
differentials.overlap: Apparent unresponsiveness, mutism, complete functional dependency.
differentials.physical_signs: Quadriplegia and lower cranial nerve paralysis with preserved vertical eye movements and eyelid blinking; intact pupillary responses.
differentials.workup: High-resolution Brain MRI (ventral pontine infarction or severe axonal shearing); Functional MRI or Quantitative EEG showing cortical response to spoken commands.

red_flags: Total absence of peripheral sensory screening (vision and hearing) prior to diagnostic labeling.
Incongruence between expressive communication deficit and complex preserved eye-tracking comprehension.
Structural brain lesions involving sensory pathways or motor efferents with sparing of associative neocortex.

name: Language Disorder
symptoms: Persistent difficulties in the acquisition and use of language across modalities (spoken, written, sign language) due to deficits in comprehension or production (reduced vocabulary, limited sentence structure, discourse impairments).

differentials.overlap: Delayed vocabulary development, poor speech comprehension, failure to follow spoken directions.
differentials.physical_signs: Lack of startle to sudden loud sounds, excessive reliance on visual cues/gestures, compensatory visual hypervigilance.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive Pediatric Audiogram; Auditory Brainstem Response (ABR); Otoacoustic Emissions (OAE) testing.

differentials.overlap: Fluctuating speech comprehension, delayed expressive syntax, apparent inattention.
differentials.physical_signs: Dull or retracted tympanic membranes with decreased mobility, presence of middle ear air-fluid levels or bubbles.
differentials.workup: Pneumatic Otoscopy; Tympanometry (demonstrating flat Type B tympanogram); ENT surgical evaluation.

differentials.overlap: Dramatic loss of receptive and expressive language skills after age 3 following normal early language development.
differentials.physical_signs: Auditory verbal agnosia (child acts as if suddenly deaf to spoken words but hears phone ring or doorbell); normal peripheral audiogram.
differentials.workup: All-night sleep EEG (recommended gold standard: continuous spike-and-wave discharges during slow-wave sleep [CSWS] occupying > 85% of non-REM sleep); Brain MRI.

red_flags: Sudden or subacute loss of previously mastered language comprehension or production (requires urgent sleep EEG for Landau-Kleffner).
Lack of formal objective audiometry in any child presenting with delayed language.
Fluctuating hearing sensitivity associated with frequent upper respiratory or ear infections.

name: Speech Sound Disorder
symptoms: Persistent difficulty with speech sound production that interferes with speech intelligibility or prevents verbal communication of messages, not resulting from congenital or acquired physical conditions.

differentials.overlap: Impaired articulation, particularly of lingual sounds (t, d, n, l, th, s, z).
differentials.physical_signs: Short, thickened lingual frenulum restricting tongue protrusion past mandibular incisors; heart-shaped indentation of tongue tip on protrusion.
differentials.workup: Oral structural examination assessing Hazelbaker Assessment Tool for Lingual Frenulum Function; ENT surgical evaluation.

differentials.overlap: Severe speech unintelligibility, hypernasal resonance, nasal air emission during consonant production.
differentials.physical_signs: Bifid uvula, palpable notch in posterior border of hard palate, central zona pellucida of soft palate.
differentials.workup: Nasopharyngoscopy; Multiview videofluoroscopy during speech; Surgical cleft palate assessment.

differentials.mimic: Childhood Apraxia of Speech / Neurological Dysarthria (G80.0 / R47.1)
differentials.overlap: Highly unintelligible speech, inconsistent speech sound errors, severe communication frustration.
differentials.physical_signs: Inconsistent consonant/vowel errors on repeated productions, impaired coarticulatory transitions between sounds, inappropriate lexical stress.
differentials.workup: Motor speech evaluation; Brain MRI (ruling out perisylvian polymicrogyria, opercular lesions, or basal ganglia pathology).

red_flags: Hypernasal speech resonance or nasal regurgitation of fluids (indicates velopharyngeal insufficiency or occult submucous cleft).
Bifid uvula or palpable notch in hard palate.
Oral-motor groping during speech attempts with progressive deterioration on multisyllabic sequences.

name: Childhood-Onset Fluency Disorder (Stuttering)
symptoms: Disturbances in the normal fluency and time patterning of speech (sound/syllable repetitions, prolongations, broken words, audible or silent blocks, circumlocutions, physical tension during production).

differentials.overlap: Disrupted speech fluency, repetitions, blocks.
differentials.physical_signs: Onset in adulthood or adolescence following stroke, traumatic brain injury, or encephalitis; disfluencies occur equally on grammatical and substantive words, without secondary facial grimacing.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging (evaluating acute/chronic ischemic stroke or subcortical lesions); Neurological exam.

differentials.overlap: Sudden emergence of stuttering-like speech blocks and repetitions.
differentials.physical_signs: Chronologically linked to initiation or dose escalation of psychotropic drugs (clozapine, methylphenidate, bupropion, lithium).
differentials.workup: Detailed pharmacotherapy audit; Assessment of serum drug levels; Trial of dose reduction or medication switch.

differentials.overlap: Rapid, irregular speech rate with frequent speech breakdowns.
differentials.physical_signs: Excessive normal disfluencies (interjections, revisions), slurred/collapsed syllables, lack of awareness of speech difficulty (unlike stuttering where speaker is acutely aware).
differentials.workup: Standardized Cluttering Assessment; Speech-language pathology evaluation.

red_flags: Sudden emergence of stuttering in older children, adolescents, or adults without childhood history.
Accompanying focal neurological signs (hemiparesis, facial asymmetry, visual changes).
Temporal correlation with starting or increasing psychotropic medications.

name: Social (Pragmatic) Communication Disorder
symptoms: Persistent difficulties in the social use of verbal and nonverbal communication (deficits in greeting/sharing, matching context, taking turns, understanding non-literal meaning like sarcasm/humor), with *absence* of restricted/repetitive patterns of behavior.

differentials.overlap: Severe social communication deficits, peer relationship difficulties, literal interpretation of language.
differentials.physical_signs: Presence of repetitive motor mannerisms, adherence to inflexible nonfunctional routines, intense restricted fixated interests, sensory hyper/hyporeactivity (which excludes pure SPCD).
differentials.workup: Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS-2); Autism Diagnostic Interview-Revised (ADI-R).

differentials.overlap: Difficulty following rapid social conversation in groups, poor listening comprehension.
differentials.physical_signs: Marked deterioration in understanding speech specifically in the presence of background acoustic noise; normal pure-tone thresholds.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive Central Auditory Processing Battery (dichotic digits, pitch pattern sequence test, speech-in-noise testing).

differentials.overlap: Inability to grasp emotional prosody, sarcasm, humor, or implicit social context.
differentials.physical_signs: Left-sided hemispatial neglect, flat affective prosody, visuospatial constructional deficits.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI; Standardized right hemisphere cognitive battery (Mini Inventory of Right Brain Injury).

red_flags: Presence of stereotyped motor behaviors or sensory sensitivities (indicates ASD rather than SPCD).
Marked degradation of speech comprehension exclusively in noisy classrooms or social settings (warrants CAPD evaluation).
Focal neurological deficits or lateralized spatial inattention.

name: Autism Spectrum Disorder
symptoms: Persistent deficits in social communication and social interaction across multiple contexts (social-emotional reciprocity, nonverbal communicative behaviors, developing relationships) accompanied by restricted, repetitive patterns of behavior, interests, or activities.

differentials.overlap: Poor eye contact, social avoidance, hand-flapping, repetitive speech, sensory defensiveness.
differentials.physical_signs: Macroorchidism (post-pubertal), long facies, prominent ears, hyperextensible joints, high-arched palate.
differentials.workup: FMR1 DNA testing (PCR and Southern blot for CGG repeat expansion > 200 repeats).

differentials.overlap: Autistic behaviors in 40-50% of patients, severe sensory sensitivities, repetitive stereotypies.
differentials.physical_signs: Ash-leaf hypopigmented macules (>= 3 on Wood's lamp exam), facial angiofibromas (adenoma sebaceum), shagreen patches, refractory infantile spasms/seizures.
differentials.workup: Wood's UV lamp skin exam; Brain MRI (cortical tubers, subependymal nodules); Genetic testing (TSC1, TSC2).

differentials.overlap: Severe communicative impairment, lack of speech, hand-flapping, repetitive behaviors.
differentials.physical_signs: Happy/paroxysmal laughter demeanor, microcephaly, severe motor ataxia, jerky puppet-like movements, protruding tongue, hypopigmentation.
differentials.workup: DNA methylation analysis of chromosome 15q11-q13 (absence of maternal contribution); UBE3A gene sequencing.

differentials.overlap: Social withdrawal, repetitive motor stereotypies, severe behavioral agitation.
differentials.physical_signs: Fair complexion/blue eyes relative to family, eczema, brisk reflexes, mousy body odor.
differentials.workup: Plasma quantitative amino acid analysis (phenylalanine > 360-600 umol/L).

differentials.overlap: Failure to orient to name call, apparent social aloofness, delay in expressive and receptive language.
differentials.physical_signs: Normal eye contact when engaged face-to-face, expressive nonverbal gestures, lack of acoustic startle reflex.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive Audiometric Evaluation (ABR, OAE, audiogram).

red_flags: Presence of >= 3 hypopigmented ash-leaf macules under Wood's lamp (demands urgent brain MRI for Tuberous Sclerosis).
History of unprovoked developmental regression after 12-24 months of age.
Refractory seizure activity, infantile spasms, or episodic staring spells.
Post-pubertal macroorchidism or long narrow facial structure.

name: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder
symptoms: A persistent pattern of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity that interferes with functioning or development, characterized by wandering off task, lacking persistence, difficulty sustaining focus, disorganization, excessive motor activity, or hasty actions occurring in two or more settings.

differentials.overlap: Severe daytime motor restlessness, hyperactivity, emotional lability, poor concentration, academic failure.
differentials.physical_signs: Tonsillar/adenoidal hypertrophy (Brodsky grade 3-4+), chronic mouth breathing, morning headache, nocturnal snoring/gasps, nocturnal enuresis.
differentials.workup: Pediatric Overnight Polysomnography (Apnea-Hypopnea Index [AHI] >= 1 event/hour diagnostic); ENT surgical evaluation.

differentials.overlap: Frequent brief lapses of attention, staring into space, 'daydreaming', missed instructions.
differentials.physical_signs: Sudden behavioral arrest lasting 5-15 seconds, subtle eyelid fluttering, immediate return to baseline with zero postictal state; elicited by 3 minutes of hyperventilation.
differentials.workup: Routine EEG with hyperventilation demonstrating classic 3-Hz generalized spike-and-wave discharges.

differentials.overlap: Motor restlessness, fidgeting, emotional lability, distractibility, insomnia, academic decline.
differentials.physical_signs: Fine hand tremor, resting tachycardia (> 100 bpm), heat intolerance, warm moist skin, exophthalmos, diffuse goiter, weight loss despite increased appetite.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (suppressed < 0.01 mIU/L); Free T4 and Free T3 (markedly elevated); Thyroid antibodies (TRAb/TSI).

differentials.overlap: Severe impulsivity, inattention, hyperactivity, aggression, cognitive and learning impairments.
differentials.physical_signs: Microcytic anemia, pallor, intermittent abdominal colic, Burton line on gingival margins, pica history.
differentials.workup: Whole blood lead level (BLL >= 3.5 mcg/dL abnormal per CDC); Peripheral blood smear (basophilic stippling); Long bone radiographs (radiodense lead lines).

differentials.overlap: Failure to follow verbal instructions, apparent distractibility, classroom behavioral disruption.
differentials.physical_signs: History of recurrent ear infections, fluid levels behind tympanic membrane, air-bone gap on audiometry.
differentials.workup: Pneumatic otoscopy; Tympanometry; Pure-tone audiogram.

red_flags: Loud nightly snoring, gasping, or witnessed nocturnal apnea episodes.
Frequent, stereotyped brief staring spells that can be provoked by hyperventilation.
Resting sinus tachycardia, heat intolerance, or unprovoked weight loss.
Living in pre-1978 housing with peeling paint or known lead plumbing.

name: Specific Learning Disorder
symptoms: Persistent difficulties learning and using academic skills (inaccurate or slow reading, difficulty understanding meaning, spelling difficulties, written expression problems, mastering number sense or mathematical reasoning), persisting for >= 6 months despite targeted interventions.

differentials.mimic: Uncorrected Refractive Error / Convergence Insufficiency (H52.1, H52.2, H51.11)
differentials.overlap: Difficulty tracking words, slow reading rate, skipping lines, task avoidance, headaches during reading.
differentials.physical_signs: Squinting, rubbing eyes, eye strain (asthenopia), near point of convergence receded (> 6 cm), exophoria at near.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive cycloplegic ophthalmologic refraction; Binocular vision and near-point convergence testing.

differentials.overlap: Severe phonological decoding difficulties, spelling deficits, poor reading comprehension.
differentials.physical_signs: Normal peripheral pure-tone audiometry with marked failure on dichotic speech and temporal patterning tests.
differentials.workup: Full Audiologic and Central Auditory Processing Battery.

differentials.overlap: High incidence of specific learning disabilities (especially reading and visual-spatial math deficits) and ADHD.
differentials.physical_signs: >= 6 Café-au-lait spots (> 5 mm prepubertal), axillary/inguinal freckling (Crowe sign), iris Lisch nodules, neurofibromas.
differentials.workup: Clinical NIH criteria; Slit-lamp exam; Brain/orbit MRI; NF1 genetic analysis.

red_flags: Severe eye strain, blurred vision, or diplopia occurring within minutes of reading.
Multiple café-au-lait macules or axillary freckling.
Discrepancy between intact auditory understanding and isolated printed text processing without prior vision screening.

name: Developmental Coordination Disorder
symptoms: The acquisition and execution of coordinated motor skills is substantially below that expected given the individual's chronological age and opportunity for skill learning, manifested as clumsiness (dropping/bumping into objects), slowness, and inaccuracy of motor performance.

differentials.overlap: Frequent tripping, falling, clumsy gait, difficulty climbing stairs or running.
differentials.physical_signs: Gowers sign (using hands to 'walk up' thighs to rise from floor); calf pseudohypertrophy; waddling gait; lumbar lordosis; loss of motor skills.
differentials.workup: Serum Creatine Kinase (CK) (markedly elevated > 10,000-30,000 U/L in DMD); DMD gene multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA) or sequencing.

differentials.overlap: Progressive motor clumsiness, uncoordinated hand movements, unsteady gait.
differentials.physical_signs: Subacute onset, wide-based truncal ataxia, dysmetria on finger-to-nose, intention tremor, morning headache with vomiting, papilledema.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with and without gadolinium (visualizing posterior fossa/cerebellar vermis mass and hydrocephalus); Fundoscopy.

differentials.overlap: Deteriorating motor coordination, handwriting degradation, tremor, clumsiness in older children/adolescents.
differentials.physical_signs: Kayser-Fleischer rings on slit-lamp, wing-beating tremor, dystonia, dysarthria, hepatomegaly.
differentials.workup: Slit-lamp exam; Serum ceruloplasmin (< 20 mg/dL); 24-hour urine copper (> 40-100 mcg/24h); Liver enzymes.

red_flags: Positive Gowers sign (indicates progressive proximal muscle weakness, not benign developmental dyspraxia).
Progressive deterioration in motor coordination or loss of previously acquired motor milestones.
Subacute gait ataxia accompanied by morning headaches or persistent vomiting.
Kayser-Fleischer corneal rings or abnormal involuntary movements.

name: Stereotypic Movement Disorder & Tic Disorders
symptoms: Repetitive, seemingly driven, and apparently purposeless motor behaviors (hand flapping, body rocking, head banging) OR sudden, rapid, recurrent, non-rhythmic motor movements and vocalizations preceded by a premonitory urge.

differentials.overlap: Sudden dramatic explosion of motor/vocal tics, severe OCD, emotional lability.
differentials.physical_signs: Overnight dramatic onset, choreiform movements, deterioration in handwriting, associated with recent Group A Streptococcal pharyngitis.
differentials.workup: Rapid Strep throat swab / culture; Anti-streptolysin O (ASO) and Anti-DNase B titers; Autoimmune workup.

differentials.overlap: Involuntary motor jerks, behavioral disinhibition, emotional lability.
differentials.physical_signs: Choreiform movements (purposeless, continuous, non-stereotyped movements of limbs/face); milkmaid's grip; darting tongue; history of acute rheumatic fever; heart murmur.
differentials.workup: Jones criteria evaluation; ASO/Anti-DNase B titers; Echocardiogram (carditis/valvulitis); Throat culture.

differentials.overlap: Motor and vocal tics emerging in adolescence or adulthood.
differentials.physical_signs: Onset following prolonged exposure to dopamine receptor antagonists (antipsychotics, antiemetics); absence of classic premonitory urge; concurrent tardive dyskinesia.
differentials.workup: Medication history audit; Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale (AIMS) exam; Brain MRI.

red_flags: Explosive, overnight onset of severe tics following a sore throat or viral illness (PANDAS/PANS).
Continuous, non-stereotyped flowing choreic movements with milkmaid's grip (Sydenham chorea).
Tics emerging de novo in an adult on chronic neuroleptic medications (Tardive Tourettism).

name: Delusional Disorder
category: Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorders
symptoms: Presence of one (or more) non-bizarre or bizarre delusions with a duration of 1 month or longer, without meeting Criterion A for schizophrenia (hallucinations, disorganized speech, disorganized behavior are not prominent), and functioning is not markedly impaired outside the impact of the delusion.

differentials.overlap: Circumscribed paranoid or persecutory delusions with preserved cognitive function and affect.
differentials.physical_signs: Anosmia (loss of smell), subtle optic nerve pallor, Foster Kennedy syndrome (ipsilateral optic atrophy + contralateral papilledema), morning headache.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with and without gadolinium (high-resolution coronal T1/T2/FLAIR); Formal cranial nerve and fundoscopic exam.

differentials.overlap: Paranoid delusions, persecutory ideation, sleep disturbance, irritability.
differentials.physical_signs: Moon facies, facial plethora, buffalo hump, central obesity, wide purple abdominal striae (> 1 cm), proximal muscle weakness.
differentials.workup: 24-hour urinary free cortisol (> 3x ULN); 1 mg overnight Dexamethasone suppression test (serum cortisol failure to suppress < 1.8 mcg/dL at 8 AM); Pituitary MRI.

differentials.overlap: Fixed circumscribed persecutory delusions, jealousy, somatic delusions (e.g. formication/delusional parasitosis).
differentials.physical_signs: Mydriasis, tachycardia, hypertension, diaphoresis, excoriations on skin from picking.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive Urine Drug Screen (amphetamines, methylphenidate, cocaine, synthetic cathinones); Medication audit.

differentials.overlap: Delusional misidentification syndromes (Capgras, Fregoli, or Somatoparaphrenia).
differentials.physical_signs: Left hemispatial neglect, left visual field cut (homonymous hemianopia), anosognosia (denial of deficit).
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI); Carotid duplex ultrasound; Echocardiogram.

red_flags: New onset of fixed delusions in patients over age 40 without prior psychiatric history.
Olfactory deficit (anosmia) or visual field restriction accompanying delusions.
Presence of cushingoid physical features (purple striae, buffalo hump, proximal myopathy).
Delusional parasitosis / formication accompanied by dilated pupils and tachycardia.

name: Brief Psychotic Disorder
category: Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorders
symptoms: Sudden onset of at least one core psychotic symptom (delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, or grossly disorganized/catatonic behavior) lasting at least 1 day but less than 1 month, with eventual full return to premorbid level of functioning.

differentials.overlap: Explosive acute onset of florid psychosis, bizarre behavior, visual/auditory hallucinations, catatonia in young adults/adolescents.
differentials.physical_signs: Orofacial dyskinesias (chewing, tongue writhing), autonomic instability (hyperthermia, tachycardia, labile BP), central hypoventilation, seizures.
differentials.workup: CSF and serum anti-GluN1 NMDA receptor antibody panel; Lumbar puncture (pleocytosis, oligoclonal bands); Pelvic ultrasound/MRI (screening for ovarian teratoma in young females); Continuous video-EEG.

differentials.overlap: Acute confusion, bizarre behavioral disinhibition, paranoia, olfactory hallucinations, memory disruption.
differentials.physical_signs: Fever, neck stiffness, temporal lobe seizures, dysphasia, rapid deterioration of consciousness.
differentials.workup: Lumbar puncture with CSF HSV-1/2 PCR; Brain MRI (asymmetric temporal and inferior frontal T2/FLAIR hyperintensity); Immediate IV acyclovir initiation.

differentials.overlap: Sudden acute psychotic delirium, hallucinations, agitation, severe anxiety, confusion.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe colicky abdominal pain out of proportion to physical exam, tachycardia, dark port-wine urine, motor weakness.
differentials.workup: Spot urine porphobilinogen (PBG > 5-10x ULN during acute attack); Erythrocyte PBG deaminase activity; HMBS gene sequencing.

differentials.overlap: Violent agitation, acute paranoia, hallucinations, combativeness, delirium.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe tachycardia, hyperthermia, mydriasis, diaphoresis, muscle rigidity, rhabdomyolysis.
differentials.workup: Expanded gas chromatography-mass spectrometry toxicology panel; Serum CK (rhabdomyolysis); Serum electrolytes.

red_flags: Fever, autonomic instability, or fluctuating level of consciousness.
Involuntary orofacial dyskinesias or choreoathetosis in a young psychotic patient.
Severe abdominal pain preceding psychotic agitation.
Absence of psychiatric family history with explosive first-episode presentation in a medically unstable patient.

name: Schizophreniform Disorder
category: Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorders
symptoms: An episode of psychotic illness characterized by delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, disorganized behavior, and/or negative symptoms lasting at least 1 month but less than 6 months, without requiring the social/occupational decline demanded by schizophrenia.

differentials.overlap: Subacute emergence of delusions, hallucinations, behavioral regression, emotional lability over several months.
differentials.physical_signs: Argyll Robertson pupils (accommodate to near focus but do NOT react to direct light), tremors of tongue and hands, slurred speech, hyperreflexia.
differentials.workup: Serum treponemal antibody screen (TP-PA, FTA-ABS) + RPR/VDRL; Lumbar puncture (CSF-VDRL, CSF pleocytosis, elevated protein).

differentials.overlap: Psychosis, paranoia, affective blunting, cognitive decline over 1-5 months.
differentials.physical_signs: Malar butterfly rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, non-deforming polyarthritis, Raynaud phenomenon, serositis.
differentials.workup: Antinuclear Antibodies (ANA); Anti-dsDNA; Anti-Smith (anti-Sm); Serum complement levels (low C3, C4); Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Psychosis, personality deterioration, affective symptoms, cognitive slowing in late adolescence.
differentials.physical_signs: Kayser-Fleischer rings on slit-lamp, wing-beating tremor, dystonia, parkinsonian rigidity, hepatomegaly.
differentials.workup: Slit-lamp exam; Serum ceruloplasmin (< 20 mg/dL); 24-hour urine copper (> 100 mcg/24h); ATP7B gene testing.

differentials.overlap: Fluctuating psychosis, hallucinations, cognitive decline, emotional lability over 2-6 months.
differentials.physical_signs: Stimulus-sensitive myoclonus, tremor, hyperreflexia, ataxia, often in euthyroid individuals.
differentials.workup: Serum Anti-Thyroperoxidase (anti-TPO) antibodies (> 200-500 IU/mL); Anti-Thyroglobulin antibodies; TSH/Free T4; CSF analysis.

red_flags: Argyll Robertson pupils (small, irregular pupils unreactive to light).
Malar butterfly facial rash, photosensitivity, or systemic polyarthralgias.
Kayser-Fleischer corneal rings or tremor.
Marked elevation of antithyroid antibodies in a patient with fluctuating encephalopathic psychosis.

name: Schizophrenia
category: Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorders
symptoms: A chronic, severe psychiatric disorder characterized by >= 2 Criterion A symptoms (delusions, hallucinations, disorganized speech, grossly disorganized or catatonic behavior, negative symptoms) persisting for >= 6 months with marked social or occupational dysfunction.

differentials.overlap: Chronic auditory hallucinations, grandiose/persecutory delusions, flat affect, social withdrawal, dementia.
differentials.physical_signs: Argyll Robertson pupils, dysarthria, sensory ataxia (positive Romberg test), loss of vibratory sense.
differentials.workup: Serum syphilis treponemal antibody testing (TP-PA/FTA-ABS); CSF-VDRL and cell count.

differentials.overlap: Chronic paranoid delusions, religious/mystical preoccupations, auditory hallucinations, hypergraphia, circumstantiality (Geschwind syndrome).
differentials.physical_signs: Stereotyped auras (rising epigastric sensation, olfactory hallucinations, deja vu), postictal confusion, automatisms.
differentials.workup: Prolonged Video-EEG with anterior temporal leads; 3T Brain MRI (epilepsy protocol evaluating hippocampal sclerosis/mesial temporal atrophy).

differentials.overlap: Insidious emergence of paranoid delusions, bizarre behavior, auditory hallucinations, progressive cognitive blunting.
differentials.physical_signs: Spasticity, hyperreflexia, ataxia, peripheral neuropathy (loss of deep tendon reflexes in legs alongside Babinski signs).
differentials.workup: Leukocyte Arylsulfatase A (ARSA) enzyme activity (< 10% normal); Brain MRI (symmetric periventricular white matter tigroid pattern); ARSA gene sequencing.

differentials.overlap: Schizophrenia develops in 25-30% of affected individuals; social withdrawal, paranoia, cognitive limitations.
differentials.physical_signs: Submucous cleft palate, velopharyngeal insufficiency (hypernasal speech), congenital heart defects (conotruncal), hypocalcemia, hooded eyelids, bulbous nasal tip.
differentials.workup: Chromosomal Microarray (CMA) or 22q11.2 targeted FISH; Serum calcium and PTH levels.

differentials.mimic: Severe Vitamin B12 Deficiency ('Megaloblastic Madness') (E53.8 / G32.0)
differentials.overlap: Paranoid delusions, auditory/visual hallucinations, apathy, severe cognitive decline.
differentials.physical_signs: Loss of vibratory sense and proprioception in lower extremities, sensory ataxia, atrophic glossitis (smooth beefy tongue), lemon-yellow skin.
differentials.workup: Serum Vitamin B12 (< 200 pg/mL); Serum Methylmalonic Acid (MMA > 400 nmol/L); Complete Blood Count.

red_flags: Hypernasal speech resonance, history of cleft palate, or congenital heart defect in a psychotic patient (22q11.2 deletion).
Episodic stereotyped auras (epigastric sensations, burnt-rubber smells) preceding hallucinations.
Subcortical motor signs (spasticity, ataxia, loss of vibratory sense) in early schizophrenia.
Late onset (>= 40 years old) without antecedent schizoid/schizotypal prodrome.

name: Schizoaffective Disorder
category: Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorders
symptoms: An uninterrupted period of illness during which there is a major mood episode (major depressive or manic) concurrent with Criterion A of schizophrenia, alongside delusions or hallucinations for >= 2 weeks in the *absence* of a major mood episode during the lifetime duration.

differentials.overlap: Grandiosity, manic excitement, rapid pressured speech, paranoia, auditory hallucinations.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting sinus tachycardia, fine hand tremor, goiter, lid lag, weight loss despite increased appetite, diaphoresis.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (< 0.01 mIU/L); Free T4 and Total T3 (elevated); TRAb/TSI antibodies.

differentials.overlap: Severe treatment-resistant psychotic depression, paranoia, emotional lability, insomnia.
differentials.physical_signs: Moon facies, buffalo hump, central adiposity, wide violaceous striae, proximal muscle weakness, easy bruising.
differentials.workup: 24-hour urinary free cortisol (> 3x ULN); 1 mg overnight Dexamethasone suppression test; Pituitary/adrenal imaging.

differentials.overlap: Affective lability, mood swings, hallucinations, paranoia, short-term memory impairment.
differentials.physical_signs: Faciobrachial dystonic seizures (brief unilateral grimacing/arm spasms), sleep architectural breakdown, hyperreflexia.
differentials.workup: Serum and CSF autoimmune encephalopathy antibody panel; Brain MRI (bilateral mesial temporal T2 hyperintensity).

differentials.overlap: Bipolar-like mood cycling, paranoid psychosis, hallucinations, progressive executive decline.
differentials.physical_signs: Vertical Supranuclear Gaze Palsy (inability to execute voluntary downward saccades), gelastic cataplexy, ataxia.
differentials.workup: Ophthalmologic examination assessing vertical saccades; Plasma oxysterols / cholestanetriol; NPC1/NPC2 sequencing.

red_flags: Vertical gaze palsy (patient cannot look down voluntarily).
Prominent cushingoid stigmata (violaceous striae, buffalo hump, proximal myopathy).
Frequent, brief unilateral facial and arm twitches (faciobrachial dystonic seizures).
Marked heat intolerance, resting tachycardia > 110 bpm, and fine hand tremor.

name: Substance/Medication-Induced Psychotic Disorder
category: Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorders
symptoms: Prominent delusions and/or hallucinations developing during or soon after substance intoxication or withdrawal or after exposure to a medication capable of producing psychotic symptoms.

differentials.overlap: Euphoria, mania, flight of ideas, followed by severe persecutory delusions, auditory hallucinations, confusion.
differentials.physical_signs: Facial flushing, hypertension, peripheral edema, hyperglycemia, temporally correlated with high-dose prednisone (> 40 mg/day).
differentials.workup: Medication audit and timeline analysis; Blood glucose check; Resolution upon corticosteroid dose reduction.

differentials.overlap: Visual/tactile hallucinations (picking at clothes), muttering speech, severe paranoia, agitated delirium.
differentials.physical_signs: 'Mad as a hatter, blind as a bat, red as a beet, hot as a hare, dry as a bone': dilated pupils, anhidrosis, urinary retention, tachycardia.
differentials.workup: Toxidrome recognition; Bladder ultrasound scan (retention > 500 mL); ECG (ruling out QRS widening from TCAs); Urine tox screen.

differentials.overlap: Acute psychotic agitation, bizarre delusions, visual hallucinations often mistaken for drug ingestion in teens/young adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Orofacial dyskinesias, autonomic lability, hypoventilation, negative routine urine toxicology.
differentials.workup: CSF and serum anti-GluN1 NMDA receptor antibody testing; Pelvic ultrasound (ovarian teratoma); Continuous EEG.

differentials.overlap: Severe auditory, visual, and tactile hallucinations (zoopsia), terror, disorientation.
differentials.physical_signs: Coarse resting/intention tremor, profuse diaphoresis, tachycardia (> 120 bpm), hypertension, hyperthermia, seizures.
differentials.workup: CIWA-Ar scoring; Blood alcohol concentration; BMP (hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia); Liver function tests.

red_flags: Severe autonomic hyperactivity (hyperthermia, tachycardia > 130 bpm, profuse diaphoresis, or total anhidrosis).
Urinary retention with palpable bladder globe.
Persistence of florid psychotic symptoms > 4 weeks after complete elimination of the suspected substance.
Negative comprehensive toxicology screen in a patient presumed to be under the influence.

name: Psychotic Disorder Due to Another Medical Condition
category: Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorders
symptoms: Prominent hallucinations or delusions directly caused by the physiological consequences of another medical condition, not occurring exclusively during the course of a delirium.

differentials.overlap: Delusions of grandeur, auditory/visual hallucinations, personality dissolution, dementia.
differentials.physical_signs: Argyll Robertson pupils, dysarthria, tabetic gait, hyperreflexia, facial tremor.
differentials.workup: Serum treponemal antibody test (TP-PA/FTA-ABS); Lumbar puncture with CSF-VDRL, cell count, and protein.

differentials.overlap: Acute-to-subacute florid psychosis, persecutory delusions, catatonic posturing, visual hallucinations.
differentials.physical_signs: Choreoathetoid movements, orofacial grimacing/chewing, autonomic instability (blood pressure swings, fever), hypoventilation.
differentials.workup: CSF anti-GluN1 NMDA receptor antibodies (sensitivity ~100%); Pelvic ultrasound/MRI; EEG.

differentials.overlap: Depressive psychosis, paranoid delusions, auditory hallucinations, apathy, cognitive slowing.
differentials.physical_signs: Musculoskeletal weakness, hyporeflexia, abdominal pain (pancreatitis/nephrolithiasis), severe constipation.
differentials.workup: Serum total and ionized calcium (elevated > 10.5 mg/dL); Intact Parathyroid Hormone (PTH, inappropriately elevated); 24-hour urine calcium.

differentials.overlap: Paranoid delusions, visual hallucinations, confusion, intense agitation.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe colicky abdominal pain without peritoneal signs, tachycardia, hypertension, motor peripheral neuropathy, port-wine urine.
differentials.workup: Spot urine porphobilinogen (PBG); Urinary delta-ALA; Erythrocyte PBG deaminase activity.

red_flags: Total serum calcium > 11.5 mg/dL with altered mental status and constipation.
Pupillary unresponsiveness to light with preserved accommodation (Argyll Robertson pupils).
Severe unremitting abdominal pain preceding psychotic breakdown.
Stereotyped orofacial and lingual dyskinesias in an antipsychotic-naive patient.

name: Catatonia Associated with Mental Disorder / Medical Condition
category: Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorders
icd10: F06.1 (Due to Medical Condition), F20.9 (Catatonia Specifier)
symptoms: A neuropsychiatric syndrome characterized by >= 3 of: stupor, catalepsy, waxy flexibility, mutism, negativism, posturing, mannerism, stereotypy, agitation, grimacing, echolalia, or echopraxia.

differentials.overlap: Catatonic stupor, mutism, immobility, posturing, prominent diaphoresis.
differentials.physical_signs: 'Lead-pipe' muscular rigidity (diffuse hypertonicity), severe hyperthermia (> 38.0-40.0 C / 100.4-104 F), autonomic storm (tachycardia, labile BP, sialorrhea).
differentials.workup: Serum Creatine Kinase (CK markedly elevated > 1,000-50,000 U/L); CBC (leukocytosis 10,000-40,000/uL); CMP (acute kidney injury, myoglobinuria).

differentials.overlap: Agitation, confusion, immobility, hyperthermia, autonomic lability.
differentials.physical_signs: Spontaneous or inducible clonus (markedly pronounced in lower extremities), ocular clonus, hyperreflexia, shivering, bilateral Babinski signs.
differentials.workup: Hunter Serotonin Toxicity Criteria evaluation; Comprehensive toxicology screening; Serum CK; Arterial blood gas.

differentials.overlap: Catatonic mutism, waxy flexibility, staring, echolalia, autonomic instability.
differentials.physical_signs: Orofacial dyskinesias, choreoathetosis, alternating between catatonic stupor and intense violent agitation.
differentials.workup: CSF and serum anti-NMDA receptor antibodies; Pelvic MRI/ultrasound (teratoma); Continuous video-EEG.

differentials.overlap: Stupor, mutism, staring spells, unresponsiveness, posturing.
differentials.physical_signs: Subtle rhythmic twitching of eyelids, facial muscles, or fingers; absence of lead-pipe rigidity.
differentials.workup: Urgent Continuous Video-EEG (demonstrating continuous epileptiform spike-and-wave or rhythmic discharges responsive to IV benzodiazepines).

red_flags: Hyperthermia (temperature > 38.0 C / 100.4 F) with lead-pipe rigidity and autonomic storm (NMS emergency).
Bilateral ankle clonus and ocular flutter following serotonergic medication changes.
Subtle rhythmic eyelid fluttering in an unresponsive patient (requires urgent EEG for NCSE).
Failure to respond to IV Lorazepam 1-2 mg diagnostic challenge (Bush-Francis protocol).

name: Schizotypal Personality Disorder
category: Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorders
symptoms: A pervasive pattern of social and interpersonal deficits marked by acute discomfort with close relationships, as well as cognitive or perceptual distortions and eccentricities of behavior (ideas of reference, odd beliefs/magical thinking, bodily illusions, suspiciousness, constricted affect).

differentials.overlap: Deeply idiosyncratic philosophical/religious preoccupations, hypergraphia, circumstantiality, interpersonal stickiness (viscosity).
differentials.physical_signs: Brief stereotypic auras (epigastric sensation, olfactory hallucinations, deja vu), postictal confusion.
differentials.workup: Prolonged Video-EEG with temporal electrodes; High-resolution Brain MRI (epilepsy protocol).

differentials.overlap: Social awkwardness, eccentric special interests, difficulty with peer relationships, odd communication.
differentials.physical_signs: Absence of paranoid ideation or magical thinking; presence of sensory hypersensitivities and motor mannerisms; early developmental onset.
differentials.workup: Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS-2); Standardized neuropsychological assessment.

differentials.overlap: Odd magical beliefs, illusions, ideas of reference, eccentric lifestyle, social detachment.
differentials.physical_signs: Injection track marks, chronic conjunctival injection, tremors, pupillary abnormalities.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive Urine Drug Screen; Substance use history audit.

red_flags: Brief paroxysmal olfactory or epigastric sensations preceding episodes of heightened magical thinking.
Prominent sensory aversions to sounds, textures, or clothing dating back to early childhood.
Abrupt onset in middle age without childhood or adolescent eccentric prodrome.

name: Other Specified & Unspecified Schizophrenia Spectrum
category: Schizophrenia Spectrum and Other Psychotic Disorders
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a schizophrenia spectrum disorder predominate (hallucinations, delusions, disorganized thought) but do not meet full criteria for any specific disorder, or information is inadequate to specify.

differentials.overlap: Early psychiatric symptoms: bizarre delusions, visual hallucinations, severe anxiety, depression, personality disintegration.
differentials.physical_signs: Rapidly progressive cognitive decline over weeks/months, pathognomonic startle myoclonus, cerebellar ataxia, akinetic mutism.
differentials.workup: CSF RT-QuIC (sensitivity > 90%, specificity ~100%); CSF 14-3-3 protein; Brain MRI (DWI cortical ribboning and basal ganglia hyperintensity); EEG (1 Hz periodic sharp waves).

differentials.overlap: Delusions, hallucinations, apathy, psychomotor slowing, cognitive deficits.
differentials.physical_signs: Oral candidiasis, generalized lymphadenopathy, cachexia, focal neurological deficits (hemiparesis, cranial neuropathies).
differentials.workup: HIV 4th generation antigen/antibody immunoassay; CD4+ count; Brain MRI (multiple ring-enhancing lesions in basal ganglia); Serum Toxoplasma IgG.

differentials.overlap: Subacute emergence of complex psychiatric symptoms, hallucinations, emotional lability, memory loss.
differentials.physical_signs: Ataxia, sensory neuronopathy, sleep disturbance, rapid progression, older age.
differentials.workup: Paraneoplastic antibody panel (Anti-Hu, Anti-Ma2, Anti-CRMP5); Whole-body CT / FDG-PET (screening for occult small cell lung cancer or testicular tumor).

red_flags: Startle myoclonus (violent generalized myoclonic jerking in response to loud claps or sudden touch).
Rapid dementia progressing over weeks to months in a patient presenting with new psychosis.
Multiple ring-enhancing cerebral lesions on neuroimaging in an immunosuppressed individual.
Older adult presenting with subacute first-break psychosis and sensory neuronopathy.

name: Bipolar I Disorder (Manic / Depressed / Mixed)
symptoms: Characterized by the occurrence of at least one manic episode (a distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood and abnormally and persistently increased activity or energy lasting >= 1 week, with >= 3 of: grandiosity, decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, racing thoughts, distractibility, goal-directed agitation, risky impulsive behavior).

differentials.overlap: Severe psychomotor agitation, insomnia (decreased need for sleep), pressured speech, emotional lability, irritability.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting sinus tachycardia (> 100 bpm), fine resting hand tremor, goiter, lid lag, exophthalmos, heat intolerance, weight loss despite ravenous appetite.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (suppressed < 0.01 mIU/L); Free T4 and Total/Free T3 (elevated); TSH Receptor Antibodies (TRAb/TSI).

differentials.overlap: Euphoria, flight of ideas, grandiosity, insomnia, followed by rapid switching into refractory psychotic depression.
differentials.physical_signs: Moon facies, buffalo hump, central obesity, wide purple abdominal striae (> 1 cm), proximal muscle weakness (difficulty rising from a chair without arms).
differentials.workup: 24-hour urinary free cortisol (> 3x ULN); 1 mg overnight Dexamethasone suppression test; Late-night salivary cortisol; Pituitary/adrenal MRI.

differentials.overlap: Euphoric grandiosity, hyperactivity, bizarre disinhibition, hypersexuality, severe insomnia in adolescents/young adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Orofacial dyskinesias, chorea, autonomic lability (tachycardia, hyperthermia), progressive speech breakdown/mutism.
differentials.workup: CSF and serum anti-GluN1 NMDA receptor antibodies; Lumbar puncture (pleocytosis); Pelvic ultrasound/MRI (teratoma); Video-EEG.

differentials.overlap: Sudden late-onset mania, grandiosity, reckless financial behavior, hypersexuality, disinhibition.
differentials.physical_signs: Left hemiparesis or facial weakness, left visual field deficit, anosognosia, absence of prior psychiatric history.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI); Carotid duplex; Echocardiogram.

differentials.overlap: Manic-like disinhibition, emotional volatility, explosive rage outbursts, impulsivity in adolescents/young adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Kayser-Fleischer rings on slit-lamp, wing-beating tremor, dysarthria, dystonia, hepatomegaly.
differentials.workup: Slit-lamp exam; Serum ceruloplasmin (< 20 mg/dL); 24-hour urine copper (> 100 mcg/24h); Liver enzymes.

red_flags: First-episode mania in an individual over 40 years old (strongly indicates cerebrovascular, neoplastic, or metabolic disease).
Resting sinus tachycardia > 110 bpm, fine hand tremor, and dramatic weight loss (demands urgent thyroid panel).
Cushingoid physical stigmata: wide violaceous striae, buffalo hump, proximal myopathy.
Subtle involuntary orofacial twitches or dyskinesias in an adolescent presenting with explosive mania.

name: Bipolar II Disorder
symptoms: Characterized by a clinical course of recurring mood episodes consisting of one or more Major Depressive Episodes and at least one Hypomanic Episode (lasting >= 4 consecutive days, clear change in functioning, but *without* psychotic features and *not* severe enough to cause marked impairment or hospitalization).

differentials.overlap: Subtle hypomanic surges of energy, insomnia, and irritability alternating with profound lethargic depression.
differentials.physical_signs: Atrial fibrillation or resting sinus tachycardia, weight loss, fine tremor, warm extremities, goiter.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (suppressed < 0.01 mIU/L); Free T4 and Free T3; 12-lead ECG.

differentials.overlap: Paroxysmal bursts of extreme psychomotor energy, impending doom, agitation, sweating, insomnia, mistaken for rapid mood cycling.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe paroxysmal hypertension (> 180-220 mmHg systolic), pounding headache, profuse diaphoresis, pallor during attacks.
differentials.workup: Plasma free metanephrines and normetanephrines; 24-hour urine fractionated metanephrines; Abdominal/pelvic CT/MRI.

differentials.overlap: Severe depressive withdrawal and hypersomnia alternating with periods of disinhibition, hyperphagia, and hypersexuality.
differentials.physical_signs: Periodic episodes lasting days to weeks with complete baseline functioning between episodes; slurred speech during attacks.
differentials.workup: Clinical evaluation; Overnight Polysomnography; Brain MRI; Functional neuroimaging.

differentials.overlap: Hypomanic grandiosity, hypersexuality, decreased sleep, explosive irritability, followed by severe depression on withdrawal.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe cystic acne (face and back), muscular hypertrophy, gynecomastia, testicular atrophy, premature balding.
differentials.workup: Serum total/free testosterone (supraphysiologic); Suppressed LH/FSH (< 0.5 mIU/mL); Severely low HDL cholesterol; Elevated hematocrit.

red_flags: Severe paroxysmal hypertension with episodic headache and diaphoresis.
Cystic acne, gynecomastia, testicular atrophy, and supraphysiologic muscle mass.
Recurrent episodes of sleeping 18-22 hours daily accompanied by compulsive eating and hypersexuality (Kleine-Levin).
Unexplained new-onset atrial fibrillation or persistent resting tachycardia.

name: Cyclothymic Disorder
symptoms: For at least 2 years (1 year in children/adolescents), there have been numerous periods with hypomanic symptoms that do not meet criteria for a hypomanic episode and numerous periods with depressive symptoms that do not meet criteria for a major depressive episode, present for at least half the time without remission > 2 months.

differentials.overlap: Rapid swings between hypomanic restlessness, anxiety, and insomnia followed by profound depressive fatigue and cold intolerance.
differentials.physical_signs: Enlarged, firm, or tender thyroid goiter; transient resting tachycardia alternating with bradycardia; fluctuating skin moisture/dryness.
differentials.workup: Serial Serum TSH, Free T4, Free T3 (demonstrating fluctuating thyrotoxic and hypothyroid phases); Anti-TPO and Anti-Thyroglobulin antibodies.

differentials.overlap: Frequent, brief affective lability, sudden mood shifts, irritability, impulsive behaviors.
differentials.physical_signs: Stereotyped auras (epigastric sensations, deja vu), brief staring, brief manual automatisms, absence of true prolonged mood episodes.
differentials.workup: Prolonged Ambulatory or Video-EEG monitoring; Brain MRI 3T with epilepsy protocol.

differentials.overlap: Intense emotional lability, reactive mood swings lasting hours, impulsivity, irritability.
differentials.physical_signs: Mood shifts are reactive to interpersonal stressors/rejection (unlike autonomous biological cycles); frantic fears of abandonment; recurrent self-harm.
differentials.workup: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-5 Personality Disorders (SCID-5-PD).

differentials.mimic: Intermittent Stimulant & Sedative Polysubstance Cycling (F15.10 / F13.10)
differentials.overlap: Alternating states of hyperactivity, euphoria, energy and crashed depressive hypersomnia.
differentials.physical_signs: Fluctuating pupil size (mydriasis on stimulants, miosis on sedatives/opioids), track marks, nasal septal erosion.
differentials.workup: Serial Comprehensive Urine Drug Screens; Substance use history audit.

red_flags: Fluctuating thyroid tender mass or rapid swings between tachycardia and bradycardia.
Stereotyped brief paroxysmal neurological symptoms (epigastric flutter, olfactory aura).
Nasal mucosal ulceration or septal perforation from intranasal stimulant abuse.

name: Substance/Medication-Induced Bipolar & Related Disorder
symptoms: A prominent and persistent disturbance in mood characterized by elevated, expansive, or irritable mood developing during or soon after substance intoxication or withdrawal or after exposure to a medication.

differentials.overlap: Severe grandiosity, euphoria, decreased sleep, rapid speech, flight of ideas, impulsive spending, restlessness.
differentials.physical_signs: Facial plethora, elevated BP, peripheral edema, hyperglycemia, temporally correlated with oral/IV corticosteroids (e.g. prednisone >= 40 mg/day).
differentials.workup: Medication audit; Blood glucose; Electrolytes; Response to corticosteroid taper or low-dose atypical antipsychotic.

differentials.overlap: Hypomania, compulsive hypersexuality, pathological gambling, nocturnal restlessness, compulsive tinkering (punding).
differentials.physical_signs: Underlying Parkinson's disease or restless legs syndrome; taking pramipexole, ropinirole, or carbidopa-levodopa.
differentials.workup: Medication review quantifying daily Levodopa Equivalent Daily Dose (LEDD); QUIP-RS scale; Resolution upon dopamine agonist dose reduction.

differentials.overlap: Emergence of full manic syndrome following initiation or dose escalation of SSRI, SNRI, or TCA.
differentials.physical_signs: Tremor, insomnia, motor restlessness, absence of prior spontaneous manic history.
differentials.workup: Pharmacotherapy timeline; Discontinuation of antidepressant; Assessment for underlying bipolar diathesis.

differentials.overlap: Grandiosity, explosive irritability, aggressive behavior, hypersexuality, decreased sleep.
differentials.physical_signs: Cystic acne, gynecomastia, testicular atrophy, profound muscular hypertrophy, elevated hematocrit.
differentials.workup: Serum testosterone (supraphysiologic); Suppressed LH/FSH (< 0.5 mIU/mL); Lipid panel.

red_flags: Emergence of mania within 1-2 weeks of high-dose corticosteroid therapy.
Development of compulsive gambling or hypersexuality in a Parkinson's patient on pramipexole.
Profound cystic acne, gynecomastia, and testicular atrophy in a manic bodybuilder.
Persistence of full manic syndrome > 4 weeks after complete elimination of causative medication (suggests unmasked primary Bipolar I).

name: Bipolar & Related Disorder Due to Another Medical Condition
symptoms: A prominent and persistent period of abnormally elevated, expansive, or irritable mood and abnormally increased activity or energy directly attributable to the physiological effects of another medical condition.

differentials.overlap: Severe psychomotor agitation, insomnia, grandiosity, flight of ideas, emotional lability.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting sinus tachycardia (> 100 bpm), fine hand tremor, exophthalmos, diffuse vascular goiter, weight loss.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (< 0.01 mIU/L); Free T4 and Total T3 (markedly elevated); Thyroid stimulating immunoglobulin (TSI).

differentials.overlap: Euphoria sclerotica (pathological cheerfulness/grandiosity despite severe disability), disinhibition, manic episodes.
differentials.physical_signs: Lhermitte sign (electric shock down spine on neck flexion), Uhthoff phenomenon, optic neuritis, internuclear ophthalmoplegia, hyperreflexia.
differentials.workup: Brain and Spinal Cord MRI with gadolinium (Dawson fingers, periventricular/corpus callosum demyelinating plaques); CSF oligoclonal bands.

differentials.overlap: Grandiose mania, megalomania, reckless spending, impulsive behavior, insomnia.
differentials.physical_signs: Argyll Robertson pupils (non-reactive to direct light with preserved accommodation), slurred speech, tremor, sensory ataxia.
differentials.workup: Serum treponemal antibodies (TP-PA/FTA-ABS); Lumbar puncture with CSF-VDRL, cell count, and protein.

differentials.overlap: Mania, grandiosity, hypersexuality, impulsivity, emotional disinhibition in older adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Foster Kennedy syndrome (optic atrophy + contralateral papilledema), focal motor deficits, morning headache.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with and without gadolinium; Fundoscopy.

red_flags: Argyll Robertson pupils (bilaterally small pupils that do not react to light).
Lhermitte electric sensation down the spine or heat-induced weakness (Uhthoff phenomenon).
First-episode mania in a patient over age 45 without personal or family history of bipolar disorder.
Resting tachycardia > 110 bpm, fine hand tremor, and goiter.

name: Other Specified Bipolar & Related Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a bipolar and related disorder predominate but do not meet the full criteria for any specific bipolar disorder (e.g., short-duration hypomanic episodes [2-3 days] and major depressive episodes; hypomanic episodes without prior major depressive episode; short-duration cyclothymia [< 24 months]).

differentials.overlap: Brief periods of hypomanic restlessness, irritability, insomnia, and mild anxiety.
differentials.physical_signs: Mild resting tachycardia, borderline fine tremor, normal physical exam.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (suppressed 0.01-0.4 mIU/L) with normal Free T4 and Free T3; Serial monitoring; Radioactive iodine uptake scan.

differentials.overlap: Brief nocturnal or daytime behavioral agitation, hypermotor activity, emotional excitement.
differentials.physical_signs: Brief stereotypic motor automatisms (< 30-60 seconds), abrupt onset/offset, normal baseline.
differentials.workup: Overnight Video-EEG monitoring; Brain MRI 3T.

differentials.mimic: Chronic Sleep Deprivation with Hypomanic Rebound (G47.9)
differentials.overlap: Transient state of disinhibition, pressured speech, and giddy euphoria after prolonged sleep loss.
differentials.physical_signs: Ptosis, microsleeps, cognitive slowing under objective testing despite subjective feeling of high energy.
differentials.workup: Sleep diary / Actigraphy; Epworth Sleepiness Scale.

red_flags: Stereotyped nocturnal motor thrashing or bicycling movements lasting < 60 seconds (epilepsy).
Suppressed TSH in a patient with recurrent brief bursts of unexplained agitation.
Complete resolution of hypomanic symptoms following one night of restorative sleep.

name: Unspecified Bipolar & Related Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a bipolar and related disorder predominate but there is insufficient information to make a specific diagnosis (e.g., emergency room evaluations where full history is unavailable).

differentials.overlap: Extreme agitation, grandiosity, pressured speech, hypervigilance, sleeplessness.
differentials.physical_signs: Mydriasis, diaphoresis, severe tachycardia, hypertension, bruxism, track marks.
differentials.workup: Urine Drug Screen (UDS); Serum CPK; 12-lead ECG; Vital signs monitoring.

differentials.overlap: Agitation, disorganized behavior, emotional lability, insomnia, disorientation.
differentials.physical_signs: Fever or hypothermia, tachypnea, tachycardia, leukocytosis, altered mental status with fluctuating attention.
differentials.workup: CBC with diff; Blood cultures x 2; Urinalysis and urine culture; Chest X-ray; Serum lactate.

differentials.overlap: Severe acute psychiatric symptoms, agitation, bizarre affect, sleep disruption.
differentials.physical_signs: Fever prodrome, seizures, autonomic lability, rapid progression.
differentials.workup: Lumbar puncture (CSF pleocytosis, protein); Brain MRI; Autoimmune encephalopathy antibody panel.

red_flags: Fever, tachypnea, or elevated serum lactate in an agitated patient.
Dilated pupils, profuse diaphoresis, and severe hypertension (sympathomimetic toxidrome).
Fluctuating level of consciousness and inattention (demands delirium workup).

name: Rapid-Cycling Bipolar Specifier Manifestations
symptoms: Presence of at least four mood episodes (major depressive, manic, or hypomanic) in the previous 12 months, demarcated either by partial or full remission for at least 2 months or by a switch to an episode of the opposite polarity.

differentials.overlap: Strongly linked to rapid mood cycling, treatment-refractory depression, frequent affective switches.
differentials.physical_signs: Delayed reflex relaxation (Woltman sign), cold intolerance, weight gain, constipation, dry coarse skin.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (elevated > 4.5 mIU/L; often optimized to < 2.5 in rapid cyclers); Free T4 (subnormal); Anti-TPO antibodies.

differentials.overlap: Paradoxical rapid cycling, cycle acceleration, mixed states induced by chronic antidepressant monotherapy.
differentials.physical_signs: Irritability, agitated insomnia, absence of sustained euthymia while taking SSRIs, SNRIs, or TCAs.
differentials.workup: Medication audit; Stepwise discontinuation/taper of offending antidepressant; Mood stabilizer optimization.

differentials.mimic: Complex Partial Seizure Disorder / Temporal Lobe Epilepsy (G40.209)
differentials.overlap: Frequent, rapid mood swings, episodic rage, sudden affective shifts lasting hours to days.
differentials.physical_signs: Stereotyped auras, automatisms, postictal confusion, lack of classic multi-day sustained mood polarity.
differentials.workup: Prolonged Video-EEG with temporal leads; Brain MRI with thin coronal temporal cuts.

differentials.overlap: Weekly swings between hypomanic euphoria/hyperactivity and vegetative, suicidal depression.
differentials.physical_signs: Track marks, pupillary dilation, nasal mucosa erosion, weight fluctuations.
differentials.workup: Serial random Urine Drug Screens; Substance history verification.

red_flags: Elevated TSH or high anti-TPO titers in a patient experiencing rapid cycling (thyroid optimization often stabilizes cycles).
Acceleration of mood cycles following the addition of an antidepressant.
Brief paroxysmal affective outbursts lasting minutes with postictal tiredness.
Weekly swings coinciding with weekend stimulant binges and weekday crashes.

name: Disruptive Mood Dysregulation Disorder
symptoms: Severe recurrent temper outbursts manifested verbally and/or behaviorally that are grossly out of proportion in intensity or duration to the situation or provocation, occurring >= 3 times per week, with persistently irritable or angry mood between outbursts in children aged 6 to 18.

differentials.overlap: Extreme irritability, explosive emotional outbursts, daytime aggression, low frustration tolerance.
differentials.physical_signs: Tonsillar/adenoidal hypertrophy, mouth breathing, loud nightly snoring with witnessed apneas, morning headaches, nocturnal enuresis.
differentials.workup: Pediatric Overnight Polysomnography (AHI >= 1 event/hr); ENT surgical evaluation.

differentials.overlap: Sudden dramatic emotional lability, explosive rage outbursts, personality regression.
differentials.physical_signs: Overnight onset, accompanying motor/vocal tics, handwriting deterioration, choreiform movements, recent streptococcal infection.
differentials.workup: Throat culture / rapid strep; Anti-streptolysin O (ASO) and Anti-DNase B titers; Pediatric autoimmune workup.

differentials.overlap: Chronic irritability, violent outbursts, impulsivity, poor behavioral self-regulation.
differentials.physical_signs: Microcytic anemia, pallor, intermittent abdominal pain, Burton line on gums, pica history.
differentials.workup: Whole blood lead level (BLL >= 3.5 mcg/dL); Peripheral smear (basophilic stippling); Long bone X-rays.

differentials.overlap: Explosive behavioral dysregulation, emotional volatility, academic decline in older children.
differentials.physical_signs: Kayser-Fleischer rings on slit-lamp, subtle tremor, dysarthria, hepatomegaly.
differentials.workup: Slit-lamp exam; Serum ceruloplasmin (< 20 mg/dL); 24-hour urine copper (> 40-100 mcg/24h).

red_flags: Severe tonsillar hypertrophy, loud snoring, and witnessed apneas during sleep.
Explosive, overnight onset of emotional volatility accompanied by tics or obsessive rituals.
Living in older housing with verified elevated blood lead level.
Tremor, dysarthria, or golden-brown corneal rings (Wilson's disease).

name: Major Depressive Disorder (Single Episode)
symptoms: Presence of a single major depressive episode lasting >= 2 weeks characterized by depressed mood or loss of interest/pleasure (anhedonia), along with >= 4 of: significant weight/appetite change, insomnia/hypersomnia, psychomotor agitation/retardation, fatigue/energy loss, feelings of worthlessness/excessive guilt, diminished concentration, or recurrent suicidal ideation.

differentials.overlap: Profound fatigue, psychomotor slowing, anhedonia, hypersomnia, weight gain, cognitive slowing ('pseudodementia').
differentials.physical_signs: Delayed relaxation of deep tendon reflexes (Woltman sign), periorbital puffiness, coarse dry skin, cold intolerance, bradycardia, constipation.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (elevated > 4.5 mIU/L; often > 10 mIU/L in overt disease); Free T4 (subnormal < 0.8 ng/dL); Anti-TPO antibodies.

differentials.overlap: Refractory major depression, apathy, cognitive slowing, fatigue, irritability, paranoia.
differentials.physical_signs: Loss of vibration/proprioception in toes, sensory ataxia (positive Romberg), hyperreflexia/Babinski, atrophic glossitis (beefy tongue), lemon-yellow pallor.
differentials.workup: Serum Vitamin B12 (< 200 pg/mL); Serum Methylmalonic Acid (MMA > 400 nmol/L); Homocysteine; CBC (macrocytosis, MCV > 100 fL).

differentials.overlap: Severe apathy, chronic fatigue, anhedonia, weight loss, anorexia, generalized weakness.
differentials.physical_signs: Cutaneous hyperpigmentation (palmar creases, buccal mucosa, scars), orthostatic hypotension (> 20 mmHg drop), salt craving, vitiligo.
differentials.workup: Morning serum cortisol (8:00 AM < 3 mcg/dL); Cosyntropin (ACTH) stimulation test (peak cortisol < 18 mcg/dL); Plasma ACTH (> 100 pg/mL); BMP (hyponatremia + hyperkalemia).

differentials.overlap: Sudden onset of severe major depression, profound anhedonia, sense of impending doom in a patient > 50 with no psychiatric history.
differentials.physical_signs: Unexplained rapid weight loss, anorexia, dull epigastric pain radiating to back relieved by leaning forward, Courvoisier sign (painless palpable gallbladder with jaundice).
differentials.workup: Abdominal multiphase contrast CT (pancreatic protocol); Serum CA 19-9 tumor marker (> 37 U/mL); Endoscopic ultrasound (EUS).

differentials.overlap: Severe fatigue, psychomotor slowing, apathy, depression, cognitive impairment, poor concentration.
differentials.physical_signs: Conjunctival pallor, koilonychia (spoon nails), angular cheilitis, atrophic glossitis, restless legs syndrome, pica (ice craving / pagophagia).
differentials.workup: Serum Ferritin (< 30 ng/mL; < 15 diagnostic); Serum Iron and TIBC (saturation < 15%); CBC (microcytic hypochromic anemia, MCV < 80 fL).

red_flags: Delayed deep tendon reflex relaxation (Woltman sign) and cold intolerance.
Cutaneous hyperpigmentation of palmar creases and buccal mucosa with orthostatic hypotension (Addison's).
Sudden severe depression with unexplained weight loss in a patient > 50 years old (occult malignancy).
Loss of vibratory sensation in toes with gait unsteadiness (subacute combined degeneration / B12 deficiency).

name: Major Depressive Disorder (Recurrent Episode)
symptoms: Presence of two or more Major Depressive Episodes separated by an interval of at least 2 consecutive months in which criteria are not met for a major depressive episode.

differentials.overlap: Recurrent major depressive episodes (preceding neurological signs in 20-40%), severe fatigue, emotional lability.
differentials.physical_signs: Lhermitte sign (electric shock down spine on neck flexion), Uhthoff phenomenon (symptom worsening in heat/hot shower), optic neuritis, hyperreflexia, Babinski sign.
differentials.workup: Brain and Spinal Cord MRI with gadolinium (periventricular Dawson fingers, spinal cord plaques); Lumbar puncture (CSF oligoclonal bands >= 2, elevated IgG index).

differentials.overlap: Recurrent depressive episodes, cognitive 'brain fog', profound chronic fatigue.
differentials.physical_signs: Malar rash, photosensitivity, non-erosive arthritis, oral ulcers, serositis, Raynaud phenomenon.
differentials.workup: Antinuclear Antibodies (ANA > 1:160); Anti-dsDNA; Anti-Smith; Serum complement (C3/C4 low in flares); Urinalysis (proteinuria).

differentials.overlap: Recurrent depressive states, cognitive deficits, chronic disabling fatigue, migratory musculoskeletal pain.
differentials.physical_signs: History of erythema migrans rash, peripheral facial palsy (Bannwarth syndrome, often bilateral), large joint arthritis (knee swelling).
differentials.workup: Two-Tier Serologic Testing: Serum EIA/ELISA followed by Western Blot IgG (>= 5 bands); CSF-to-serum Borrelia antibody index (> 1.3).

differentials.overlap: Apathy, lethargy, psychomotor retardation, vivid nightmares, erectile dysfunction.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting sinus bradycardia (HR < 50-60 bpm), blunted heart rate response to exercise, cool extremities.
differentials.workup: Medication audit correlating beta-blocker dosing (especially lipophilic agents: propranolol, metoprolol); Resting ECG; Trial of hydrophilic agent (atenolol).

differentials.overlap: Severe depressive apathy, psychomotor retardation, vegetative fatigue, cognitive 'brain fog', anhedonia ('psychiatric overtones').
differentials.physical_signs: Proximal muscle weakness, hypertension, band keratopathy, recurrent nephrolithiasis ('stones'), diffuse osteopenia/bone pain ('bones'), abdominal discomfort/constipation ('abdominal groans').
differentials.workup: Serum Total and Ionized Calcium (elevated > 10.5 mg/dL); Intact Parathyroid Hormone (PTH) (inappropriately normal or markedly elevated); 24-hour urinary calcium; Neck ultrasound and Technetium-99m Sestamibi SPECT scan.

red_flags: Transient neurological deficits (visual blurring, numbness, electric shocks down spine) occurring months apart.
Inflammatory joint pain, malar rash, or photosensitivity.
Severe resting bradycardia (HR < 50 bpm) in a depressed patient on cardiac medications.
Recurrent major depression refractory to >= 3 antidepressant trials (demands full medical rule-out).

name: Persistent Depressive Disorder (Dysthymia)
symptoms: Depressed mood for most of the day, for more days than not, for at least 2 years (1 year in children/adolescents), accompanied by >= 2 of: poor appetite/overeating, insomnia/hypersomnia, low energy/fatigue, low self-esteem, poor concentration, feelings of hopelessness, without remission > 2 months.

differentials.overlap: Chronic low-grade fatigue, mild depressive mood, sluggish cognition, mild weight gain, constipation.
differentials.physical_signs: Subtle delayed relaxation of reflexes, mild thyroid enlargement / goiter, dry skin.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (elevated 4.5-10.0 mIU/L) with normal Free T4 (0.8-1.8 ng/dL); Anti-TPO antibodies (predicts progression to overt hypothyroidism).

differentials.overlap: Chronic unrefreshing sleep, daytime fatigue, cognitive slowing, executive dysfunction, low motivation.
differentials.physical_signs: Elevated BMI, neck circumference (> 17 inches men, > 16 inches women), crowded oropharynx (Mallampati III/IV), loud habitual snoring, retrognathia.
differentials.workup: STOP-Bang Questionnaire (score >= 3); In-lab or Home Sleep Apnea Testing (HSAT) demonstrating AHI >= 5 events/hr with symptoms.

differentials.overlap: Profound chronic fatigue, apathy, depressive mood, 'brain fog', myalgias, lasting years.
differentials.physical_signs: Often asymptomatic; hepatomegaly, palmar erythema, spider angiomas in advanced disease.
differentials.workup: HCV Antibody screening; Quantitative HCV RNA PCR (viral load); Liver enzymes (AST/ALT, often fluctuating).

differentials.overlap: Chronic non-restorative sleep, low mood, chronic fatigue, cognitive impairment ('fibro fog').
differentials.physical_signs: Widespread multisite tenderness on standardized pressure palpation, absence of joint synovitis.
differentials.workup: ACR Diagnostic Criteria (Widespread Pain Index and Symptom Severity Scale); Rule-out labs (normal ESR, CRP, TSH, CK).

red_flags: Neck circumference > 17 inches with loud nightly snoring and daytime somnolence.
Subclinical elevation of TSH > 5.0 mIU/L with positive anti-TPO antibodies.
History of past intravenous drug use or blood transfusions prior to 1992 (demands HCV screening).
Widespread musculoskeletal tender points without inflammatory joint swelling.

name: Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder (PMDD)
symptoms: In the majority of menstrual cycles, clinicians should identify at least 5 symptoms present in the final week before menses onset, improve within a few days after onset, and become minimal or absent in the week postmenses: marked affective lability, irritability/anger, depressed mood/hopelessness, marked anxiety/tension, lethargy, appetite change, sleep disturbance, physical symptoms (breast tenderness, bloating, joint pain).

differentials.overlap: Severe cyclical premenstrual irritability, fatigue, depression, somatic distress.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe dysmenorrhea (debilitating menstrual cramps), deep dyspareunia, dyschezia (pain with bowel movements), localized pelvic tenderness, nodularity along uterosacral ligaments.
differentials.workup: Pelvic examination; Transvaginal Ultrasound (evaluating endometriomas / 'chocolate cysts'); Diagnostic laparoscopy (definitive gold standard).

differentials.overlap: Cyclical worsening of severe fatigue, depressive mood, weight gain, fluid retention, cold intolerance in the luteal phase.
differentials.physical_signs: Delayed reflex relaxation, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, goiter.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH and Free T4; Thyroid antibody panel; Prospective daily symptom tracking across 2 menstrual cycles.

differentials.overlap: Severe mood lability, depression, anxiety, body image distress.
differentials.physical_signs: Oligomenorrhea/amenorrhea, hirsutism (Ferriman-Gallwey score >= 8), severe inflammatory cystic acne, androgenic alopecia, acanthosis nigricans, central obesity.
differentials.workup: Rotterdam Criteria; Serum total and free testosterone; DHEA-S; LH/FSH ratio (> 2:1); Fasting glucose/insulin; Pelvic ultrasound ('string of pearls' ovarian morphology).

differentials.mimic: Premenstrual Exacerbation (PME) of Major Depression / Bipolar (F32.9 / F31.9)
differentials.overlap: Marked worsening of depression and irritability in the late luteal phase.
differentials.physical_signs: Symptoms do *not* completely remit in the follicular week following menses (unlike true PMDD which shows total follicular euthymia).
differentials.workup: Prospective Daily Record of Severity of Problems (DRSP) tracked across 2 consecutive menstrual cycles.

red_flags: Persistent depressive symptoms during the post-menses follicular phase (indicates PME of underlying mood disorder, not pure PMDD).
Severe pelvic pain, dyspareunia, or pain with defecation (demands endometriosis evaluation).
Marked hirsutism, severe cystic acne, and irregular menstrual cycles (indicates PCOS).
