name: Substance/Medication-Induced Depressive Disorder
symptoms: A prominent and persistent disturbance in mood characterized by depressed mood or markedly diminished interest or pleasure in all activities, developing during or soon after substance intoxication or withdrawal or after exposure to a medication.

differentials.overlap: Severe major depression, profound anhedonia, fatigue, psychomotor retardation, high suicide risk in 30-50% of patients.
differentials.physical_signs: Flu-like symptoms (chills, myalgias, fever), weight loss, alopecia, temporal link to interferon therapy for HCV or melanoma.
differentials.workup: Medication review; Complete Blood Count (cytopenias); TSH (ruling out interferon-induced thyroiditis); Pre-treatment PHQ-9 tracking.

differentials.overlap: Profound fatigue, lack of motivation, blunted affect, anhedonia, nightmares, sexual dysfunction.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting sinus bradycardia (HR < 50 bpm), cool extremities, orthostasis.
differentials.workup: Medication audit; Resting 12-lead ECG; Trial of hydrophilic beta-blocker or calcium channel blocker.

differentials.overlap: Emergence of depressed mood, tearfulness, social withdrawal, suicidal ideation within weeks of starting isotretinoin.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe mucosal dryness (cheilitis in 100%), xerophthalmia, epistaxis, resolving acne.
differentials.workup: Medication timeline; Liver function tests; Fasting lipid panel; Immediate discontinuation if severe depression/suicidality develops.

differentials.overlap: Profound dysphoria, intense anhedonia, hypersomnia, hyperphagia, vivid unpleasant dreams, severe suicidal ideation.
differentials.physical_signs: Bradycardia, psychomotor retardation, pupillary constriction (relative to intoxicated state), absence of fever.
differentials.workup: Urine Drug Screen (confirming recent stimulant exposure); Vital signs monitoring; Suicide safety protocol.

red_flags: Severe new-onset depression and suicidality within 2-8 weeks of starting oral isotretinoin or interferon.
Resting sinus bradycardia < 50 bpm in a patient taking lipophilic beta-blockers.
Profound suicidal crash following acute cessation of cocaine or methamphetamine binges.
Persistence of major depressive episode > 4 weeks after complete medication/substance cessation.

name: Depressive Disorder Due to Another Medical Condition
icd10: F06.31 (With Depressive Features), F06.32 (With Major Depressive-Like Episode)
symptoms: A prominent and persistent period of depressed mood or markedly diminished interest or pleasure directly attributable to the physiological consequences of another medical condition.

differentials.overlap: Profound psychomotor slowing, anhedonia, lethargy, hypersomnia, weight gain, cognitive impairment.
differentials.physical_signs: Delayed relaxation phase of deep tendon reflexes, periorbital puffiness, coarse dry skin, cold intolerance, bradycardia.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (> 4.5 mIU/L); Free T4 (< 0.8 ng/dL); Anti-TPO antibodies.

differentials.mimic: Post-Stroke Depression (Left Frontal / Basal Ganglia Stroke) (I69.30)
differentials.overlap: Major depressive syndrome, apathy, emotional incontinence / pseudobulbar affect, psychomotor retardation.
differentials.physical_signs: Right hemiparesis, facial asymmetry, dysarthria, hyperreflexia, extensor plantar response.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging (demonstrating left anterior cortical or basal ganglia infarction); Carotid ultrasound; Echocardiogram.

differentials.overlap: Lethargy, apathy, depressive psychosis, cognitive slowing, severe generalized fatigue.
differentials.physical_signs: Hypotonia, hyporeflexia, abdominal pain (nephrolithiasis, peptic ulcer, pancreatitis), severe constipation.
differentials.workup: Total serum calcium (> 10.5 mg/dL) and ionized calcium; Intact PTH (inappropriately elevated); 24-hour urine calcium.

differentials.overlap: Major depression, apathy, anhedonia, psychomotor slowing preceding motor symptoms by years.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting asymmetric 'pill-rolling' tremor, cogwheel rigidity, bradykinesia, hypomimia (masked facies), loss of arm swing on walking, anosmia, REM sleep behavior disorder.
differentials.workup: Clinical neurological examination (UPDRS); Dopamine Transporter (DaT) SPECT scan (reduced striatal uptake); Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Severe treatment-refractory depression, profound anhedonia, anorexia, sense of doom.
differentials.physical_signs: Rapid unintentional weight loss, epigastric/back pain, Courvoisier sign, Trousseau syndrome (migratory thrombophlebitis).
differentials.workup: Abdominal CT (pancreatic protocol); Chest CT; Serum CA 19-9; CEA.

red_flags: Hypercalcemia (serum calcium > 10.5 mg/dL) with lethargy and constipation.
Asymmetric resting tremor, masked facial expression, or loss of arm swing in a depressed patient.
Depression emerging within weeks following acute stroke or focal neurological deficit.
Rapid unintentional weight loss > 10% of body weight in an older patient with new depression.

name: Other Specified Depressive Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a depressive disorder predominate but do not meet full criteria for any specific depressive disorder (e.g., recurrent brief depression [2-13 days once a month for >= 12 months]; short-duration depressive episode [4-13 days]; depressive episode with insufficient symptoms).

differentials.overlap: Recurrent brief bouts of depressive lethargy, cold intolerance, fatigue.
differentials.physical_signs: Mild thyroid fullness, fluctuating energy, normal baseline physical exam.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH; Free T4; Anti-Thyroperoxidase (anti-TPO) and Anti-Thyroglobulin antibodies.

differentials.overlap: Paroxysmal brief depressive episodes lasting hours to a few days, irritability, explosive dysphoria.
differentials.physical_signs: Stereotyped auras, automatisms, brief unresponsiveness, postictal sleepiness.
differentials.workup: Prolonged Ambulatory or Video-EEG monitoring; Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Recurrent fatigue, depressive feelings, difficulty concentrating, irritability.
differentials.physical_signs: Mild mucosal pallor, normal reflex exam.
differentials.workup: Serum Vitamin B12 (200-350 pg/mL borderline range); Serum Methylmalonic Acid (MMA); RBC Folate.

red_flags: Brief dysphoric episodes lasting hours to 2 days accompanied by paroxysmal sensory auras (epilepsy).
High anti-TPO antibody titers with borderline elevated TSH.
Macrocytosis (MCV > 100 fL) on routine CBC in a patient with recurrent brief depression.

name: Unspecified Depressive Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a depressive disorder predominate but there is insufficient information to make a specific diagnosis (e.g., in emergency room settings).

differentials.overlap: Depression, lethargy, psychomotor blunting, headache, fatigue, confusion, nausea.
differentials.physical_signs: Retinal hemorrhages, confusion, multiple family members or cohabitants with similar 'flu-like' or depressive symptoms in winter.
differentials.workup: Venous or arterial carboxyhemoglobin (COHb > 3-5% non-smoker, > 10% smoker); 12-lead ECG; Brain MRI.

differentials.mimic: Occult Sepsis / Urinary Tract Infection in Elderly (A41.9 / N39.0)
differentials.overlap: Apathy, withdrawal, refusal to eat, somnolence, pseudo-depressive presentation.
differentials.physical_signs: Low-grade fever or hypothermia, tachypnea, tachycardia, costovertebral angle tenderness, suprapubic tenderness, delirium.
differentials.workup: Urinalysis and urine culture; CBC with diff (leukocytosis or leukopenia with left shift); Blood cultures; Serum lactate.

differentials.overlap: Lethargy, psychomotor slowing, apathy, headache, cognitive dulling.
differentials.physical_signs: Gait unsteadiness, hyporeflexia, nausea, confusion; absence of peripheral edema in SIADH.
differentials.workup: Basic Metabolic Panel (serum sodium < 130 mEq/L; severe < 120); Serum osmolality; Urine osmolality.

red_flags: Multiple family members or pets exhibiting sudden lethargy and headache in winter (CO poisoning).
Serum sodium < 125 mEq/L with progressive lethargy and confusion.
Elderly patient presenting with sudden refusal to eat and apathy (check urinalysis and sepsis markers).

name: Prolonged Grief Disorder
symptoms: The death of a person close to the bereaved occurred at least 12 months ago (6 months in children/adolescents), characterized by persistent and pervasive grief response: intense yearning/longing for the deceased and/or preoccupation with thoughts/memories of the deceased, accompanied by >= 3 of: identity disruption, disbelief about the death, avoidance of reminders, intense emotional pain, difficulty reintegrating into life, emotional numbness, feeling that life is meaningless, or intense loneliness.

differentials.overlap: Intense acute emotional anguish, severe chest pressure, dyspnea, fatigue following the death of a loved one.
differentials.physical_signs: Acute chest pain, dyspnea, hypotension, diaphoresis, apical systolic murmur, signs of pulmonary edema.
differentials.workup: 12-lead ECG (ST elevations or T-wave inversions mimicking acute anterior myocardial infarction); Serum troponin (elevated); Transthoracic Echocardiogram (pathognomonic transient apical ballooning of left ventricle); Coronary angiography (absence of obstructive CAD).

differentials.overlap: Severe persistent post-loss lethargy, apathy, inability to mobilize energy, weight loss or gain.
differentials.physical_signs: Orthostatic hypotension, delayed reflexes, extreme fatigue.
differentials.workup: Morning serum cortisol; Serum TSH and Free T4; Basic Metabolic Panel.

differentials.mimic: Major Depressive Disorder Triggered by Bereavement (F32.9)
differentials.overlap: Depressed mood, insomnia, weight loss, suicidal thoughts.
differentials.physical_signs: Feelings of worthlessness, global self-loathing, pervasive anhedonia not limited to memories of deceased; PGD grief focuses specifically on the loss and yearning.
differentials.workup: Structured Clinical Interview; Inventory of Complicated Grief (ICG score > 25).

red_flags: Acute chest pain, shortness of breath, or diaphoresis triggered by acute grief (demands immediate ECG and troponin for Takotsubo cardiomyopathy).
Severe active suicidal intent to join the deceased in death.
Profound physical wasting, malnutrition, or refusal of all fluids and food.

name: Separation Anxiety Disorder
symptoms: Developmentally inappropriate and excessive fear or anxiety concerning separation from major attachment figures, manifested by persistent distress upon anticipating or experiencing separation, persistent worry about harm befalling attachment figures, reluctance/refusal to leave home, school, or sleep away.

differentials.overlap: Explosive, overnight onset of incapacitating separation anxiety (clinging, refusal to let parent out of sight), panic.
differentials.physical_signs: Concurrent sudden-onset motor/vocal tics, severe OCD (contamination fears), choreiform movements, emotional lability, post-streptococcal infection.
differentials.workup: Throat culture / rapid strep; Anti-streptolysin O (ASO) and Anti-DNase B titers; Comprehensive pediatric autoimmune panel.

differentials.mimic: Severe Pediatric Vestibular Dysfunction / Benign Paroxysmal Vertigo of Childhood (H81.10)
differentials.overlap: Intense terror of being left alone, refusal to walk without holding parent's hand, clinging.
differentials.physical_signs: Paroxysmal ataxia, unsteadiness, nystagmus, paleness, child clings to attachment figure due to true uncompensated physical vertigo.
differentials.workup: Videonystagmography (VNG); Vestibular Evoked Myogenic Potentials (VEMP); ENT evaluation.

differentials.mimic: Childhood Absence Epilepsy with Paroxysmal Fear (G40.A09)
differentials.overlap: Sudden freezing, panic, running to mother during brief episodes.
differentials.physical_signs: Brief blank staring spells (5-10 sec) with eyelid fluttering, provoked by hyperventilation; absence of true psychosocial separation triggers.
differentials.workup: Routine EEG with hyperventilation.

red_flags: Overnight emergence of extreme separation clinging in a previously independent child (suspect PANDAS/PANS).
Physical unsteadiness, stumbling, or nystagmus accompanying the child's refusal to walk away from parent (vestibular).
Stereotyped staring episodes or eyelid fluttering.

name: Selective Mutism
symptoms: Consistent failure to speak in specific social situations in which there is an expectation for speaking (e.g., at school) despite speaking in other situations, lasting at least 1 month (not limited to first month of school), interfering with educational or social achievement.

differentials.overlap: Failure to speak in group classrooms, social withdrawal, apparent refusal to respond to teachers.
differentials.physical_signs: Intact spoken communication in quiet home environment with parents; marked deterioration in acoustic processing in noisy school rooms.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive Audiometric Evaluation; Acoustic tympanometry.

differentials.mimic: Subtle Childhood Apraxia of Speech / Expressive Dyspraxia (R48.2)
differentials.overlap: Reluctance to speak in public, extreme self-consciousness, speaking only to trusted parents.
differentials.physical_signs: Speech sound sequencing errors, oral motor groping, vowel distortions on testing; child avoids speaking due to fear of motor breakdown.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive Speech-Language Motor Evaluation.

differentials.overlap: Lack of verbal communication in social settings, social awkwardness.
differentials.physical_signs: Mutism is *not* limited to specific social situations; presence of restricted/repetitive behaviors, sensory sensitivities, impaired nonverbal communication.
differentials.workup: ADOS-2; Developmental history.

red_flags: Mutism occurring across ALL settings including home and parents (suggests severe trauma, conversion mutism, or neurogenic speech arrest).
Motor speech groping or structural palate/tongue anomalies.
Complete absence of formal audiometry prior to psychological labeling.

name: Specific Phobia
symptoms: Marked fear or anxiety about a specific object or situation (e.g., flying, heights, animals, receiving an injection, seeing blood), almost always provoking immediate fear or anxiety, actively avoided or endured with intense distress, out of proportion to actual danger, lasting >= 6 months.

differentials.overlap: Fainting, nausea, dizziness, diaphoresis upon sight of blood, needles, or medical procedures.
differentials.physical_signs: Biphasic autonomic response: brief initial tachycardia followed by profound reflex bradycardia and hypotension; true loss of consciousness with pallor.
differentials.workup: 12-lead ECG; Tilt Table Testing; Orthostatic vital signs (distinguishing psychological anxiety panic [sympathetic surge] from vasovagal syncope [parasympathetic bradycardic collapse]).

differentials.overlap: Intense avoidance of heights, bridges, supermarkets, escalators, and open moving visual environments.
differentials.physical_signs: Subjective chronic non-spinning dizziness, swaying sensations exacerbated by upright posture and complex visual environments; absence of true motor phobia.
differentials.workup: Videonystagmography (VNG); Dynamic Visual Acuity; Neuro-otology evaluation.

differentials.overlap: Extreme phobic dread of open spaces, crossing streets, or sudden sounds, panic attacks.
differentials.physical_signs: Board-like axial muscle stiffness (thoracolumbar), painful muscle spasms triggered by sudden tactile or acoustic stimuli, abnormal hyperlordosis.
differentials.workup: Serum and CSF Anti-GAD65 antibodies (> 10,000 IU/mL); Surface EMG (continuous motor unit activity at rest).

red_flags: Profound bradycardia and true syncope upon blood exposure (vasovagal reflex mechanism).
Axial lumbar muscle board-like stiffness with stimulus-triggered spasms (demands anti-GAD65 antibody test for Stiff Person Syndrome).
Chronic sensation of rocking or floor instability in visual environments (demands vestibular evaluation for PPPD).

name: Social Anxiety Disorder (Social Phobia)
symptoms: Marked fear or anxiety about one or more social situations in which the individual is exposed to possible scrutiny by others (social interactions, being observed, performing in front of others), fearing negative evaluation (humiliation, embarrassment, rejection), lasting >= 6 months.

differentials.overlap: Tremulousness, intense anxiety, sweating, facial flushing, heart pounding during social encounters.
differentials.physical_signs: Fine resting hand tremor present *even in private solitary situations*, resting tachycardia > 90-100 bpm, warm moist palms, goiter.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (< 0.01-0.4 mIU/L); Free T4 and Free T3.

differentials.overlap: Severe social embarrassment, avoidance of eating, drinking, or writing in public due to hand shaking.
differentials.physical_signs: Bilateral postural and kinetic tremor of hands (demonstrated on Archimedes spiral drawing, drinking from cup); head 'yes-yes' or 'no-no' tremor; temporary relief with small alcohol intake.
differentials.workup: Neurological examination; Archimedes spiral drawing; Thyroid function tests; Brain MRI (ruling out secondary tremor).

differentials.overlap: Extreme anxiety in social settings, panic-like avoidance of public presentations.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe drenching facial and palmar sweating occurring spontaneously in response to mild thermal or emotional stimuli; primary autonomic dysregulation.
differentials.workup: Starch-iodine sweat test; Rule out pheochromocytoma, carcinoid syndrome, and hyperthyroidism.

differentials.overlap: Heart pounding, lightheadedness, autonomic distress during social performance.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting sinus heart rate persistently > 100 bpm, or rapid acceleration > 130 bpm with minimal emotional or postural stress.
differentials.workup: 24-hour ambulatory Holter monitor; 12-lead ECG; Echocardiogram.

red_flags: Hand tremor persists at rest in private when totally calm and unobserved (essential tremor or hyperthyroidism).
Resting sinus heart rate > 100 bpm throughout a 24-hour Holter recording.
Tremor substantially dampens within 15 minutes of consuming a small dose of alcohol (classic for essential tremor).

name: Panic Disorder
symptoms: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks (an abrupt surge of intense fear or intense discomfort that reaches a peak within minutes), with >= 4 of: palpitations/accelerated HR, sweating, trembling, shortness of breath, feelings of choking, chest pain/discomfort, nausea, dizziness/lightheadedness, chills/heat sensations, paresthesias, derealization/depersonalization, fear of losing control, fear of dying, followed by >= 1 month of persistent worry about additional attacks or maladaptive change in behavior.

differentials.overlap: Paroxysmal catastrophic panic attacks, intense terror, pounding palpitations, diaphoresis, tremulousness.
differentials.physical_signs: Paroxysmal severe hypertension (BP > 180-220/110 mmHg during episode), severe throbbing headache, pallor (not flushing) during attack.
differentials.workup: Plasma free metanephrines and normetanephrines (drawn supine after 30 min rest; > 3-4x ULN diagnostic); 24-hour urine fractionated metanephrines; Abdominal CT/MRI with contrast.

differentials.overlap: Sudden racing heartbeat, severe chest tightness, lightheadedness, acute panic, impending doom.
differentials.physical_signs: Abrupt onset and abrupt termination ('light-switch' phenomenon), heart rate 150-220 bpm, regular rhythm, terminated by vagal maneuvers (Valsalva, cold water face immersion).
differentials.workup: 12-lead ECG; 14-day ambulatory continuous ECG patch; Electrophysiology (EP) study.

differentials.overlap: Surges of panic, tremulousness, palpitations, dizziness, chest discomfort.
differentials.physical_signs: Sustained increase in heart rate of >= 30 bpm (or >= 40 bpm in adolescents) within 10 minutes of standing without orthostatic hypotension; dependent acrocyanosis.
differentials.workup: 10-minute active standing test or Head-Up Tilt Table Test (HUTT); Echocardiogram.

differentials.overlap: Paroxysmal sudden surge of terror, rising epigastric sensation, dread, depersonalization.
differentials.physical_signs: Attack lasts only 30-90 seconds (true panic attacks peak at 10 minutes and last 20-30 min), accompanied by olfactory/gustatory hallucination, lip-smacking, postictal confusion.
differentials.workup: Video-EEG monitoring; High-resolution 3T Brain MRI (hippocampal sclerosis).

differentials.overlap: Acute episodes of anxiety, diaphoresis, palpitations, tremors, confusion, hunger.
differentials.physical_signs: Whipple triad: symptoms of hypoglycemia, verified plasma glucose < 55 mg/dL during episode, prompt relief upon glucose ingestion.
differentials.workup: 72-hour supervised inpatient fast; Serum glucose, insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin; Endoscopic ultrasound.

differentials.overlap: Sudden onset of severe anxiety, apprehension, breathlessness, chest discomfort, tachycardia.
differentials.physical_signs: Tachypnea, resting tachycardia, hypoxemia (low SpO2 on pulse oximetry), unilateral calf swelling/tenderness (DVT), pleuritic chest pain.
differentials.workup: D-dimer; CT Pulmonary Angiography (CTPA); Venous duplex ultrasound of lower extremities; Arterial blood gas.

differentials.mimic: Celiac Disease & Gluten Neuroenteropathy / Ataxia (K90.0 / G11.1)
differentials.overlap: Paroxysmal panic-like autonomic rushes, tremors, somatic palpitations, chronic systemic irritability, fatigue, brain fog.
differentials.physical_signs: Dermatitis herpetiformis (intensely pruritic blistering rash over elbows/knees), aphthous stomatitis, refractory iron-deficiency anemia, mild sensory/gait ataxia on tandem stance.
differentials.workup: Serum Tissue Transglutaminase IgA (tTG-IgA) paired with Total Serum IgA; Anti-Deamidated Gliadin Peptide (DGP) IgG; Upper endoscopy with multi-site duodenal mucosal biopsies; HLA-DQ2/DQ8 genotype.

red_flags: Severe paroxysmal hypertension (> 180 mmHg) with throbbing headache and pallor (pheochromocytoma).
Heart rate abruptly jumps to > 150-200 bpm and abruptly stops within seconds (PSVT).
Attacks last < 90 seconds and feature rising epigastric sensations or metallic taste (temporal lobe epilepsy).
Attacks occur exclusively upon standing from a seated or supine position (POTS).
Unexplained hypoxemia (SpO2 < 94%) accompanying acute breathlessness and panic (pulmonary embolism).

name: Agoraphobia
symptoms: Marked fear or anxiety about >= 2 of: using public transportation, being in open spaces, being in enclosed places, standing in line or being in a crowd, being outside of the home alone, fearing that escape might be difficult or help unavailable in the event of panic-like or incapacitating symptoms, actively avoided or endured with distress, lasting >= 6 months.

differentials.overlap: Severe fear and avoidance of open crowded spaces, supermarkets, malls, transit hubs.
differentials.physical_signs: Oscillopsia (visual blurring of the environment while walking), positive Romberg sign, head impulse test abnormal bilaterally, absence of classic panic cognitions.
differentials.workup: Video-Head Impulse Test (vHIT); Rotary Chair testing; Vestibular rehabilitation evaluation.

differentials.mimic: Severe Inflammatory Bowel Disease / Fecal Incontinence (K50.9 / K51.9 / R15.9)
differentials.overlap: Refusal to leave the house, avoidance of public transportation and crowds due to fear of incapacitation.
differentials.physical_signs: Urgent fecal incontinence, nocturnal bowel movements, hematochezia, abdominal cramping, weight loss.
differentials.workup: Fecal Calprotectin (> 150-250 mcg/g); Colonoscopy with ileal biopsies; Pelvic floor manometry.

differentials.overlap: Severe fear of crossing open streets, agoraphobia-like immobility in public plazas.
differentials.physical_signs: Thoracolumbar spinal stiffness, hyperlordosis, severe painful muscle spasms triggered by unexpected sounds or visual motion.
differentials.workup: Serum and CSF Anti-GAD65 antibodies; Surface EMG.

red_flags: Oscillopsia (horizon bouncing or blurring when walking, forcing avoidance of open streets).
Fecal urgency, nocturnal diarrhea, or rectal bleeding driving home confinement.
Board-like abdominal or paraspinal muscle rigidity triggered by crossing streets.

name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (GAD)
symptoms: Excessive anxiety and worry (apprehensive expectation) occurring more days than not for at least 6 months about a number of events or activities, difficult to control, accompanied by >= 3 of: restlessness/on edge, easily fatigued, difficulty concentrating, irritability, muscle tension, sleep disturbance.

differentials.overlap: Chronic restlessness, nervousness, irritability, muscle tension, insomnia, fatigue.
differentials.physical_signs: Fine hand tremor, resting tachycardia (> 90-100 bpm), heat intolerance, warm moist skin, hyperreflexia, weight loss.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (suppressed < 0.01-0.4 mIU/L); Free T4 and Free T3; Thyroid ultrasound.

differentials.overlap: Chronic generalized anxiety, irritability, restlessness, fatigue, cognitive 'brain fog'.
differentials.physical_signs: Musculoskeletal aching, proximal weakness, constipation, nephrolithiasis history.
differentials.workup: Total serum calcium (> 10.5 mg/dL) and ionized calcium; Intact PTH (elevated or inappropriately high-normal); 24-hr urine calcium.

differentials.overlap: Restlessness, nervousness, excitement, insomnia, diuresis, muscle twitching, psychomotor agitation.
differentials.physical_signs: Tachycardia, cardiac arrhythmia, flushed face, gastrointestinal disturbance; daily intake typically > 250-500 mg.
differentials.workup: Dietary caffeine audit (coffee, energy drinks, pre-workout supplements, OTC analgesics); Gradual taper.

differentials.overlap: Chronic apprehension, air hunger, restlessness, sleep disruption, chronic fatigue.
differentials.physical_signs: Accentuated pulmonic component of second heart sound (loud P2), elevated JVP, exertional dyspnea, SpO2 < 95%.
differentials.workup: Transthoracic Echocardiogram (elevated pulmonary artery systolic pressure); Pulse oximetry; V/Q scan.

differentials.overlap: Intense inner motor restlessness, inability to sit still, severe anxiety, insomnia.
differentials.physical_signs: Continuous pacing, rocking, crossing/uncrossing legs; inner urge to move limbs; taking dopamine receptor antagonists.
differentials.workup: Medication audit; Barnes Akathisia Rating Scale (BARS); Trial of propranolol or dose reduction.

red_flags: Suppressed TSH with fine resting hand tremor and heat intolerance.
Elevated serum calcium (> 10.5 mg/dL) in a patient with chronic refractory anxiety.
Resting tachycardia > 100 bpm or loud pulmonic heart sound (P2) with exertional dyspnea.
Motor pacing and inability to sit still emerging after starting an antipsychotic or prokinetic antiemetic.

name: Substance/Medication-Induced Anxiety Disorder
symptoms: Prominent anxiety or panic attacks predominating in the clinical picture, developing during or soon after substance intoxication or withdrawal or after exposure to a medication.

differentials.overlap: Severe generalized anxiety, panic attacks, emotional lability, insomnia, irritability.
differentials.physical_signs: Mydriasis, resting tachycardia (> 110 bpm), hypertension, diaphoresis, bruxism, motor agitation.
differentials.workup: Urine Drug Screen; 12-lead ECG; Medication dosing audit; Blood pressure log.

differentials.overlap: Severe rebound anxiety, panic attacks, agoraphobia, autonomic arousal, tremor.
differentials.physical_signs: Coarse hand tremor, diaphoresis, resting tachycardia, systolic hypertension, hyperreflexia, visual/tactile hypersensitivity, seizure risk.
differentials.workup: Clinical Institute Withdrawal Assessment (CIWA-Ar or CIWA-B); UDS; Vital signs monitoring.

differentials.overlap: Tremulousness, palpitations, acute panic, chest tightness, restlessness.
differentials.physical_signs: Fine peripheral tremor, sinus tachycardia, history of frequent rescue inhaler overuse.
differentials.workup: Prescription audit; Serum theophylline level (if applicable); Pulmonary function optimization.

differentials.overlap: Sudden explosion of severe panic attacks, depersonalization, insomnia, paranoia, agitation.
differentials.physical_signs: Tremors, myoclonus, hyperreflexia, Achilles tendon tenderness or tendon rupture.
differentials.workup: Medication timeline confirming fluoroquinolone initiation within 24-72 hours; Drug discontinuation.

red_flags: Severe coarse hand tremor, diaphoresis, and hypertension following abrupt cessation of sedatives/alcohol (seizure risk).
Sudden severe panic, tendon pain, and insomnia within 3 days of starting a fluoroquinolone antibiotic.
Resting heart rate > 120 bpm and severe pupillary dilation in a patient taking stimulants.

name: Anxiety Disorder Due to Another Medical Condition
symptoms: Prominent anxiety or panic attacks directly attributable to the physiological consequences of another medical condition.

differentials.overlap: Severe chronic anxiety, panic attacks, tremor, irritability, sleep disruption.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting sinus tachycardia, fine hand tremor, exophthalmos, diffuse goiter, heat intolerance, weight loss.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (< 0.01 mIU/L); Free T4 and Free T3 (elevated); TSI antibodies.

differentials.overlap: Paroxysmal panic attacks, impending doom, palpitations, sweating, tremulousness.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe paroxysmal hypertension (> 180-220 mmHg), pounding headache, marked pallor during episodes.
differentials.workup: Plasma free metanephrines/normetanephrines; 24-hour urine metanephrines; Abdominal MRI/CT.

differentials.overlap: Acute severe panic, feeling of suffocation, apprehension, restlessness.
differentials.physical_signs: Tachypnea, resting tachycardia, SpO2 < 94%, pleuritic chest pain, calf swelling.
differentials.workup: D-dimer; CT Pulmonary Angiogram (CTPA); Venous duplex ultrasound.

differentials.overlap: Chronic severe generalized anxiety, irritability, cognitive fatigue.
differentials.physical_signs: Hypotonia, hyporeflexia, bone aches, abdominal pain, severe constipation.
differentials.workup: Total serum calcium (> 10.5 mg/dL); Ionized calcium; Intact PTH.

red_flags: Severe episodic hypertension with pounding headache and pallor (pheochromocytoma).
Acute air hunger with resting tachycardia and hypoxemia (pulmonary embolism).
Persistent resting tachycardia > 100 bpm and fine hand tremor (hyperthyroidism).
Hypercalcemia on routine metabolic panel.

name: Other Specified Anxiety Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of an anxiety disorder predominate but do not meet full criteria for any specific anxiety disorder (e.g., generalized anxiety not occurring more days than not; limited-symptom panic attacks).

differentials.overlap: Atypical chest pains, palpitations, episodic lightheadedness, mild anxiety.
differentials.physical_signs: Midsystolic click followed by a late systolic murmur best heard at cardiac apex; lean asthenic build.
differentials.workup: Transthoracic Echocardiogram (demonstrating systolic displacement of mitral valve leaflets >= 2 mm above annular plane).

differentials.overlap: Episodic postprandial anxiety, shakiness, sweating, lightheadedness occurring 2-4 hours after high-carbohydrate meals.
differentials.physical_signs: Tremulousness, diaphoresis, tachycardia during episode; relieved promptly by eating.
differentials.workup: Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (extended 5-hour OGTT); Home blood glucose log during symptoms.

differentials.overlap: Episodic dizziness, motion sensitivity, spatial anxiety, nausea.
differentials.physical_signs: Normal interictal neurological exam; history of migraine headaches, photophobia, motion sickness.
differentials.workup: Videonystagmography; Neurological evaluation.

red_flags: Midsystolic click and late systolic murmur on cardiac auscultation.
Episodes occur reliably 2-4 hours after high-sugar meals and resolve immediately with food.
Paroxysmal motion sensitivity accompanied by visual aura or photophobia.

name: Unspecified Anxiety Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of an anxiety disorder predominate but there is insufficient information to make a specific diagnosis.

differentials.mimic: Acute Coronary Syndrome / Myocardial Ischemia (I21.9 / I20.0)
differentials.overlap: Severe acute anxiety, feeling of impending doom, diaphoresis, lightheadedness, nausea.
differentials.physical_signs: Substernal chest pressure radiating to left arm/jaw, diaphoresis, pallor, hypotension or hypertension.
differentials.workup: Urgent 12-lead ECG (ST elevations, depressions, T-wave inversions); Serial high-sensitivity cardiac troponin.

differentials.overlap: Violent panic, agitation, tachycardia, palpitations, paranoia.
differentials.physical_signs: Mydriasis, severe hypertension, hyperthermia, diaphoresis.
differentials.workup: Urine Drug Screen; Comprehensive metabolic panel; Serum CPK.

differentials.overlap: Sudden onset of severe anxiety, acute dyspnea, chest discomfort.
differentials.physical_signs: Unilateral decreased breath sounds, hyperresonance to percussion on affected side, tachypnea; tall thin young male or COPD patient.
differentials.workup: Urgent Upright Chest X-ray; Thoracic bedside ultrasound (loss of lung sliding).

red_flags: Substernal crushing chest pain radiating to jaw or left arm with diaphoresis (ACS).
Sudden sharp pleuritic chest pain with unilateral absent breath sounds (pneumothorax).
Severe hypertension with hyperthermia and mydriasis in an agitated patient.

name: Nocturnal Panic Attack Specifier
symptoms: Waking from non-REM sleep (typically stages 2 or 3) in a state of sudden terror, intense autonomic arousal, palpitations, diaphoresis, dyspnea, without apparent dream trigger, occurring in 40-70% of panic disorder patients.

differentials.overlap: Abrupt nocturnal awakenings with gasping, choking, pounding heart, diaphoresis, terror.
differentials.physical_signs: Witnessed nocturnal apneas, loud snoring, morning headache, elevated BMI, crowded oropharynx.
differentials.workup: Overnight Polysomnography (demonstrating severe AHI >= 30 events/hr with arterial oxygen desaturations terminating in autonomic awakenings).

differentials.overlap: Sudden, violent nighttime awakenings in a state of terror and agitation.
differentials.physical_signs: Bizarre hypermotor movements (bicycling, pelvic thrusting, flailing), stereotypic brief duration (< 30-60 seconds), occurring multiple times per night.
differentials.workup: Polysomnography with continuous synchronous 32-channel video-EEG; 3T Brain MRI.

differentials.mimic: Nocturnal Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD) with Laryngospasm (K21.9)
differentials.overlap: Waking abruptly in terror, feeling of strangulation/choking, coughing, chest tightness.
differentials.physical_signs: Acid/bitter taste in mouth, water brash, hoarseness, absence of primary fear cognitions prior to choking sensation.
differentials.workup: 24-hour ambulatory esophageal pH/impedance monitoring; Upper endoscopy (EGD).

differentials.overlap: Waking in panic with profuse cold sweating, palpitations, tremulousness, confusion.
differentials.physical_signs: Diaphoresis (drenched bedsheets), tachycardia, morning headache, taking insulin or sulfonylureas.
differentials.workup: Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) demonstrating nocturnal glucose drops < 55-70 mg/dL; Fasting insulin/C-peptide.

red_flags: Loud nightly snoring and witnessed breathing cessation preceding sudden awakenings.
Violent stereotypic motor thrashing or bicycling leg movements lasting < 60 seconds (epilepsy).
Awakening drenched in cold sweat with confusion in a diabetic patient on insulin.
Severe acid taste in mouth and acute stridor/laryngospasm upon waking.

name: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
symptoms: Presence of obsessions (recurrent, persistent, intrusive thoughts, urges, or images causing marked anxiety/distress) and/or compulsions (repetitive behaviors or mental acts driven to perform according to rigid rules to reduce anxiety or prevent a dreaded event), time-consuming (> 1 hour/day) or causing significant impairment.

differentials.overlap: Explosive, overnight onset of severe contamination obsessions, washing rituals, symmetry compulsions.
differentials.physical_signs: Choreiform piano-playing finger movements, sudden fine motor dysgraphia, vocal/motor tics, urinary urgency, emotional lability following Group A Strep.
differentials.workup: Rapid Strep test and throat culture; Anti-streptolysin O (ASO) and Anti-DNase B titers; Autoimmune workup.

differentials.overlap: Severe obsessive-compulsive rituals, intrusive thoughts, emotional volatility.
differentials.physical_signs: Continuous flowing involuntary choreic movements of face and limbs, milkmaid's grip, darting tongue, cardiac murmur (rheumatic fever carditis).
differentials.workup: Jones criteria evaluation; ASO/Anti-DNase B titers; Echocardiogram (mitral regurgitation).

differentials.overlap: Severe obsessions, rigid mental inflexibility, perseveration, irritability, preceding motor signs by years.
differentials.physical_signs: Motor impersistence (inability to sustain tongue protrusion), subtle chorea of fingers/toes, saccadic eye movement slowing, family history of autosomal dominant chorea/dementia.
differentials.workup: Targeted HTT gene genetic testing (CAG repeat expansion >= 36); Brain MRI (bilateral caudate head atrophy).

differentials.overlap: Stereotyped, compulsive rituals, clock-watching, counting, hoarding, ritualistic eating routines in middle-aged adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Profound social disinhibition, loss of empathy, hyperorality, primitive frontal release signs (grasp, snout reflexes), progressive executive decay.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (asymmetric frontal/anterior temporal atrophy); FDG-PET scan (frontal hypometabolism).

differentials.mimic: Autoimmune Basal Ganglia Encephalitis (Anti-Basal Ganglia Antibodies) (G04.81)
differentials.overlap: Subacute severe obsessive rituals, compulsive checking, cognitive slowing, anxiety.
differentials.physical_signs: Parkinsonian rigidity, tremors, sleep disturbance, autonomic dysfunction.
differentials.workup: Serum and CSF autoimmune encephalopathy antibody panel; Brain MRI with contrast; Video-EEG.

red_flags: Explosive, overnight onset of incapacitating contamination or checking compulsions in a child (PANDAS/PANS).
Involuntary choreiform jerking or darting tongue movements accompanying obsessive symptoms (Sydenham's or Huntington's).
New-onset compulsive hoarding or clock-watching rituals in a patient aged 50-65 with personality disinhibition (FTD).
Subtle extrapyramidal rigidity or resting tremor emerging alongside obsessions.

name: Body Dysmorphic Disorder
symptoms: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others, accompanied by repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, excessive grooming, skin picking, reassurance seeking) or mental acts (comparing appearance with others), causing significant distress.

differentials.overlap: Preoccupation with skin blemishes, constant facial picking, scarring.
differentials.physical_signs: Actual mild comedonal acne or folliculitis present, but picking behavior produces deep excoriations, ulcerations, and hyperpigmented scarring disproportionate to initial lesion.
differentials.workup: Dermatologic examination; Slit-lamp skin microscopy; Biopsy of atypical non-healing ulcers.

differentials.overlap: Intense distress and obsession regarding facial hair, body shape, weight, and acne.
differentials.physical_signs: True objective moderate-to-severe hirsutism (Ferriman-Gallwey score >= 8), inflammatory cystic acne, androgenic alopecia, acanthosis nigricans, irregular menses.
differentials.workup: Serum total and free testosterone; DHEA-S; Pelvic ultrasound; Fasting insulin.

differentials.overlap: Bizarre complaints about facial symmetry or distortion, prolonged mirror staring.
differentials.physical_signs: Inability to recognize familiar faces, visual agnosia, preserved non-facial object recognition, right fusiform gyrus lesion.
differentials.workup: Warrington Recognition Memory Test; High-resolution Brain MRI (fusiform / lingual gyrus pathology).

red_flags: Objective physical signs of virilization (clitoromegaly, severe hirsutism, cystic acne) in a patient preoccupied with masculine features (PCOS or adrenal tumor).
Multiple cosmetic surgical procedures with persistent dissatisfaction and escalating surgical demands.
Visual field defects or inability to recognize familiar family faces (fusiform gyrus lesion).

name: Hoarding Disorder
symptoms: Persistent difficulty discarding or parting with possessions, regardless of their actual value, due to a perceived need to save items and distress associated with discarding them, resulting in the accumulation of possessions that congest and clutter active living areas.

differentials.overlap: Compulsive acquisition and hoarding of useless objects, garbage, or food; total squalor.
differentials.physical_signs: Complete lack of insight, absence of distress when objects are touched by others, apathy, loss of empathy, hyperorality, primitive frontal reflexes (grasp/snout).
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (bilateral frontal and temporal atrophy); Neuropsychological testing (severe executive dysfunction with preserved memory early).

differentials.overlap: Severe hoarding, clutter, disorganization, inability to prioritize possessions.
differentials.physical_signs: History of traumatic brain injury or rupture of anterior communicating artery (ACoA) aneurysm; disinhibition, impaired decision making.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI / CT Angiography (orbitofrontal cortex, rectus gyrus, or ventromedial prefrontal damage).

differentials.overlap: Extreme self-neglect, domestic squalor, compulsive hoarding of rubbish (syllogomania), complete social alienation in the elderly.
differentials.physical_signs: Malnutrition, pressure ulcers, severe dehydration, flea/scabies infestation, lack of shame or awareness regarding squalor.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive Geriatric Assessment; Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA); Brain CT/MRI; Nutritional panel (B12, folate, albumin).

red_flags: Late-onset hoarding (> 55 years old) without antecedent collecting history (strongly indicates frontal lobe degeneration or dementia).
Severe domestic squalor accompanied by malnutrition and unconcern (Diogenes syndrome).
History of subarachnoid hemorrhage or head injury preceding hoarding behavior.

name: Trichotillomania (Hair-Pulling Disorder)
symptoms: Recurrent pulling out of one's hair, resulting in hair loss, along with repeated attempts to decrease or stop hair pulling, causing clinically significant distress or impairment.

differentials.overlap: Patchy hair loss, distress regarding appearance.
differentials.physical_signs: Completely smooth, completely hairless round/oval patches with *absence* of broken hairs; 'exclamation mark' hairs at margin of patch; positive hair pull test at periphery; nail pitting.
differentials.workup: Dermoscopy / Trichoscopy (yellow dots, black dots, exclamation mark hairs); Scalp punch biopsy (peribulbar lymphocytic 'swarm of bees' infiltrate).

differentials.overlap: Scalp hair loss, itching, scratching, broken hairs.
differentials.physical_signs: Scalp erythema, scaling, pruritus, cervical/occipital lymphadenopathy, 'black dot' hair breakage flush with scalp, kerion (boggy inflammatory mass).
differentials.workup: KOH direct microscopic examination of hair shafts; Wood's UV lamp (green fluorescence in Microsporum); Fungal culture.

differentials.mimic: Gastric Trichobezoar / Rapunzel Syndrome (T18.2XXA / F63.3 complication)
differentials.overlap: Hair pulling accompanied by trichophagia (swallowing hair), abdominal pain, nausea.
differentials.physical_signs: Epigastric mass, early satiety, severe halitosis, bowel obstruction, patchy alopecia.
differentials.workup: Abdominal CT with oral contrast; Upper endoscopy (EGD visualizing massive hairball extending into duodenum).

red_flags: Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, or palpable epigastric mass in a hair-puller (Rapunzel syndrome / trichobezoar emergency).
Cervical lymphadenopathy and scalp scaling/erythema (demands fungal culture for Tinea Capitis).
Completely bare, smooth patches with exclamation-mark hairs (Alopecia Areata).

name: Excoriation (Skin-Picking) Disorder
symptoms: Recurrent skin picking resulting in skin lesions, accompanied by repeated attempts to decrease or stop skin picking, causing clinically significant distress or impairment.

differentials.overlap: Severe compulsive picking, scratching, excoriations, sleep disruption.
differentials.physical_signs: Pathognomonic burrows in web spaces of fingers, flexor wrists, axillae, beltline, genitalia; intense nocturnal pruritus; family members itching.
differentials.workup: Skin scrapings in mineral oil under light microscopy demonstrating mites, eggs, or scybala (feces); Dermoscopy (delta-wing sign).

differentials.overlap: Compulsive picking at skin, creating deep ulcers, believing bugs/parasites are under skin.
differentials.physical_signs: Dilated pupils, tachycardia, hypertension, track marks, severe dental erosion ('meth mouth'), excoriations concentrated on accessible areas (arms, face).
differentials.workup: Urine Drug Screen for amphetamines/cocaine; Comprehensive tox screen.

differentials.overlap: Intensely pruritic lesions that patient picks and scratches into bleeding excoriations.
differentials.physical_signs: Symmetrically distributed grouped papulovesicles on extensor surfaces (elbows, knees, buttocks, scalp), burning itch.
differentials.workup: Direct immunofluorescence (DIF) of perilesional skin biopsy (granular IgA deposition in dermal papillae); Serum tTG-IgA.

differentials.overlap: Severe intractable whole-body scratching and excoriation.
differentials.physical_signs: Sallow complexion, uremic frost, jaundice, scleral icterus, xanthomas, excoriations sparing mid-back ('butterfly sign').
differentials.workup: Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (BUN/creatinine, total bilirubin, alkaline phosphatase); Serum bile acids.

red_flags: Severe nocturnal itching with burrows in finger webs (Scabies).
Formication ('bugs crawling under skin') with dilated pupils, tachycardia, and weight loss (stimulant toxicity).
Elevated BUN, creatinine, or bilirubin in a patient presenting with whole-body skin excoriation.

name: Substance/Medication-Induced OCRD
symptoms: Prominent obsessive-compulsive symptoms, body-focused repetitive behaviors, or skin picking developing during or soon after substance intoxication or withdrawal or after exposure to a medication.

differentials.overlap: Intense repetitive, purposeless, stereotyped handling, sorting, or dismantling of mechanical objects, compulsive checking.
differentials.physical_signs: Underlying Parkinson's disease; taking pramipexole, ropinirole, or carbidopa-levodopa; patient remains absorbed in repetitive activity for hours.
differentials.workup: Medication audit; QUIP-RS rating scale; Discontinuation or dose reduction of dopamine agonist.

differentials.mimic: Atypical Antipsychotic-Induced De Novo OCD (Clozapine, Olanzapine) (T43.595A)
differentials.overlap: New-onset or marked aggravation of severe obsessions and checking/washing rituals within weeks of starting second-generation antipsychotics.
differentials.physical_signs: Absence of prior OCD history; patient is on clozapine, olanzapine, or aripiprazole for schizophrenia or bipolar disorder.
differentials.workup: Medication timeline; Assessment of plasma clozapine level; Adjunctive low-dose aripiprazole or SSRI switch.

differentials.overlap: Compulsive skin picking, repetitive grooming, compulsive organizing, paranoia.
differentials.physical_signs: Mydriasis, tachycardia, hypertension, diaphoresis, weight loss.
differentials.workup: Urine Drug Screen; Vital signs monitoring.

red_flags: Emergence of severe obsessive-compulsive rituals following clozapine or olanzapine initiation.
Repetitive purposeless tinkering/punding in a Parkinson's patient on dopamine agonists.
Pupillary dilation, tachycardia, and skin picking linked to stimulant use.

name: OCRD Due to Another Medical Condition
symptoms: Prominent obsessive-compulsive symptoms or related behaviors directly attributable to the physiological consequences of another medical condition.

differentials.overlap: Sudden onset of severe contamination obsessions, checking rituals, emotional lability.
differentials.physical_signs: Chorea of face and limbs, milkmaid's grip, darting tongue, systolic heart murmur.
differentials.workup: ASO and Anti-DNase B titers; Throat culture; Echocardiogram.

differentials.overlap: Obsessive-compulsive symptoms, rigidity of thought, affective changes, behavioral deterioration.
differentials.physical_signs: Kayser-Fleischer rings on slit-lamp, tremor, dystonia, dysarthria, hepatomegaly.
differentials.workup: Slit-lamp exam; Serum ceruloplasmin (< 20 mg/dL); 24-hour urine copper (> 100 mcg/24h).

differentials.overlap: Abrupt emergence of compulsive checking, counting, symmetrical arranging, apathy in older adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Contralateral motor/sensory deficits, dystonic posturing, abulia, cognitive slowing.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) showing acute basal ganglia ischemia; Carotid ultrasound.

differentials.overlap: Obsessive rituals, stereotyped repetitive movements, agitation, psychosis.
differentials.physical_signs: Orofacial dyskinesias, autonomic lability, seizures, hypoventilation.
differentials.workup: CSF and serum anti-GluN1 NMDA receptor antibodies; Pelvic ultrasound.

red_flags: Abrupt onset of OCD following an acute focal neurological event (demands brain MRI for basal ganglia stroke).
Choreic movements or cardiac murmurs in a pediatric or adolescent OCD patient.
Kayser-Fleischer corneal rings, dysarthria, or tremor (Wilson's disease).

name: Other Specified OCRD (e.g., Olfactory Reference)
symptoms: Presentations characteristic of an OCRD that do not meet full criteria, including Olfactory Reference Disorder (false preoccupation that one emits a foul or offensive body odor not perceived by others, leading to repetitive washing, checking, and social avoidance).

differentials.overlap: Perception of foul, offensive, rotting, or burning odors, intense anxiety, panic.
differentials.physical_signs: Odors are episodic, paroxysmal, lasting 30-90 seconds (unlike continuous olfactory reference delusions); accompanied by epigastric rising sensation, lip-smacking, postictal confusion.
differentials.workup: Prolonged Video-EEG; 3T Brain MRI (uncus / mesial temporal lobe lesions).

differentials.overlap: Belief that one emits an intolerable foul odor, social isolation, excessive bathing.
differentials.physical_signs: True objective excretion of trimethylamine in sweat, urine, and breath causing rotting fish odor, exacerbated by menses or choline-rich food.
differentials.workup: Urinary measurement of trimethylamine (TMA) and trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) after choline challenge; FMO3 gene sequencing.

differentials.mimic: True Chronic Halitosis / Zenker's Diverticulum (R19.6 / K44.9)
differentials.overlap: Obsession with bad breath, excessive teeth brushing, mouthwash use, social avoidance.
differentials.physical_signs: Objective fetor ex ore, regurgitation of undigested food hours after eating, dysphagia, gurgling sound in neck.
differentials.workup: Barium swallow esophagram; Halimeter volatile sulfur compound testing; ENT exam.

red_flags: Brief paroxysmal episodes of smelling foul burning odors accompanied by lip smacking or confusion (uncinate fits / temporal lobe epilepsy).
Regurgitation of undigested food and gurgling neck mass (Zenker's diverticulum).
Confirmed objective fish-like odor on independent clinical examination (trimethylaminuria).

name: Body-Focused Repetitive Behavior Disorder
symptoms: Characterized by recurrent body-focused repetitive behaviors other than hair pulling and skin picking (e.g., severe nail biting [onychophagia], lip biting [morsicatio labiorum], cheek chewing), accompanied by repeated attempts to decrease or stop the behaviors.

differentials.overlap: Severe compulsive self-mutilating behaviors (severe biting of lips, tongue, and fingers), distress.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe tissue destruction of lips and fingertips; spastic cerebral palsy, choreoathetosis, dystonia, intellectual disability; orange uric acid crystals in diaper/urine.
differentials.workup: Serum uric acid (markedly elevated > 10-15 mg/dL); Hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase (HPRT1) enzyme assay (< 1.5% normal); HPRT1 gene sequencing.

differentials.overlap: Nail destruction, preoccupation with damaged nails, picking/biting nails.
differentials.physical_signs: Subungual hyperkeratosis, nail plate thickening, yellow-brown discoloration, onycholysis; lack of primary compulsive urge.
differentials.workup: Nail clipping with PAS (Periodic acid-Schiff) stain and fungal culture.

differentials.mimic: Congenital Insensitivity to Pain with Anhidrosis (CIPA) (G60.8)
differentials.overlap: Severe biting of tongue, lips, and fingers in early childhood.
differentials.physical_signs: Complete lack of pain and temperature sensation; recurrent unexplained high fevers due to anhidrosis; tongue and finger mutilation.
differentials.workup: NTRK1 gene sequencing; Quantitative sensory testing; Histopathology of sweat glands.

red_flags: Compulsive biting producing severe loss of lip or finger tissue in young boys (Lesch-Nyhan syndrome).
Total absence of pain withdrawal reflexes or lack of sweating with recurrent fevers (CIPA).
Orange 'sand' or gravel in the urine (uric acid nephrolithiasis).

name: Unspecified OCRD
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of an obsessive-compulsive and related disorder predominate but there is insufficient information to make a specific diagnosis.

differentials.overlap: Bizarre compulsive rituals, perseverative questions, agitation, insomnia.
differentials.physical_signs: Autonomic instability, focal seizures, rapid cognitive decay.
differentials.workup: CSF autoimmune encephalopathy panel; Brain MRI with gadolinium.

differentials.overlap: Compulsive pacing, repetitive vocalizations, confusion, restlessness.
differentials.physical_signs: Fever, headache, meningismus, altered sensorium.
differentials.workup: Lumbar puncture (CSF PCR for HSV, VZV, enterovirus); Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Compulsive repetitive grooming, pacing, skin manipulation.
differentials.physical_signs: Mydriasis, tachycardia, hypertension, diaphoresis.
differentials.workup: Urine Drug Screen; Comprehensive metabolic panel.

red_flags: Fever, headache, and neck stiffness preceding acute compulsive behaviors.
Pupillary dilation, tachycardia, and hypertension in an agitated repetitive pacing patient.
Rapid onset of cognitive disorientation over 24-48 hours.

name: Reactive Attachment Disorder
symptoms: A consistent pattern of inhibited, emotionally withdrawn behavior toward adult caregivers (child rarely or minimally seeks or responds to comfort when distressed), accompanied by persistent social/emotional disturbance (minimal social responsiveness, limited positive affect, unexplained episodes of irritability/sadness/fearfulness) in children who experienced extreme insufficient care/neglect.

differentials.overlap: Impaired social reciprocity, failure to seek comfort, limited emotional sharing.
differentials.physical_signs: Presence of restricted repetitive behaviors, motor stereotypies, adherence to nonfunctional routines, sensory sensitivities (which are absent in pure RAD); ASD persists across all caregiving environments.
differentials.workup: ADOS-2; Detailed caregiving and institutional neglect history.

differentials.overlap: Failure to respond to caregiver vocal comfort, apparent aloofness, lack of affective mirroring.
differentials.physical_signs: Normal visual engagement and comfort seeking when visual contact is maintained; lack of acoustic startle.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive Audiometric Evaluation (ABR/OAE).

differentials.mimic: Untreated Inborn Error of Metabolism (e.g., PKU, Urea Cycle) (E70.0 / E72.20)
differentials.overlap: Apathy, irritability, developmental withdrawal, poor eye contact.
differentials.physical_signs: Eczema, microcephaly, brisk reflexes, mousy odor, episodic vomiting.
differentials.workup: Plasma amino acids; Urine organic acids; Plasma ammonia.

red_flags: Presence of restricted motor stereotypies and sensory sensitivities (indicates ASD rather than RAD).
Lack of acoustic startle response on clinical testing.
Episodic lethargy or vomiting triggered by protein feeds (urea cycle defect).

name: Disinhibited Social Engagement Disorder
symptoms: A pattern of behavior in which a child actively approaches and interacts with unfamiliar adults and exhibits >= 2 of: reduced/absent reticence in approaching unfamiliar adults, overly familiar verbal/physical behavior, diminished/absent checking back with adult caregiver after venturing away, willingness to go off with an unfamiliar adult with minimal hesitation, following severe social neglect.

differentials.overlap: Extremely indiscriminate social friendliness, lack of stranger fear, loquacious expressive speech ('cocktail party personality').
differentials.physical_signs: 'Elfin' facies (broad forehead, short nose with broad tip, full cheeks, wide mouth with full lips), starry iris pattern, supravalvular aortic stenosis (ejection systolic murmur), infantile hypercalcemia.
differentials.workup: Chromosomal Microarray (CMA) or targeted FISH for 7q11.23 deletion (ELN gene); Echocardiogram; Serum calcium.

differentials.overlap: Impulsive social approach, blurting out comments, intruding into stranger spaces.
differentials.physical_signs: Child checks back with primary caregiver when anxious or injured; social behavior is driven by generalized motor impulsivity rather than attachment disinhibition.
differentials.workup: Vanderbilt ADHD Diagnostic Rating Scales; Caregiving attachment history.

differentials.overlap: Extreme social disinhibition, lack of boundary awareness, poor judgment regarding dangerous adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Smooth philtrum, thin upper lip, short palpebral fissures, microcephaly.
differentials.workup: 4-Digit Diagnostic Code assessment; Brain MRI.

red_flags: Elfin facial features, starry eyes, and a loud cardiac ejection murmur (pathognomonic for Williams syndrome).
Facial dysmorphic features of prenatal alcohol exposure (smooth philtrum, thin vermilion).
History of severe infantile hypercalcemia.

name: Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD)
symptoms: Exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence, followed by symptoms across 4 clusters lasting > 1 month: (1) Intrusion (flashbacks, nightmares, physiological reactivity), (2) Avoidance of trauma-related stimuli, (3) Negative alterations in cognitions and mood (amnesia, negative beliefs, detachment), (4) Alterations in arousal and reactivity (hypervigilance, exaggerated startle, insomnia, irritability).

differentials.mimic: Temporal Lobe Epilepsy (Ictal Flashbacks & Deja Vu) (G40.209)
differentials.overlap: Vivid recurrent panoramic memory reenactments ('experiential hallucinations'), intense fear, tachycardia.
differentials.physical_signs: Stereotyped rising epigastric aura, olfactory/gustatory sensations, automatisms, brief duration (< 60-90 sec), postictal confusion; episodes occur without environmental trauma cues.
differentials.workup: Prolonged Video-EEG monitoring with temporal leads; 3T Brain MRI (epilepsy protocol).

differentials.overlap: Paroxysmal hyperarousal, pounding tachycardia, profuse sweating, trembling, catastrophic dread.
differentials.physical_signs: Paroxysmal severe hypertension (> 180-220 mmHg), severe headache, pallor during episode, unprovoked by trauma memories.
differentials.workup: Plasma free metanephrines/normetanephrines; 24-hr urine fractionated metanephrines; Abdominal CT/MRI.

differentials.overlap: Severe irritability, insomnia, cognitive deficits, headache, emotional lability following physical trauma.
differentials.physical_signs: Photophobia, phonophobia, balance impairment, convergence insufficiency, history of physical head impact with loss of consciousness.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI evaluating microhemorrhages / diffuse axonal injury); Vestibular-ocular motor screening (VOMS).

differentials.overlap: Extreme hypervigilance, insomnia, fine tremor, palpitations, emotional lability.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting tachycardia (> 100 bpm), lid lag, fine tremor, warm moist skin, goiter, weight loss.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (< 0.01 mIU/L); Free T4 and Free T3; TSI antibodies.

red_flags: Flashbacks are stereotyped, last < 90 seconds, and feature rising epigastric auras or metallic taste (temporal lobe epilepsy).
Hypertension > 180 mmHg accompanied by pounding headache and pallor (pheochromocytoma).
Persistent photophobia, dizziness, and worsening of symptoms with cognitive exertion following a head strike (post-concussion syndrome).
Elevated resting heart rate > 100 bpm persisting during sleep.

name: Acute Stress Disorder
symptoms: Exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violation, resulting in >= 9 symptoms across intrusion, negative mood, dissociation, avoidance, and arousal clusters, lasting 3 days to 1 month immediately following trauma.

differentials.mimic: Acute Traumatic Brain Injury / Intracranial Hemorrhage (S06.9X9A / I62.9)
differentials.overlap: Confusion, amnesia for the traumatic event, emotional lability, headache, dizziness.
differentials.physical_signs: Focal neurological deficits, asymmetric pupils, progressive somnolence, vomiting, retroauricular ecchymosis (Battle sign), periorbital ecchymosis (raccoon eyes).
differentials.workup: Urgent Non-contrast Head CT (ruling out epidural, subdural, or subarachnoid hemorrhage and skull fracture); Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS).

differentials.overlap: Acute terror, feelings of dying, chest pressure, severe breathlessness following catastrophic stress.
differentials.physical_signs: Hypotension, diaphoresis, pulmonary crackles, apical systolic murmur.
differentials.workup: 12-lead ECG (ST elevation/T-wave inversion); Cardiac troponin (elevated); Transthoracic Echocardiogram (apical ballooning).

differentials.mimic: Acute Toxic Ingestion / Drug Facilitated Assault (T42.4X1A / T41.291A)
differentials.overlap: Profound anterograde amnesia, confusion, emotional distress following an assault.
differentials.physical_signs: Ataxia, slurred speech, hypothermia, respiratory depression, nystagmus.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive expanded urine and blood toxicology (including GHB, flunitrazepam, ketamine, scopolamine); Forensic medical examination.

red_flags: Unequal pupils, Battle sign, or deteriorating level of consciousness following trauma (urgent neurosurgical emergency).
Severe chest pain or acute pulmonary edema following extreme psychological stress (Takotsubo cardiomyopathy).
Unexplained amnesia with profound motor ataxia following a social gathering (drug-facilitated assault screening).

name: Adjustment Disorders
symptoms: Development of emotional or behavioral symptoms (depressed mood, anxiety, mixed anxiety/depression, disturbance of conduct) in response to an identifiable psychosocial stressor occurring within 3 months of stressor onset, out of proportion to stressor or causing significant impairment, resolving within 6 months of stressor termination.

differentials.overlap: Mild emotional distress, fatigue, anxiety, sleep disruption, low stress tolerance.
differentials.physical_signs: Subtle changes in heart rate, skin texture, or reflexes; symptoms persist long after external stressor is removed.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH and Free T4; Anti-TPO antibodies.

differentials.overlap: Fatigue, low mood, sleep disturbance, irritability, attributed erroneously to job or marital stress.
differentials.physical_signs: Painless lymphadenopathy, drenching night sweats, unexplained weight loss (> 10%), low-grade fevers (Pel-Ebstein fevers).
differentials.workup: Complete Blood Count; Peripheral blood smear; ESR / CRP; Chest/abdominal CT.

differentials.overlap: Malaise, fatigue, tearfulness, inability to cope with normal daily demands.
differentials.physical_signs: Exudative pharyngitis, posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, hepatomegaly.
differentials.workup: Heterophile antibody test (Monospot); EBV viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgM and IgG; CBC (atypical lymphocytosis > 10%).

red_flags: Drenching night sweats, persistent unexplained fevers, or painless firm lymphadenopathy (lymphoma / occult malignancy).
Posterior cervical lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly (EBV mononucleosis).
Persistence of symptoms > 6 months after the psychosocial stressor has fully resolved.

name: Other Specified Trauma- and Stressor-Related Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a trauma- and stressor-related disorder predominate but do not meet full criteria for any specific disorder (e.g., persistent complex bereavement disorder manifestations; cultural bereavement syndromes).

differentials.overlap: Severe chest tightness, fear, autonomic distress occurring during periods of severe stress.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe rest angina occurring characteristically between midnight and early morning, normal exercise tolerance.
differentials.workup: Ambulatory continuous ECG monitoring; Coronary angiography with provocative acetylcholine testing.

differentials.overlap: Severe exhaustion, emotional collapse, nausea, dizziness following acute stress.
differentials.physical_signs: Orthostatic hypotension, postural dizziness, mild salt cravings.
differentials.workup: Morning serum cortisol; Cosyntropin stimulation test; BMP.

differentials.mimic: Transient Global Amnesia (TGA) Triggered by Stress (G45.4)
differentials.overlap: Sudden dense anterograde amnesia, confusion, and repetitive questioning following acute emotional stress.
differentials.physical_signs: Patient repeatedly asks 'What am I doing here? What happened?'; preserved personal identity, resolves in < 24 hours.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with DWI (punctate diffusion restriction in CA1 field of hippocampus); EEG.

red_flags: Sudden dense amnesia with perseverative questioning lasting < 24 hours (TGA).
Severe rest chest pain with ST elevations occurring in the early morning hours (Prinzmetal angina).
Severe postural hypotension with salt cravings following emotional shock.

name: Unspecified Trauma- and Stressor-Related Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a trauma- and stressor-related disorder predominate but there is insufficient information to make a specific diagnosis.

differentials.overlap: Severe agitation, confusion, apprehension, tachycardia following motor vehicle accident or physical trauma.
differentials.physical_signs: Hypotension, tachycardia, cold clammy extremities, pallor, tachypnea, abdominal distension.
differentials.workup: FAST exam (Focused Assessment with Sonography for Trauma); Serial hemoglobin/hematocrit; Serum lactate.

differentials.overlap: Acute emotional distress, breathlessness, confusion, terror following an industrial accident or fire.
differentials.physical_signs: Wheezing, soot in nares/oropharynx, stridor, conjunctival suffusion, carbon monoxide poisoning.
differentials.workup: Carboxyhemoglobin (COHb); Arterial blood gas; Chest X-ray.

differentials.overlap: Intense unprovoked terror, panic, agitation, hallucinations following an animal bite weeks prior.
differentials.physical_signs: Paresthesias at bite site, pathognomonic hydrophobia (violent laryngeal spasms upon drinking water or air draft), hypersalivation, fever.
differentials.workup: Nuchal skin biopsy (rabies antigen DFA); Saliva rabies RT-PCR; CSF rabies antibodies.

red_flags: Tachycardia with declining blood pressure and cold extremities following trauma (internal bleeding).
Severe hydrophobia and violent laryngeal spasms triggered by attempts to drink water (rabies emergency).
Soot in the airway, stridor, or carboxyhemoglobin > 5% after fire exposure.

name: Complex PTSD / Developmental Trauma Manifestations
symptoms: Severe, persistent psychological trauma following exposure to prolonged, repeated interpersonal trauma from which escape was difficult or impossible (e.g., childhood abuse, chronic domestic violence), featuring core PTSD plus severe disturbances in: (1) Affect regulation (emotional volatility, explosive anger, dissociation), (2) Negative self-concept (feelings of worthlessness, shame, guilt), (3) Relational disturbances (inability to sustain intimate relationships).

differentials.overlap: Severe emotional dysregulation, chronic emptiness, interpersonal instability, recurrent self-harm.
differentials.physical_signs: BPD features frantic fears of abandonment, alternating idealization/devaluation (splitting), and identity disturbance; CPTSD centers on persistent negative self-worth, shame, and avoidance of relationships.
differentials.workup: Structured Clinical Interview (SCID-5-PD); International Trauma Interview (ITI for ICD-11 CPTSD).

differentials.overlap: Episodic affective outbursts, sudden rage, dissociative states, intense visceral sensations.
differentials.physical_signs: Stereotyped auras, postictal state, automatisms; lack of emotional recovery between seizures.
differentials.workup: Prolonged Video-EEG monitoring; High-resolution Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Widespread multisite somatic pain, chronic exhaustion, sleep fragmentation, cognitive fog, high trauma overlap.
differentials.physical_signs: Widespread standardized tender points, allodynia, absence of joint synovitis.
differentials.workup: ACR Fibromyalgia Diagnostic Criteria; Rule-out laboratory panel.

red_flags: Episodic stereotyped rising epigastric sensations or visual distortions preceding affective breakdowns.
Widespread multisite allodynia and hyperalgesia (central sensitization).
Severe persistent self-injurious behavior requiring immediate safety stabilization.

name: Dissociative Subtype of PTSD
symptoms: Meets all criteria for PTSD and in addition, in response to the stressor, the individual experiences persistent or recurrent symptoms of either: (1) Depersonalization (feeling detached from one's own body or mental processes, like an outside observer), or (2) Derealization (persistent or recurrent experiences of unreality of surroundings, world seems unreal, dreamlike, distant, or distorted).

differentials.overlap: Sudden intense depersonalization, derealization, out-of-body experiences, micropsia/macropsia (Alice in Wonderland syndrome).
differentials.physical_signs: Brief paroxysmal duration (< 60-120 seconds), automatisms (lip smacking, fumbling), postictal fatigue/confusion, absence of trauma memory trigger.
differentials.workup: Continuous Video-EEG with sphenoidal or temporal leads; 3T Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Floating sensations, disconnected from body, visual unreality, spatial disorientation.
differentials.physical_signs: Nystagmus, motion intolerance, headache, phonophobia, photophobia.
differentials.workup: Videonystagmography (VNG); Neuro-otology evaluation.

differentials.mimic: Dissociative Hallucinogen / Cannabinoid Toxicity (Ketamine, PCP, THC) (T41.291A / F16.10)
differentials.overlap: Profound feelings of unreality, detachment from body, dreamlike state, visual distortions.
differentials.physical_signs: Horizontal, vertical, or rotary nystagmus (classic for PCP/ketamine), analgesia, ataxia, hypertension.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive Urine Drug Screen (GC-MS testing for dissociatives); Vital signs monitoring.

red_flags: Vertical or rotary nystagmus (pathognomonic for dissociative NMDA antagonist toxicity like PCP/ketamine).
Episodes of depersonalization last < 2 minutes with lip smacking or confusion (focal seizures).
True visual spinning (vertigo) and nystagmus accompanying out-of-body sensations.

name: Dissociative Identity Disorder
symptoms: Disruption of identity characterized by two or more distinct personality states (which may be described in some cultures as an experience of possession), involving marked discontinuity in sense of self and sense of agency, accompanied by related alterations in affect, behavior, consciousness, memory, perception, cognition, and/or sensory-motor functioning, along with recurrent gaps in the recall of everyday events, important personal information, and/or traumatic events.

differentials.mimic: Complex Partial Seizures / Temporal Lobe Epilepsy (G40.209)
differentials.overlap: Amnestic episodes ('lost time'), unexplained transitions in behavior, trance-like states.
differentials.physical_signs: Stereotyped rising epigastric auras, lip-smacking/fumbling automatisms, postictal confusion, brief episode duration (< 2-3 minutes).
differentials.workup: Prolonged Continuous Video-EEG monitoring with anterior temporal leads; 3T Brain MRI (epilepsy protocol).

differentials.overlap: Sudden dramatic behavioral shifts, personality disintegration, bizarre speech, amnesia in young females.
differentials.physical_signs: Involuntary orofacial dyskinesias, choreoathetosis, autonomic instability, hypoventilation, seizures.
differentials.workup: CSF and serum anti-GluN1 NMDA receptor antibodies; Pelvic ultrasound (ovarian teratoma screening); Continuous EEG.

differentials.overlap: Severe identity disturbance, rapid shifts in self-image and interpersonal presentation, stress-related dissociation.
differentials.physical_signs: Absence of true distinct identity states with separate autobiographical amnestic barriers; intense fear of abandonment, chronic emptiness.
differentials.workup: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-5 Dissociative Disorders (SCID-D); SCID-5-PD.

differentials.overlap: Periods of unremembered complex behaviors ('lost time'), waking in strange locations.
differentials.physical_signs: Slurred speech, ataxia, nystagmus, elevated blood alcohol concentration or positive benzodiazepine screen.
differentials.workup: Serial Urine Drug Screen; Blood alcohol level; Collateral history from observers.

red_flags: Brief stereotypic trance episodes lasting < 3 minutes accompanied by lip smacking or hand fumbling (epilepsy).
Involuntary facial dyskinesias or choreic movements (autoimmune encephalitis).
Amnestic periods correlating strictly with alcohol or sedative consumption.

name: Dissociative Amnesia
symptoms: An inability to recall important autobiographical information, usually of a traumatic or stressful nature, that is inconsistent with ordinary forgetfulness (localized, selective, or generalized amnesia), with or without purposeful travel or bewildered wandering associated with identity amnesia (dissociative fugue).

differentials.overlap: Sudden dense anterograde amnesia, confusion, loss of recent memory.
differentials.physical_signs: Preserved personal identity (patient knows who they are, unlike generalized dissociative amnesia/fugue), perseverative repetitive questioning ('What am I doing here?'), duration < 24 hours (median 6-8 hrs).
differentials.workup: High-resolution Brain MRI with DWI (punctate diffusion restriction in CA1 region of hippocampus on 24-48h scan); EEG.

differentials.overlap: Recurrent brief episodes of waking with complete loss of memory for recent days/weeks.
differentials.physical_signs: Episodes typically occur upon waking, last 30-60 minutes, recur frequently (often multiple times per year), responsive to anticonvulsants.
differentials.workup: Sleep-deprived EEG or Video-EEG monitoring demonstrating temporal epileptiform sharp waves; Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Severe anterograde and retrograde autobiographical amnesia, confabulation.
differentials.physical_signs: Ataxia, horizontal nystagmus, ophthalmoplegia (Wernicke triad); chronic alcoholism or severe malnutrition history.
differentials.workup: Whole blood thiamine diphosphate; Brain MRI (T2 hyperintensities in mamillary bodies, medial thalami); Immediate IV thiamine.

differentials.overlap: Inability to remember events surrounding a traumatic event, memory gaps.
differentials.physical_signs: Documented head impact, loss of consciousness, retrograde and anterograde amnesia gradient, confusion, scalp contusion.
differentials.workup: Non-contrast Head CT / Brain MRI; Neurological examination.

red_flags: Dense anterograde amnesia with perseverative questioning lasting < 24 hours (Transient Global Amnesia).
Recurrent morning episodes of amnesia lasting < 1 hour (Transient Epileptic Amnesia).
Ataxia, nystagmus, or ophthalmoplegia in a malnourished or alcohol-dependent patient (Wernicke emergency).
Scalp hematoma or focal neurological deficits indicating traumatic brain injury.

name: Depersonalization / Derealization Disorder
symptoms: Persistent or recurrent experiences of depersonalization (experiences of unreality, detachment, or being an outside observer with respect to one's thoughts, feelings, sensations, body, or actions) and/or derealization (experiences of unreality or detachment with respect to surroundings - e.g., individuals or objects are experienced as unreal, dreamlike, foggy, lifeless, or visually distorted), with *intact reality testing*.

differentials.overlap: Sudden episodes of feeling outside of one's body, dreamlike unreality, micropsia/macropsia.
differentials.physical_signs: Paroxysmal duration (30-90 seconds), stereotyped aura (epigastric rising, burnt smell), automatisms, postictal confusion.
differentials.workup: Prolonged Video-EEG with temporal leads; 3T Brain MRI (epilepsy protocol).

differentials.overlap: Floating sensations, feeling disconnected from the ground, spatial unreality, visual distortion.
differentials.physical_signs: True vestibular dysfunction: abnormal head impulse test, motion intolerance, photophobia, history of migraines.
differentials.workup: Videonystagmography (VNG); Dynamic posturography; Neuro-otology evaluation.

differentials.overlap: Profound persistent feelings of unreality, detachment, 'living in a movie' triggered by a drug experience.
differentials.physical_signs: Abrupt onset following high-dose cannabis, synthetic cannabinoids, MDMA, or psilocybin; physical exam normal interictally.
differentials.workup: Urine Drug Screen; Comprehensive substance history; Reassurance and psychoeducation.

differentials.overlap: Feelings of mental detachment, floating, unreality, confusion.
differentials.physical_signs: Diaphoresis, tachycardia, fine hand tremor, pallor, immediate relief upon eating carbohydrates.
differentials.workup: Fingerstick capillary blood glucose during episode (< 55 mg/dL diagnostic).

red_flags: Episodes are brief (< 2 minutes), paroxysmal, and accompanied by lip smacking or fumbling (focal seizure).
Episodes accompanied by true rotational vertigo, nystagmus, or headache.
Diaphoresis, tachycardia, and hunger during derealization episodes that resolve upon consuming sugar.

name: Other Specified Dissociative Disorder
