symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a dissociative disorder predominate but do not meet full criteria for any specific disorder (e.g., chronic and recurrent syndromes of mixed dissociative symptoms; identity disturbance due to prolonged and intensive coercive persuasion [brainwashing]; acute dissociative reactions to stressful events; dissociative trance).

differentials.overlap: Dissociative trances, sudden amnesia, confusion, emotional detachment.
differentials.physical_signs: Faciobrachial dystonic seizures (brief frequent arm/facial jerks), hyponatremia, sleep disruption.
differentials.workup: Serum and CSF autoimmune encephalopathy antibody panel; Brain MRI; Video-EEG.

differentials.overlap: Carrying out complex tasks with no conscious memory or awareness ('trance-like state'), lost time.
differentials.physical_signs: Excessive daytime sleepiness, cataplexy (muscle weakness with laughter), hypnagogic hallucinations, sleep paralysis.
differentials.workup: Overnight Polysomnography followed by Multiple Sleep Latency Test (MSLT: mean sleep latency <= 8 min, >= 2 SOREMPs).

differentials.overlap: Trance states, lack of responsiveness to painful stimuli, feelings of detachment.
differentials.physical_signs: Nystagmus (rotary or vertical), hypertension, tachycardia, muscle rigidity, analgesia.
differentials.workup: Expanded toxicology screening (GC-MS); Serum electrolytes.

red_flags: Vertical or rotary nystagmus with marked analgesia to pain (dissociative toxin exposure).
Brief frequent facial and arm jerking movements (faciobrachial dystonic seizures in LGI1 encephalitis).
Loss of muscle tone triggered by laughter or humor (cataplexy / narcolepsy).

name: Unspecified Dissociative Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a dissociative disorder predominate but there is insufficient information to make a specific diagnosis (e.g., in acute emergency evaluations).

differentials.overlap: Apparent dissociative trance, fluctuating responsiveness, confusion, mutism.
differentials.physical_signs: Subtle rhythmic eyelid fluttering, minor facial twitching, perseverative automatic gestures.
differentials.workup: Urgent Continuous Video-EEG (demonstrating continuous epileptiform discharges); Response to IV lorazepam.

differentials.mimic: Acute Inhalant Toxicity (Toluene, Nitrous Oxide) (T52.91XA / T41.0X1A)
differentials.overlap: Acute detachment from reality, confusion, euphoria, unresponsiveness.
differentials.physical_signs: 'Glue-sniffer's rash' (perioral eczematous erythema), chemical breath odor, cerebellar ataxia, slurred speech.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive blood/urine toxicology; BMP (hypokalemia, renal tubular acidosis from toluene); Chest X-ray.

differentials.overlap: Disorientation, detachment, altered mental status, bizarre affect.
differentials.physical_signs: Fever, neck stiffness, photophobia, headache, Kernig/Brudzinski signs.
differentials.workup: Lumbar puncture (CSF cell count, protein, glucose, viral PCR panel); Brain CT/MRI.

red_flags: Fever, headache, and nuchal rigidity in a patient with altered consciousness (meningoencephalitis).
Rhythmic eyelid twitches during unresponsiveness (NCSE).
Perioral chemical rash and strange hydrocarbon odor on breath (inhalant abuse).

name: Somatic Symptom Disorder
symptoms: One or more somatic symptoms that are distressing or result in significant disruption of daily life, accompanied by excessive thoughts, feelings, or behaviors related to the somatic symptoms or associated health concerns (disproportionate and persistent thoughts about seriousness, high health anxiety, excessive time and energy devoted to symptoms) lasting >= 6 months.

differentials.overlap: Multiple vague, migratory somatic complaints: joint pains, chest aches, severe fatigue, headaches.
differentials.physical_signs: Malar butterfly rash, photosensitivity, non-erosive arthritis, oral ulcers, Raynaud phenomenon, serositis.
differentials.workup: Antinuclear Antibodies (ANA > 1:160); Anti-dsDNA; Anti-Smith; Complement C3/C4; Urinalysis.

differentials.overlap: Vague fluctuating sensations: tingling, numbness, electric shocks, heaviness in limbs, fatigue.
differentials.physical_signs: Lhermitte sign (electric shock down spine on neck flexion), Uhthoff phenomenon (symptoms worsen with hot shower), optic neuritis, hyperreflexia, Babinski.
differentials.workup: Brain and Spinal Cord MRI with gadolinium (Dawson fingers, periventricular plaques); CSF oligoclonal bands.

differentials.overlap: Multiple diffuse somatic aches ('bones, stones, groans, psychiatric overtones'), chronic fatigue, abdominal pain.
differentials.physical_signs: Musculoskeletal weakness, hyporeflexia, constipation, nephrolithiasis.
differentials.workup: Serum total calcium (> 10.5 mg/dL); Ionized calcium; Intact PTH (elevated or inappropriately normal); 24-hr urine calcium.

differentials.overlap: Fluctuating fatigue, difficulty chewing, voice weakening, limb weakness, labeled as somatization.
differentials.physical_signs: Fatigable ptosis (worse on 1-minute upward gaze), binocular diplopia, ice-pack test positive, normal sensation.
differentials.workup: Serum Anti-Acetylcholine Receptor (AChR) antibodies; Repetitive nerve stimulation (decremental response); Chest CT (thymoma).

differentials.overlap: Widespread multisite joint pain, chronic fatigue, subluxations, gastrointestinal motility distress.
differentials.physical_signs: Beighton hypermobility score >= 5/9, skin hyperextensibility (> 1.5 cm volar forearm), atrophic papyraceous scars, easy bruising.
differentials.workup: Clinical 2017 International hEDS Criteria assessment; Echocardiogram (aortic root diameter); Rule out genetic connective tissue variants.

red_flags: Positive Lhermitte electric sensation or worsening of neurological symptoms in hot baths (Uhthoff phenomenon).
Fatigable eyelid drooping (ptosis) that improves after applying an ice pack for 2 minutes (Myasthenia Gravis).
Elevated serum calcium (> 10.5 mg/dL) with diffuse bone and abdominal pain.
Joint hypermobility (Beighton score >= 5) with joint subluxations and skin hyperextensibility (EDS).

name: Illness Anxiety Disorder
symptoms: Preoccupation with having or acquiring a serious, undiagnosed medical illness, with somatic symptoms *not* present or only mild in intensity, accompanied by high health anxiety, easily alarmed about health status, performing excessive health-related behaviors (repeated body checking) or maladaptive avoidance, lasting >= 6 months.

differentials.overlap: Constant terror that one has a fatal cardiac disease, frequent medical checks.
differentials.physical_signs: Paroxysmal severe hypertension (> 180-220 mmHg), pounding headache, profuse diaphoresis, pallor during episodes.
differentials.workup: Plasma free metanephrines/normetanephrines; 24-hr urine metanephrines; Abdominal CT/MRI.

differentials.overlap: Persistent intuition that something is physically wrong despite normal routine screenings.
differentials.physical_signs: Unexplained weight loss (> 10%), drenching night sweats, painless lymphadenopathy, occult GI bleeding (positive FIT test).
differentials.workup: Fecal Immunochemical Test (FIT); Age-appropriate cancer screening (colonoscopy, mammography, low-dose chest CT); Complete blood count; Serum protein electrophoresis.

differentials.overlap: Preoccupation with bodily sensations, vague limb stiffness, chronic internal tremulousness.
differentials.physical_signs: Loss of smell (anosmia), REM sleep behavior disorder, subtle asymmetric loss of arm swing, micrographic handwriting.
differentials.workup: DaT-SPECT scan; UPDRS motor evaluation; Neurological examination.

red_flags: Severe episodic hypertension (> 180 mmHg) with diaphoresis and pallor.
Unexplained weight loss > 10% of body weight or drenching night sweats.
Unilateral loss of arm swing or anosmia preceding motor tremor.

name: Functional Neurological Symptom Disorder (Conversion)
symptoms: One or more symptoms of altered voluntary motor or sensory function, with clinical findings providing clear evidence of *incompatibility between the symptom and recognized neurological or medical conditions*.

differentials.overlap: Convulsive paroxysmal shaking, pelvic thrusting, thrashing, apparent unresponsiveness.
differentials.physical_signs: True epileptic signs: stertorous postictal breathing, tongue biting (specifically lateral tongue borders, unlike tongue tip/lip in PNES), postictal extensor plantars (Babinski), pupillary unresponsiveness; PNES features: eye closure with resistance to opening, preserved pupillary light reflex, fluctuating ictal course.
differentials.workup: Continuous synchronous Video-EEG monitoring during a typical event (recommended gold standard: ictal epileptiform discharges vs normal awake alpha/beta background during event); Postictal serum prolactin (elevated > 2-3x baseline within 20 min of generalized tonic-clonic seizure).

differentials.overlap: Acute paraparesis, sensory loss, visual loss (apparent functional blindness).
differentials.physical_signs: True neurological signs: relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD / Marcus Gunn pupil), hyperreflexia, extensor plantars (positive Babinski), sensory level on trunk; Functional signs: Hoover sign positive (involuntary downward extension of paralyzed leg when flexing contralateral hip against resistance).
differentials.workup: Brain and Spinal Cord MRI with gadolinium (demyelinating plaques); Visual Evoked Potentials (VEP); CSF oligoclonal bands.

differentials.overlap: Acute ascending weakness, inability to walk, sensory numbness in feet.
differentials.physical_signs: True GBS signs: complete generalized areflexia (absent deep tendon reflexes), symmetric flaccid weakness, autonomic instability, facial diplegia; Hoover sign negative.
differentials.workup: Lumbar puncture (albuminocytological dissociation: elevated protein > 45-200 mg/dL with normal WBC < 5-10); EMG/NCS (demyelination).

differentials.overlap: Sudden onset of hemiparesis, facial weakness, speech difficulty, sensory loss.
differentials.physical_signs: NIHSS neurological deficits conforming to vascular anatomical territories (e.g., MCA territory); asymmetry of facial lower half with forehead sparing; positive Babinski sign.
differentials.workup: Urgent Non-contrast Head CT + CT Angiography of head/neck; Brain MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI).

red_flags: Lateral tongue border laceration or urinary incontinence during convulsions (strongly favors epileptic seizure).
Complete generalized areflexia (absent deep tendon reflexes) with ascending weakness (Guillain-Barré emergency).
Relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD) on swinging flashlight test (optic neuritis).
True Babinski sign (dorsiflexion of great toe with fanning of other toes) on plantar stimulation.

name: Psychological Factors Affecting Other Medical Conditions
symptoms: A medical symptom or condition is present, and psychological or behavioral factors adversely affect the medical condition by influencing the course, interfering with treatment adherence, constituting additional well-established health risks, or precipitating/exacerbating symptoms.

differentials.overlap: Chest discomfort or dyspnea provoked by acute psychological stress in patients with known CAD.
differentials.physical_signs: Diaphoresis, transient S4 gallop during episodes, normal resting ECG.
differentials.workup: Exercise or Pharmacologic Nuclear Stress Test (SPECT/PET myocardial perfusion); Coronary CT Angiography.

differentials.overlap: Severe glucose volatility, frequent hospitalizations, depression affecting diabetes self-care.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe dehydration, Kussmaul respirations, fruity breath, lipodystrophy at injection sites.
differentials.workup: Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM); HbA1c; Beta-hydroxybutyrate; Psychosocial insulin omission evaluation.

differentials.mimic: Severe Refractory Asthma / Vocal Cord Dysfunction (J45.909 / J38.3)
differentials.overlap: Acute severe wheezing, dyspnea, panic during interpersonal conflict.
differentials.physical_signs: Inspiratory stridor heard loudest over larynx (Vocal Cord Dysfunction) vs expiratory polyphonic wheezing (true asthma); paradoxical vocal cord adduction during inspiration.
differentials.workup: Spirometry with flow-volume loops (flattened inspiratory loop in VCD); Laryngoscopy during symptomatic episode.

red_flags: Inspiratory stridor loudest over neck rather than chest (indicates Vocal Cord Dysfunction).
Recurrent DKA admissions in adolescents (often driven by deliberate insulin omission for weight control / diabulimia).
Transient ST depressions on ECG during emotional arguments in a CAD patient.

name: Factitious Disorder (Imposed on Self / Another)
symptoms: Falsification of physical or psychological signs or symptoms, or induction of injury or disease, associated with identified deception, presenting oneself or another individual (victim) to others as ill, impaired, or injured, in the *absence of external rewards* (such as economic gain or avoiding legal duty, which defines malingering).

differentials.mimic: Exogenous Insulin / Sulfonylurea Induced Hypoglycemia (E16.0 / T38.3X1A)
differentials.overlap: Recurrent unexplained severe hypoglycemic comas, diaphoresis, confusion, seizures.
differentials.physical_signs: Whipple triad present, blood glucose < 40-55 mg/dL during episodes; patient or caregiver has access to insulin/diabetic medications.
differentials.workup: Supervised blood draw during acute hypoglycemia: low plasma glucose with high plasma insulin (> 30 mcU/mL) AND suppressed plasma C-peptide (< 0.2 ng/mL) and low proinsulin (proves exogenous insulin administration); Serum/urine sulfonylurea screen.

differentials.mimic: Factitious Fever / Injected Pathogen Sepsis (R50.9 / A41.9)
differentials.overlap: Recurrent unexplained polymicrobial bacteremia, non-healing cutaneous abscesses, persistent high fevers.
differentials.physical_signs: Normal pulse rate despite high recorded thermometer temperature ('temperature-pulse dissociation'); skin lesions accessible to dominant hand; blood cultures growing enteric flora (E. coli, Bacteroides, polymicrobial).
differentials.workup: Supervised nurse rectal temperature checks; Blood cultures growing multiple enteric/fecal organisms without intra-abdominal source.

differentials.overlap: Severe spontaneous ecchymoses, hematuria, hemarthrosis, epistaxis.
differentials.physical_signs: Diffuse bruising, petechiae, lack of prior bleeding disorder history.
differentials.workup: Prothrombin Time (PT) / INR markedly elevated (> 5.0); Partial Thromboplastin Time (PTT); Plasma Warfarin and Brodifacoum (superwarfarin rat poison) liquid chromatography level.

red_flags: High serum insulin with suppressed C-peptide (< 0.2 ng/mL) during severe hypoglycemia (proof of exogenous insulin injection).
Polymicrobial bacteremia with fecal/enteric organisms in an immunocompetent patient with normal bowel.
Marked elevation of INR with detectable plasma brodifacoum (superwarfarin rodenticide poisoning).
In Factitious Imposed on Another (Munchausen by Proxy): victim's symptoms improve exclusively when separated from the caregiver.

name: Other Specified Somatic Symptom Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a somatic symptom disorder predominate but do not meet full criteria (e.g., brief somatic symptom disorder [< 6 months]; brief illness anxiety disorder [< 6 months]; illness anxiety disorder without excessive health-related behaviors).

differentials.overlap: Vague chronic fatigue, intermittent nausea, dizziness, mild weight loss.
differentials.physical_signs: Mild cutaneous hyperpigmentation, postural drop in systolic blood pressure (> 15-20 mmHg).
differentials.workup: Morning serum cortisol; Cosyntropin stimulation test; BMP (electrolytes).

differentials.overlap: Vague malaise, myalgias, arthralgias, throat irritation, anxiety.
differentials.physical_signs: Transient maculopapular rash, generalized non-tender lymphadenopathy, pharyngitis, aphthous ulcers.
differentials.workup: HIV 4th-generation antigen/antibody immunoassay; Plasma HIV RNA viral load.

differentials.overlap: Wandering musculoskeletal pains, dry eyes, fatigue, low-grade malaise.
differentials.physical_signs: Raynaud phenomenon, mild joint puffiness without erosions.
differentials.workup: ANA; ESR; CRP; Rheumatoid factor; Anti-Ro/La antibodies.

red_flags: Postural systolic blood pressure drop > 20 mmHg with hyperpigmentation of palmar creases.
Generalized lymphadenopathy and acute flu-like rash following unprotected sexual exposure (HIV seroconversion).
Positive ANA with elevated ESR and inflammatory joint puffiness.

name: Unspecified Somatic Symptom & Related Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a somatic symptom disorder predominate but there is insufficient information to make a specific diagnosis.

differentials.overlap: Fluctuating vague somatic complaints: headache, nausea, malaise, fatigue, dizziness.
differentials.physical_signs: Absence of fever, symptoms improve when away from home/work; multiple household members affected.
differentials.workup: Venous or arterial carboxyhemoglobin (COHb); Environmental building CO inspection.

differentials.overlap: Vague dizziness, early satiety, bloating, intermittent diarrhea, sweating disturbances.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting tachycardia with fixed heart rate (loss of beat-to-beat variability), orthostatic hypotension.
differentials.workup: Fasting blood glucose; HbA1c; Autonomic reflex screen; Gastric emptying scintigraphy.

differentials.overlap: Severe burning, stinging, or aching pains in extremities with completely normal EMG/NCS.
differentials.physical_signs: Loss of pinprick and temperature sensation in stocking-glove distribution with *preserved* reflexes and normal vibratory sense.
differentials.workup: Skin punch biopsy demonstrating reduced Intraepidermal Nerve Fiber Density (IENFD); Fasting glucose / OGTT; TSH; B12.

red_flags: Severe burning limb pain with normal nerve conduction studies (demands skin punch biopsy for small fiber neuropathy).
Symptoms wax and wane depending on presence in a specific building with gas appliances (CO poisoning).
Fixed resting tachycardia with orthostatic hypotension in an undiagnosed diabetic patient.

name: Pseudocyesis
symptoms: A false belief of being pregnant that is associated with objective physical signs and reported symptoms of pregnancy, including abdominal enlargement, reduced menstrual flow, amenorrhea, subjective sensation of fetal movements, nausea, breast engorgement and secretions, and labor pains.

differentials.mimic: True Undiagnosed Pregnancy / Ectopic Pregnancy (Z33.1 / O00.9)
differentials.overlap: Amenorrhea, abdominal enlargement, breast tenderness, morning sickness, perceived fetal movements.
differentials.physical_signs: True uterine enlargement on bimanual pelvic exam, audible fetal heart tones (> 10-12 weeks by Doppler), cervical softening (Goodell sign) and bluish discoloration (Chadwick sign).
differentials.workup: Serum quantitative beta-hCG (negative in pseudocyesis; markedly elevated in true pregnancy); Pelvic / transvaginal ultrasound (demonstrating empty uterus in pseudocyesis vs gestational sac/fetus).

differentials.overlap: Secondary amenorrhea, persistent bilateral galactorrhea (milky breast secretion), breast tenderness, weight gain.
differentials.physical_signs: Galactorrhea on manual nipple expression, bitemporal visual field deficits, absence of abdominal expansion.
differentials.workup: Fasting morning serum prolactin (markedly elevated > 100-200 ng/mL in prolactinoma); Pituitary MRI with and without gadolinium.

differentials.mimic: Large Ovarian Neoplasm / Mucinous Cystadenoma (D27.9 / C56.9)
differentials.overlap: Marked progressive abdominal distension, pelvic fullness, urinary frequency, amenorrhea.
differentials.physical_signs: Large palpable, firm or cystic pelvic-abdominal mass dull to percussion; absence of normal everted umbilicus of pregnancy.
differentials.workup: Pelvic ultrasound; Abdominal/pelvic CT; Serum CA-125 tumor marker; Serum beta-hCG (negative).

red_flags: Negative serum beta-hCG with visible abdominal distension and perceived fetal kicks (definitive proof of pseudocyesis).
Bitemporal hemianopia and bilateral galactorrhea (pituitary macroadenoma).
Large pelvic-abdominal mass with negative pregnancy test (urgent gynecologic oncology evaluation for ovarian tumor).

name: Pica (Childhood & Adult)
symptoms: Persistent eating of non-nutritive, non-food substances (e.g., ice, dirt, clay, chalk, paint chips, paper, hair, laundry starch) over a period of at least 1 month, developmentally inappropriate and not part of a culturally supported practice.

differentials.overlap: Compulsive eating of large quantities of ice (pagophagia), freezer frost, clay, or dirt.
differentials.physical_signs: Conjunctival pallor, koilonychia (spoon nails), angular cheilitis, atrophic glossitis, fatigue, restless legs; pica resolves dramatically within days of oral/IV iron replacement.
differentials.workup: Serum Ferritin (< 30 ng/mL; < 15 diagnostic); Serum Iron and TIBC (saturation < 15%); Complete Blood Count (microcytic anemia, MCV < 80 fL).

differentials.mimic: Chronic Lead Poisoning (Plumbism Secondary to Pica) (T56.0X1A)
differentials.overlap: Eating paint chips, plaster, or contaminated soil, followed by cognitive decline, irritability.
differentials.physical_signs: Burton's line on gums, microcytic anemia, colicky abdominal pain, peripheral motor neuropathy, developmental regression.
differentials.workup: Whole blood lead level (BLL >= 3.5 mcg/dL in children; > 20 mcg/dL in adults); Peripheral blood smear (basophilic stippling); Long bone X-rays.

differentials.overlap: Compulsive non-food ingestion, altered taste (dysgeusia), anorexia.
differentials.physical_signs: Perioral and acral erythematous scaling dermatitis, alopecia, chronic diarrhea, impaired wound healing, hypogonadism.
differentials.workup: Serum plasma zinc level (< 60-70 mcg/dL); Alkaline phosphatase (low, as it is a zinc-dependent metalloenzyme).

differentials.overlap: Complication of pica: severe postprandial abdominal pain, early satiety, vomiting.
differentials.physical_signs: Palpable abdominal mass, peritoneal signs, severe halitosis, abdominal distension.
differentials.workup: Abdominal X-ray / CT scan with contrast; Upper endoscopy (EGD).

red_flags: Severe craving for ice (pagophagia) in a fatigued patient (pathognomonic for severe iron deficiency).
Blood lead level >= 3.5 mcg/dL in a child ingesting non-food substances.
Signs of bowel obstruction (vomiting, abdominal distension, obstipation) in a patient ingesting hair, clay, or paper (bezoar).

name: Rumination Disorder
symptoms: Repeated regurgitation of food over a period of at least 1 month, where regurgitated food may be re-chewed, re-swallowed, or spit out, not attributable to an associated gastrointestinal or other medical condition (e.g., GERD, pyloric stenosis).

differentials.overlap: Postprandial regurgitation of gastric contents into the mouth, heartburn, dysphagia.
differentials.physical_signs: Regurgitation is involuntary, sour/acidic in taste, painful, accompanied by retrosternal pyrosis and water brash; rumination regurgitation is effortless, non-acidic, pleasant/neutral in taste.
differentials.workup: 24-hour ambulatory esophageal pH/impedance monitoring; Upper endoscopy (EGD evaluating erosive esophagitis).

differentials.overlap: Postprandial nausea, vomiting of undigested food hours after meals, early satiety, weight loss.
differentials.physical_signs: Abdominal distension, epigastric tenderness, succussion splash heard on auscultation over epigastrium hours after a meal; history of diabetes mellitus.
differentials.workup: 4-hour solid-phase Gastric Emptying Scintigraphy (retention > 10% of meal at 4 hours confirms gastroparesis).

differentials.overlap: Regurgitation of completely undigested, non-acidic food, retrosternal fullness, weight loss.
differentials.physical_signs: Progressive dysphagia to both solids AND liquids from the onset, nocturnal cough/regurgitation.
differentials.workup: High-Resolution Esophageal Manometry (absence of peristalsis and failure of lower esophageal sphincter [LES] relaxation); Barium swallow ('bird's-beak' tapering of distal esophagus).

differentials.overlap: Regurgitation of undigested food hours after eating, halitosis, coughing.
differentials.physical_signs: Older adult, dysphagia, gurgling neck mass (Boyce sign), recurrent aspiration pneumonia.
differentials.workup: Barium swallow esophagram.

red_flags: Dysphagia to both solids and liquids with bird's-beak appearance on barium swallow (Achalasia).
Regurgitated material is highly acidic and accompanied by burning retrosternal pain (GERD).
Succussion splash heard in stomach > 4 hours after eating (gastroparesis).

name: Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID)
symptoms: An eating or feeding disturbance (apparent lack of interest in eating, avoidance based on sensory characteristics of food, or concern about aversive consequences of eating [choking, vomiting]) manifested by persistent failure to meet appropriate nutritional/energy needs associated with: significant weight loss, nutritional deficiency, dependence on enteral feeding/supplements, or marked psychosocial interference, in the *absence of body image distortion*.

differentials.overlap: Severe food avoidance, fear of swallowing, eating very slowly, cutting food into tiny pieces, avoiding meats/breads.
differentials.physical_signs: History of recurrent food impactions requiring ER disimpaction, retrosternal dysphagia, concurrent atopic disease (asthma, eczema, allergic rhinitis).
differentials.workup: Upper endoscopy with esophageal biopsies (demonstrating >= 15 eosinophils per high-power field [HPF]); Barium swallow (esophageal rings / 'trachealization' of esophagus).

differentials.overlap: Food refusal, chronic weight loss, nausea, abdominal pain following meals, growth failure.
differentials.physical_signs: Abdominal distension, muscle wasting, dermatitis herpetiformis, iron-deficiency anemia refractory to oral iron, aphthous stomatitis.
differentials.workup: Serum Tissue Transglutaminase IgA (tTG-IgA) and total IgA; Upper endoscopy with duodenal biopsies (villous atrophy, Marsh 3).

differentials.overlap: Refusal to eat, fear of eating due to anticipated postprandial abdominal pain, profound weight loss, anorexia.
differentials.physical_signs: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty, low-grade fevers, aphthous oral ulcers, perianal skin tags or fistulas, nocturnal diarrhea.
differentials.workup: Fecal Calprotectin (> 150-250 mcg/g); ESR / CRP (elevated); CBC (anemia); Colonoscopy with ileoscopy and biopsy.

differentials.overlap: Intense terror of choking, refusal of solid foods, liquid-only diet.
differentials.physical_signs: Coughing or throat clearing during swallowing, wet/gurgly voice after swallowing, nasal regurgitation.
differentials.workup: Modified Barium Swallow Study (MBSS) / Fiberoptic Endoscopic Evaluation of Swallowing (FEES).

red_flags: History of actual food bolus impaction requiring endoscopic removal (Eosinophilic Esophagitis).
Perianal skin tags, anal fissures, nocturnal diarrhea, or elevated fecal calprotectin (Crohn's disease).
Choking, coughing, or wet voice immediately following swallows on physical exam (oropharyngeal dysphagia).
Celiac antibodies (tTG-IgA) positive with failure to thrive.

name: Anorexia Nervosa (Restricting & Binge-Purge)
symptoms: Restriction of energy intake relative to requirements leading to significantly low body weight in the context of age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health, accompanied by intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, and disturbance in the way in which one's body weight or shape is experienced (distorted body image).

differentials.overlap: Profound emaciation, cachexia, amenorrhea, dry skin, severe anorexia, apathy.
differentials.physical_signs: Loss of axillary and pubic hair (unlike anorexia nervosa where body hair is preserved with lanugo hair growth), hypotension, lack of lactation postpartum, absence of fear of gaining weight.
differentials.workup: Basal anterior pituitary hormone panel: low/undetectable LH, FSH, TSH, Free T4, ACTH, morning cortisol, IGF-1; Pituitary MRI.

differentials.overlap: Severe weight loss, anorexia, nausea, fatigue, amenorrhea.
differentials.physical_signs: Cutaneous hyperpigmentation (palmar creases, buccal mucosa), orthostatic hypotension, salt craving; absence of distorted drive for thinness.
differentials.workup: Morning serum cortisol (< 3 mcg/dL); Cosyntropin stimulation test; Plasma ACTH (> 100 pg/mL); BMP (hyponatremia + hyperkalemia).

differentials.overlap: Profound weight loss, food restriction due to postprandial discomfort, amenorrhea.
differentials.physical_signs: Fever, perianal disease, oral aphthae, abdominal cramping, chronic diarrhea, elevated inflammatory markers.
differentials.workup: Fecal calprotectin; Colonoscopy with ileoscopy; CT enterography; CRP/ESR.

differentials.overlap: Profound weight loss, amenorrhea, physical restlessness, anxiety.
differentials.physical_signs: Tremor, tachycardia, warm moist skin, goiter, ravenous appetite (eating constantly yet losing weight, opposite of AN food restriction).
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (< 0.01 mIU/L); Free T4 and Free T3 (markedly elevated).

differentials.overlap: Rapid unintentional wasting, loss of appetite, fatigue, amenorrhea.
differentials.physical_signs: Lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, night sweats, lack of fear of weight gain.
differentials.workup: Complete blood count; Comprehensive metabolic panel; Chest/abdominal CT; ESR/CRP.

red_flags: Complete loss of pubic and axillary hair in an emaciated patient (Sheehan's / Panhypopituitarism; AN preserves hair and develops lanugo).
Cutaneous hyperpigmentation with hyperkalemia and hyponatremia (Addison's disease).
Severe weight loss occurring despite a documented ravenous food intake (hyperthyroidism or malabsorption).
Absence of fear of gaining weight or absence of body image distortion.

name: Bulimia Nervosa
symptoms: Recurrent episodes of binge eating (eating an objectively large amount of food in a discrete period with a sense of lack of control) accompanied by recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors to prevent weight gain (self-induced vomiting, misuse of laxatives/diuretics, fasting, excessive exercise), occurring at least once a week for 3 months, with self-evaluation unduly influenced by body shape and weight.

differentials.overlap: Periodic episodes of compulsive megaphagia (gorging on massive quantities of food), depression.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe periodic hypersomnia (sleeping 18-22 hours daily for days/weeks), hypersexuality, childish disinhibition; normal weight and euthymia between episodes; absence of compensatory purging.
differentials.workup: Polysomnography; Brain MRI; Clinical diagnosis.

differentials.overlap: Recurrent severe vomiting, abdominal pain, weight fluctuations.
differentials.physical_signs: Pathognomonic compulsive prolonged hot bathing/showering for relief; chronic daily heavy cannabis use; vomiting is involuntary, not self-induced; absence of body image obsession.
differentials.workup: Urine Drug Screen (positive for THC); Cessation of cannabis leads to complete symptom cure.

differentials.overlap: Hyperorality, bulimic binge eating (putting non-food items in mouth, compulsive eating), hypersexuality.
differentials.physical_signs: Visual agnosia ('psychic blindness' - inability to recognize objects visually), placidity (loss of fear/anger), bilateral anterior temporal lobe/amygdala injury.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (bilateral anterior temporal lobe lesions from herpes encephalitis, trauma, or Pick's disease).

differentials.overlap: Sudden episodes of uncontrollable ravenous eating, dizziness, anxiety, diaphoresis.
differentials.physical_signs: Whipple triad present; eating is driven by neuroglycopenic hunger; absence of purging or body shape distortion.
differentials.workup: 72-hour supervised fast; Glucose, insulin, C-peptide.

red_flags: Compulsive hot baths/showers providing relief from intractable vomiting in a chronic cannabis smoker (Cannabis Hyperemesis).
Episodes of sleeping 20 hours a day alternating with compulsive eating and hypersexuality (Kleine-Levin).
Visual agnosia (examining objects with mouth rather than eyes) following encephalitis (Klüver-Bucy).
Hypokalemic hypochloremic metabolic alkalosis on BMP (classic electrolyte footprint of frequent self-induced vomiting requiring cardiac monitoring).

name: Binge-Eating Disorder
symptoms: Recurrent episodes of binge eating characterized by eating much more rapidly than normal, eating until uncomfortably full, eating large amounts when not physically hungry, eating alone out of embarrassment, and feeling disgusted, depressed, or very guilty afterward, occurring at least once a week for 3 months, with marked distress and *absence* of regular compensatory purging behaviors.

differentials.overlap: Insatiable hunger, compulsive foraging, gorging on food, obesity, behavioral tantrums over food.
differentials.physical_signs: Short stature, small hands and feet, hypogonadism, cognitive limitations, history of severe neonatal hypotonia ('floppy baby'), almond-shaped eyes.
differentials.workup: DNA methylation analysis of chromosome 15q11-q13 (absence of paternal expression).

differentials.overlap: Compulsive binge eating, voracious appetite, craving sweets, stuffing food into mouth.
differentials.physical_signs: Social disinhibition, loss of empathy, apathy, executive dysfunction, primitive frontal release reflexes; onset aged 45-65.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (asymmetric frontal/temporal atrophy); FDG-PET scan.

differentials.overlap: Rapid onset of uncontrolled hyperphagia, massive weight gain, loss of satiety.
differentials.physical_signs: Headaches, bitemporal hemianopia, endocrine deficiencies (hypothyroidism, hypogonadism, diabetes insipidus).
differentials.workup: Brain/Pituitary MRI with contrast (suprasellar calcified cystic mass); Comprehensive pituitary hormone panel; Visual field testing.

differentials.overlap: Intense carbohydrate cravings, insatiable appetite, rapid weight gain.
differentials.physical_signs: Metabolic syndrome: rapid abdominal weight gain, dyslipidemia, hyperglycemia, taking high-metabolic-risk antipsychotics.
differentials.workup: Fasting lipid panel; Fasting glucose and HbA1c; Medication audit.

red_flags: Sudden voracious hyperphagia accompanied by bitemporal visual field deficits and headaches (craniopharyngioma / hypothalamic tumor).
History of severe neonatal hypotonia with short stature and small hands (Prader-Willi syndrome).
New-onset bingeing and sweet craving in a middle-aged adult with personality changes (FTD).
Rapid escalation of appetite following initiation of olanzapine or clozapine.

name: Other Specified Feeding or Eating Disorder (OSFED)
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a feeding and eating disorder predominate but do not meet full criteria for any specific disorder, including: Atypical Anorexia Nervosa (all criteria met except weight is within or above normal range despite massive weight loss); Subthreshold Bulimia Nervosa; Subthreshold Binge-Eating Disorder; Purging Disorder; Night Eating Syndrome.

differentials.overlap: Severe weight loss, dietary restriction, guilt, body image distress.
differentials.physical_signs: Polyuria, polydipsia, fatigue, recurrent diabetic ketoacidosis; deliberate intentional omission or under-dosing of insulin to induce glycosuria and rapid weight loss.
differentials.workup: HbA1c (markedly elevated > 10-14%); Urine glucose and ketones; Prescription refill audit comparing prescribed insulin vs actual pharmacy pickup.

differentials.overlap: Fear of eating, rapid weight loss, severe postprandial distress, labeled as atypical anorexia.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe dull postprandial epigastric pain occurring within 30 min of eating, epigastric abdominal bruit heard on auscultation, absence of body image distortion.
differentials.workup: Mesenteric Duplex Ultrasound with respiratory maneuvers; CT Angiography of abdomen demonstrating compression of celiac artery by median arcuate ligament.

differentials.overlap: Postprandial vomiting, early satiety, severe nausea, progressive food avoidance.
differentials.physical_signs: Extreme postprandial epigastric pain relieved specifically by assuming the knee-chest position or left lateral decubitus; compression of third portion of duodenum between aorta and SMA due to loss of mesenteric fat pad.
differentials.workup: Contrast CT Abdomen/Pelvis measuring aortomesenteric angle (< 22 degrees) and distance (< 8 mm); Upper GI series with small bowel follow-through.

red_flags: Severe postprandial pain relieved by assuming the knee-chest or prone position (SMA syndrome).
Epigastric vascular bruit heard on abdominal exam in a patient avoiding food (MALS).
Recurrent DKA with markedly elevated HbA1c in a diabetic patient obsessed with thinness (insulin omission / diabulimia).

name: Night Eating Syndrome
symptoms: Recurrent episodes of night eating, manifested by eating after awakening from sleep or by excessive food consumption after the evening meal (>= 25% of daily food intake consumed after evening meal), accompanied by full awareness and recall of eating, lack of morning appetite, severe insomnia, and significant distress.

differentials.overlap: Nocturnal food consumption, kitchen exploration, sleep disruption.
differentials.physical_signs: Patient consumes food during non-REM parasomnia with *partial or complete amnesia* upon morning waking; eating bizarre or dangerous food combinations (frozen foods, butter, dog food); injured while cooking in sleep.
differentials.workup: Overnight Video-Polysomnography (demonstrating awakenings from N3 slow-wave sleep associated with complex motor eating behaviors); Sleep medication review (commonly induced by zolpidem).

differentials.overlap: Waking in the middle of the night with urgent, ravenous hunger and trembling.
differentials.physical_signs: Profuse diaphoresis (night sweats), tachycardia, confusion, taking evening insulin or sulfonylurea.
differentials.workup: Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) demonstrating nocturnal glucose dips < 55 mg/dL.

differentials.overlap: Waking at 1:00 to 3:00 AM needing to eat milk or food to alleviate abdominal discomfort.
differentials.physical_signs: Epigastric gnawing pain that is reliably relieved by food intake; melena or occult blood in stool.
differentials.workup: Upper endoscopy (EGD); Helicobacter pylori stool antigen / urea breath test.

red_flags: Complete amnesia for nocturnal eating episodes or consuming bizarre inedible substances (Sleep-Related Eating Disorder / Zolpidem parasomnia).
Waking in drenching sweat with tremors and hunger in a diabetic patient.
Gnawing epigastric pain waking patient at night relieved by milk/food (peptic ulcer disease).

name: Purging Disorder
symptoms: Recurrent purging behavior to influence weight or shape (e.g., self-induced vomiting; misuse of laxatives, diuretics, or other medications) in the *absence of objective binge eating episodes* in individuals of normal or above-normal weight.

differentials.overlap: Recurrent discrete episodes of intractable vomiting and nausea.
differentials.physical_signs: Stereotypic paroxysmal episodes lasting 1-5 days occurring every few weeks/months with complete wellness between episodes; personal or family history of migraine; absence of weight/shape overvaluation.
differentials.workup: Upper endoscopy; Brain MRI; Abdominal CT (ruling out malrotation/intermittent volvulus); Response to antimigraine prophylactic agents (e.g., amitriptyline, topiramate).

differentials.overlap: Frequent episodes of vomiting, weight loss, distress.
differentials.physical_signs: Compulsive hot showering behavior; heavy daily cannabis use; absence of body image distortion.
differentials.workup: Urine Drug Screen; Resolution of vomiting upon verified cannabis cessation.

differentials.overlap: Recurrent episodes of unexplained nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramping, weight loss.
differentials.physical_signs: Orthostatic hypotension, hyperpigmentation, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia.
differentials.workup: Morning serum cortisol; Cosyntropin stimulation test; BMP.

differentials.overlap: Intractable nausea and vomiting lasting weeks, labeled erroneously as psychogenic purging.
differentials.physical_signs: Persistent hiccups, intractable vomiting without gastrointestinal lesions, followed by optic neuritis or transverse myelitis.
differentials.workup: Serum Aquaporin-4 (AQP4-IgG) antibodies; Brain MRI with contrast (demonstrating T2 lesion in dorsal medulla / area postrema).

red_flags: Intractable vomiting and hiccups lasting > 48 hours without gastrointestinal explanation (demands brain MRI for Area Postrema syndrome / NMOSD).
Stereotypic episodic vomiting cycles separated by weeks of complete health with migraine history (Cyclic Vomiting Syndrome).
Severe hypokalemia (< 3.0 mEq/L) with QT prolongation on ECG in any purging patient.

name: Enuresis (Nocturnal, Diurnal, Nocturnal & Diurnal)
symptoms: Repeated voiding of urine into bed or clothes, whether involuntary or intentional, occurring at least twice a week for 3 consecutive months, in a child who has reached a chronological age of at least 5 years.

differentials.mimic: Urinary Tract Infection & Posterior Urethral Valves (N39.0 / Q64.2)
differentials.overlap: Sudden onset of secondary enuresis, daytime frequency, urgency, damp pants.
differentials.physical_signs: Dysuria, fever, weak urinary stream, palpable bladder, suprapubic tenderness.
differentials.workup: Urinalysis and urine culture (bacteriuria, pyuria); Renal and bladder ultrasound; Voiding Cystourethrogram (VCUG).

differentials.overlap: Sudden emergence of nocturnal enuresis in a previously toilet-trained child, daytime wetting.
differentials.physical_signs: Polyuria, profound polydipsia (excessive thirst), polyphagia with weight loss, lethargy.
differentials.workup: Urine dipstick (heavy glycosuria and ketonuria); Random plasma blood glucose (> 200 mg/dL); HbA1c.

differentials.overlap: Persistent primary or secondary nocturnal enuresis, daytime behavioral irritability, ADHD symptoms.
differentials.physical_signs: Tonsillar/adenoidal hypertrophy (Brodsky grade 3-4+), chronic mouth breathing, nocturnal snoring with snorts/gasps, restless sleep.
differentials.workup: Pediatric Polysomnography (AHI >= 1 event/hr); ENT examination (adenotonsillectomy resolves enuresis in up to 75% of cases).

differentials.mimic: Tethered Spinal Cord Syndrome / Spina Bifida Occulta (Q06.8 / Q76.0)
differentials.overlap: Refractory nocturnal and diurnal enuresis, urinary dribbling, gait difficulties.
differentials.physical_signs: Cutaneous midline lumbosacral markers: hairy tuft (faun tail nevus), dermal dimple, lipoma, hemangioma; asymmetrical lower extremity reflexes, high-arched feet (pes cavus).
differentials.workup: Lumbosacral Spine MRI (low-lying conus medullaris below L2 level, thickened filum terminale > 2 mm).

red_flags: Cutaneous lumbosacral skin tags, hairy patch, or deep dimple (tethered cord).
Marked polyuria, unquenchable thirst, and weight loss (Type 1 Diabetes emergency).
Severe tonsillar hypertrophy with loud snoring and witnessed sleep gasps.
Weak, intermittent urinary stream or straining to void in boys (posterior urethral valves).

name: Encopresis (With or Without Constipation & Overflow)
symptoms: Repeated passage of feces into inappropriate places (e.g., clothing, floor), whether involuntary or intentional, occurring at least once a month for >= 3 months in a child with a chronological age of at least 4 years.

differentials.overlap: Severe chronic refractory constipation, fecal soiling, abdominal distension.
differentials.physical_signs: History of delayed passage of meconium (> 48 hours after birth), failure to thrive, empty rectal vault on digital rectal exam with a 'squirt sign' (explosive expulsion of flatus/liquid stool upon withdrawal of finger).
differentials.workup: Anorectal Manometry (absence of rectoanal inhibitory reflex [RAIR]); Contrast enema (transition zone); Rectal suction biopsy (definitive gold standard: absence of ganglion cells in submucosal plexus and hypertrophied nerve trunks).

differentials.overlap: Chronic abdominal distension, severe constipation, fecal soiling, growth stunting.
differentials.physical_signs: Pallor, muscle wasting, dermatitis herpetiformis, aphthous ulcers.
differentials.workup: Serum Tissue Transglutaminase IgA (tTG-IgA); Upper endoscopy with duodenal biopsies.

differentials.mimic: Occult Spinal Cord Dysraphism / Cauda Equina Compression (Q06.8)
differentials.overlap: Fecal soiling without constipation, loss of bowel awareness, urinary dribbling.
differentials.physical_signs: Decreased or absent anal sphincter tone ('patulous anus'), absent anal wink reflex, lower extremity weakness or sensory deficit.
differentials.workup: Lumbosacral Spine MRI; Neurological examination.

red_flags: Delayed meconium passage > 48 hours of life with explosive stool release on digital exam (Hirschsprung).
Absent anal wink reflex or patulous anal tone on rectal examination (spinal dysraphism).
Fecal incontinence in the complete absence of stool retention on abdominal palpation or rectal exam.

name: Other Specified Elimination Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of an elimination disorder predominate but do not meet full criteria (e.g., low-frequency enuresis or encopresis; isolated daytime pollakiuria).

differentials.mimic: Extraordinary Daytime Urinary Frequency (Pollakiuria / Sham Urination) (R35.0)
differentials.overlap: Voiding every 5-15 minutes throughout the day, daytime urgency, parental panic.
differentials.physical_signs: Voiding tiny amounts of normal urine; *completely normal overnight sleep* without nocturia or enuresis; completely normal physical and neurological exam.
differentials.workup: Urinalysis and culture (completely normal); Urine calcium/creatinine ratio (ruling out hypercalciuria); Reassurance (benign, self-limiting condition lasting 2-6 months).

differentials.overlap: Urinary frequency, dysuria, daytime urgency, occasional incontinence.
differentials.physical_signs: Microscopic hematuria, history of kidney stones in family.
differentials.workup: Spot urine calcium-to-creatinine ratio (> 0.21 in older children suggests hypercalciuria); 24-hr urine calcium excretion; Renal ultrasound.

differentials.overlap: Straining to defecate, incomplete evacuation, intermittent fecal spotting.
differentials.physical_signs: Paradoxical contraction or failure of relaxation of puborectalis muscle during defecation.
differentials.workup: High-Resolution Anorectal Manometry; Balloon expulsion test.

red_flags: Frequent daytime urination that completely disappears during sleep (benign Pollakiuria).
Microscopic hematuria on urinalysis (demands hypercalciuria and nephrolithiasis workup).
Severe dysuria or burning (demands urine culture).

name: Unspecified Elimination Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of an elimination disorder predominate but there is insufficient information to make a specific diagnosis.

differentials.mimic: Central or Nephrogenic Diabetes Insipidus (E23.2 / N25.1)
differentials.overlap: Massive polyuria, nocturnal enuresis, daytime urinary flooding.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe unquenchable thirst, drinking gallons of cold ice water, dehydration, elevated serum sodium.
differentials.workup: Serum sodium and osmolality; Urine specific gravity (< 1.005) and low urine osmolality (< 200 mOsm/kg); Water deprivation test; Desmopressin challenge test; Pituitary MRI.

differentials.mimic: Chronic Laxative Abuse / Factitious Diarrhea (F68.10 / T47.2X1A)
differentials.overlap: Uncontrolled fecal incontinence, watery diarrhea, weight loss.
differentials.physical_signs: Dehydration, muscle weakness, hypokalemia, melanosis coli on endoscopy.
differentials.workup: Urine and stool laxative screening (phenolphthalein, bisacodyl, anthraquinones); Serum electrolytes (hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis); Colonoscopy (melanosis coli).

differentials.overlap: New-onset urinary urgency and urge incontinence in an older adult.
differentials.physical_signs: Magnetic gait ataxia (feet glued to floor), cognitive slowing (Hakim-Adams triad).
differentials.workup: Brain CT/MRI (ventriculomegaly out of proportion to sulcal enlargement); High-volume CSF tap test.

red_flags: Urine specific gravity persistently < 1.005 despite water restriction (Diabetes Insipidus).
Hypokalemia with melanosis coli on endoscopy (surreptitious laxative abuse).
Urinary incontinence accompanied by magnetic gait ataxia in an older adult (NPH).

name: Insomnia Disorder
symptoms: A predominant complaint of dissatisfaction with sleep quantity or quality, associated with difficulty initiating sleep, difficulty maintaining sleep, or early-morning awakening with inability to return to sleep, occurring at least 3 nights per week for at least 3 months, despite adequate opportunity for sleep.

differentials.overlap: Severe sleep-onset and sleep-maintenance insomnia, daytime restlessness, racing thoughts.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting sinus tachycardia (> 90-100 bpm), fine hand tremor, warm moist skin, heat intolerance, weight loss, lid lag, goiter.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (suppressed < 0.01-0.4 mIU/L); Free T4 and Free T3; Thyroid antibody panel.

differentials.overlap: Severe sleep-onset insomnia, pacing floors at night, daytime fatigue.
differentials.physical_signs: Uncomfortable crawling/creeping urge to move legs, occurring exclusively at rest/in bed, temporarily relieved by movement; normal physical exam.
differentials.workup: Serum Ferritin and iron panel (ferritin < 50-75 ng/mL warrants iron therapy); Rule out peripheral neuropathy.

differentials.mimic: Congestive Heart Failure / Paroxysmal Nocturnal Dyspnea (I50.9)
differentials.overlap: Frequent middle-of-the-night awakenings, inability to sleep lying flat, daytime fatigue.
differentials.physical_signs: Orthopnea (requiring multiple pillows to sleep), paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, bilateral pitting ankle edema, elevated JVP, bilateral basilar crackles.
differentials.workup: Serum BNP / NT-proBNP; Transthoracic Echocardiogram; Chest X-ray.

differentials.overlap: Frequent nighttime awakenings, sleep fragmentation, poor sleep quality.
differentials.physical_signs: Sour taste in mouth upon waking, chronic morning hoarseness, nocturnal cough, retrosternal pyrosis.
differentials.workup: 24-hour ambulatory esophageal pH/impedance monitoring; Upper endoscopy (EGD).

red_flags: Resting tachycardia > 100 bpm, heat intolerance, and fine tremor (hyperthyroidism).
Need to sleep on multiple pillows or waking gasping for breath relieved by sitting up (orthopnea / heart failure).
Urge to move legs that worsens in bed and improves with walking (RLS).
Suppressed TSH on routine laboratory screening.

name: Hypersomnolence Disorder
symptoms: Self-reported excessive sleepiness (hypersomnolence) despite a main sleep period lasting at least 7 hours, with >= 1 of: recurrent periods of sleep within the same day, a prolonged main sleep episode of > 9 hours that is non-restorative, or difficulty being fully awake after abrupt awakening (sleep drunkenness), occurring >= 3 times per week for >= 3 months.

differentials.overlap: Excessive daytime sleepiness, prolonged unrefreshing sleep, fatigue, psychomotor slowing.
differentials.physical_signs: Delayed reflex relaxation (Woltman sign), cold intolerance, weight gain, periorbital edema, dry coarse skin, bradycardia.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (> 4.5 mIU/L); Free T4 (< 0.8 ng/dL); Anti-TPO antibodies.

differentials.overlap: Profound daytime sleepiness, falling asleep while driving, prolonged unrefreshing sleep.
differentials.physical_signs: Elevated BMI, neck circumference > 17 inches, crowded airway (Mallampati IV), habitual snoring, morning dry mouth.
differentials.workup: In-lab Diagnostic Polysomnography (AHI >= 15-30 events/hr confirms moderate/severe OSA).

differentials.overlap: Profound daytime somnolence, exhaustion, inability to stay awake.
differentials.physical_signs: Marked conjunctival pallor, tachycardia, postural dizziness, lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly.
differentials.workup: Complete Blood Count (Hgb < 8-9 g/dL); Peripheral blood smear; Iron panel; B12/Folate.

differentials.mimic: Chronic Epstein-Barr Virus / Cytomegalovirus / Lyme (B27.00 / A69.20)
differentials.overlap: Disabling hypersomnolence, post-viral fatigue syndrome, 'brain fog', body aches.
differentials.physical_signs: Posterior cervical lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, low-grade fevers.
differentials.workup: EBV VCA-IgM/IgG, EBNA; CMV serology; Lyme two-tier serology.

red_flags: Severe habitual snoring with witnessed apneas and gasping during sleep (OSA).
Delayed deep tendon reflex relaxation with cold intolerance (hypothyroidism).
Severe pallor and tachycardia (hemoglobin < 8 g/dL).
Hepatosplenomegaly or firm lymphadenopathy.

name: Narcolepsy (Type 1 & Type 2)
icd10: G47.411 (Type 1 with Cataplexy), G47.419 (Type 2 without Cataplexy)
symptoms: Recurrent periods of an irrepressible need to sleep, lapsing into sleep, or napping occurring within the same day, occurring >= 3 times per week over >= 3 months, accompanied by at least one of: (1) Cataplexy episodes, (2) Hypocretin deficiency in CSF, or (3) Nocturnal sleep polysomnography showing REM latency <= 15 min or MSLT showing mean sleep latency <= 8 min and >= 2 SOREMPs.

differentials.overlap: Sudden loss of muscle tone causing falls to the ground.
differentials.physical_signs: Loss of consciousness occurs during drop attack, postictal confusion, lack of emotional trigger (cataplexy is triggered specifically by laughter/jokes and preserves full consciousness); EEG abnormalities.
differentials.workup: Routine / Continuous Video-EEG monitoring (epileptiform generalized discharges vs normal awake background during cataplexy).

differentials.overlap: Gelastic cataplexy (sudden loss of muscle tone triggered by laughter), cognitive decline, psychosis.
differentials.physical_signs: Vertical Supranuclear Gaze Palsy (pathognomonic early inability to look downward voluntarily), cerebellar ataxia, hepatosplenomegaly.
differentials.workup: Ophthalmologic assessment of vertical saccades; Plasma oxysterols; NPC1/NPC2 gene testing.

differentials.overlap: Severe daytime sleepiness, falling asleep in strange locations, dream-like hallucinations.
differentials.physical_signs: Episodic course (sleeping 18-22 hrs/day for weeks) with complete normalcy between episodes; megaphagia, hypersexuality.
differentials.workup: Clinical history; Overnight PSG and MSLT.

differentials.overlap: Abrupt onset of severe daytime sleep attacks, cataplexy-like drop episodes.
differentials.physical_signs: Headaches, bitemporal visual field cuts, endocrine deficiencies (diabetes insipidus, galactorrhea).
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with contrast (lesions in posterior hypothalamus or bilateral paramedian thalami); CSF hypocretin-1 (orexin-A) level (undetectable or <= 110 pg/mL).

red_flags: Inability to voluntarily look downward (Vertical Supranuclear Gaze Palsy in Niemann-Pick C).
Drop attacks accompanied by loss of consciousness or postictal confusion (epileptic drop attacks).
Bitemporal hemianopia or diabetes insipidus accompanying new sleepiness (hypothalamic mass).
Cataplexy (bilateral knee buckling or jaw drooping triggered specifically by laughter with preserved awareness).

name: Obstructive Sleep Apnea Hypopnea
symptoms: Either: (1) Evidence by polysomnography of at least 5 obstructive apneas or hypopneas per hour of sleep accompanied by nocturnal breathing disturbances (snoring, snorting, gasping, breathing pauses) or daytime sleepiness/fatigue/unrefreshing sleep; OR (2) Evidence by polysomnography of 15 or more obstructive apneas/hypopneas per hour of sleep regardless of accompanying symptoms.

differentials.overlap: Severe nocturnal sleep disruption, paroxysmal arousals, daytime somnolence.
differentials.physical_signs: Crescendo-decrescendo pattern of tidal volume separated by central apneas (absence of respiratory effort); heart failure signs (elevated JVP, S3 gallop, peripheral edema).
differentials.workup: Diagnostic Polysomnography (demonstrating central apneas without ribcage/abdominal effort); Echocardiogram.

differentials.mimic: Severe Nasal Polyposis / Deviated Septum (J33.9 / J34.2)
differentials.overlap: Mouth breathing, noisy nocturnal breathing, poor sleep quality.
differentials.physical_signs: Bilateral glistening nasal polyps, completely obstructed nasal passages; absence of pharyngeal collapse.
differentials.workup: Anterior rhinoscopy / nasal endoscopy; Maxillofacial CT.

differentials.overlap: Severe OSA, loud snoring, daytime fatigue, macroglossia.
differentials.physical_signs: Acral enlargement (increasing shoe/ring size), coarse facial features, prognathism (jaw protrusion), prominent frontal bossing, carpal tunnel syndrome, spade-like hands.
differentials.workup: Serum IGF-1 (elevated); Oral glucose tolerance test with GH measurement (failure of GH to suppress < 1 mcg/L); Pituitary MRI.

differentials.overlap: Severe sleep apnea, loud snoring, profound daytime sleepiness, weight gain.
differentials.physical_signs: Macroglossia, periorbital edema, delayed reflexes, coarse skin, severe cold intolerance.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH and Free T4.

red_flags: Prognathism, enlarged hands/feet, and frontal bossing (Acromegaly as the driver of severe OSA).
Crescendo-decrescendo respiratory waxing and waning with central apneas (Cheyne-Stokes breathing / severe CHF).
Macroglossia and severe delayed deep tendon reflex relaxation (myxedema).

name: Central Sleep Apnea
symptoms: Evidence by polysomnography of 5 or more central apneas per hour of sleep (apneas characterized by cessation of airflow with *absent respiratory effort* across thoracic and abdominal belts), categorized into Cheyne-Stokes breathing, idiopathic CSA, or secondary to medication/substance.

differentials.overlap: Cheyne-Stokes breathing pattern during sleep, frequent arousals, severe daytime fatigue.
differentials.physical_signs: Third heart sound (S3 gallop), elevated jugular venous distension (> 8 cm H2O), hepatojugular reflux, bibasilar pulmonary crackles, pitting pretibial edema.
differentials.workup: Diagnostic Polysomnography; Serum BNP (> 400 pg/mL); Transthoracic Echocardiogram (LVEF < 35-40%).

differentials.mimic: Chronic High-Dose Opioid Induced Central Apnea (T40.2X1A)
differentials.overlap: Central sleep apneas, severe daytime drowsiness, sleep fragmentation.
differentials.physical_signs: Miosis (constricted pinpoint pupils), taking chronic opioids (methadone, oxycodone, buprenorphine, fentanyl), bradypnea.
differentials.workup: Medication audit calculating daily Morphine Milligram Equivalents (MME); Urine drug screen; Polysomnography showing Ataxic (Biot's) respiration or high central apnea index.

differentials.overlap: New-onset central sleep apnea, failure of automatic respiration (Ondine's curse).
differentials.physical_signs: Cranial nerve palsies (IX, X, XII), dysphagia, dysarthria, Horner syndrome, crossed sensory deficits (Wallenberg syndrome).
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with DWI (focusing on dorsal medulla and respiratory centers in brainstem).

red_flags: Pinpoint pupils and taking chronic high-dose opioid therapy (opioid-induced central respiratory depression).
Crescendo-decrescendo Cheyne-Stokes breathing in an edematous patient (severe heart failure).
New central apneas following stroke or accompanied by dysphagia and Horner's syndrome (brainstem stroke).

name: Sleep-Related Hypoventilation
symptoms: Polysomnography demonstrates episodes of decreased respiration associated with elevated arterial PaCO2 levels (PaCO2 > 55 mmHg for >= 10 minutes or an increase in PaCO2 >= 10 mmHg during sleep exceeding 50 mmHg), not primarily due to apneas.

differentials.overlap: Severe daytime hypersomnolence, morning carbon dioxide headaches, sluggishness.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe obesity (BMI >= 30, often > 40 kg/m2), plethora, cyanosis, somnolence, pedal edema, asterixis.
differentials.workup: Arterial Blood Gas (awake daytime PaCO2 > 45 mmHg); Serum bicarbonate (compensatory elevated HCO3 > 27 mEq/L); Polysomnography.

differentials.overlap: Nocturnal hypoventilation, frequent awakenings, morning headaches, orthopnea.
differentials.physical_signs: Paradoxical abdominal breathing when supine (abdomen sinks inward during inspiration), tongue fasciculations, mixed upper and lower motor neuron signs (atrophy + hyperreflexia).
differentials.workup: Upright and supine spirometry (FVC drop > 20% in supine position confirms diaphragmatic paralysis); EMG/NCS; Maximum Inspiratory Pressure (MIP / NIF).

differentials.mimic: Severe Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD 'Blue Bloater') (J44.9)
differentials.overlap: Nocturnal desaturation, morning headaches, daytime fatigue, confusion.
differentials.physical_signs: Barrel chest, wheezing, decreased breath sounds, pursed-lip breathing, peripheral cyanosis.
differentials.workup: Pulmonary Function Tests (FEV1/FVC < 0.70); Arterial Blood Gas; Chest CT.

red_flags: Paradoxical inward abdominal movement during inspiration while lying flat (diaphragmatic weakness / ALS).
Severe morning headaches and confusion with elevated serum bicarbonate > 28 mEq/L (chronic CO2 retention).
Awake daytime arterial PaCO2 > 45 mmHg in an obese patient (Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome).

name: Circadian Rhythm Sleep-Wake Disorders
symptoms: A persistent or recurrent pattern of sleep disruption that is primarily due to an alteration of the circadian system or to a misalignment between the endogenous circadian rhythm and the physical environment or social/work schedule (Delayed Sleep Phase, Advanced Sleep Phase, Irregular Sleep-Wake, Non-24-Hour, Shift Work).

differentials.mimic: Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Rhythm in Totally Blind Individuals (G47.24)
differentials.overlap: Progressive daily shifting of sleep onset by 1-2 hours, cyclical daytime somnolence and insomnia.
differentials.physical_signs: Complete lack of bilateral light perception (enucleation, optic nerve severing); absence of photic entrainment of the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN).
differentials.workup: Comprehensive ophthalmologic confirmation of zero light perception; Actigraphy for >= 14-28 days; Salivary Dim Light Melatonin Onset (DLMO) tracking.

differentials.mimic: Cushing's Syndrome (Loss of Diurnal Cortisol Rhythm) (E24.9)
differentials.overlap: Severe sleep-wake disruption, midnight wakefulness, daytime fatigue.
differentials.physical_signs: Moon facies, buffalo hump, purple striae, central obesity, proximal myopathy.
differentials.workup: Late-night salivary cortisol (loss of normal midnight nadir); 24-hour urinary free cortisol.

differentials.overlap: Daytime hypersomnia and profound nighttime alertness/wakefulness (day-night reversal).
differentials.physical_signs: Asterixis (flapping tremor on wrist dorsiflexion), fetor hepaticus, spider angiomas, palmar erythema, jaundice.
differentials.workup: Blood ammonia (elevated on ice); Liver panel (elevated bilirubin, prolonged INR, low albumin); Abdominal ultrasound.

red_flags: Day-night sleep reversal accompanied by asterixis (flapping tremor) and liver stigmata (hepatic encephalopathy).
Complete bilateral blindness with cyclically drifting sleep times (Non-24 in blind individuals).
Loss of normal midnight cortisol nadir with cushingoid physical features.

name: NREM Sleep Arousal Disorders (Sleepwalking & Sleep Terrors)
symptoms: Recurrent episodes of incomplete awakening from sleep, usually occurring during the first third of the major sleep episode (N3 slow-wave sleep), accompanied by either: (1) Sleepwalking (rising from bed and walking about with blank stare, unresponsive, difficult to wake), or (2) Sleep Terrors (abrupt terror awakenings beginning with a panicky scream, intense autonomic arousal, unresponsiveness to comforting), with partial/complete amnesia for the episode.

differentials.overlap: Abrupt nighttime awakenings in terror, motor thrashing, screaming, wandering.
differentials.physical_signs: Bizarre stereotypic movements (bicycling legs, pelvic thrusting), brief duration (< 30-60 seconds, unlike parasomnias which last 5-15 min), multiple episodes per night (often 5-10x), occurring at any time of night.
differentials.workup: Continuous synchronous Video-Polysomnography with 32-channel EEG; 3T Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Complex, bizarre sleepwalking, sleep-eating, sleep-driving with complete morning amnesia.
differentials.physical_signs: Taking zolpidem, eszopiclone, or zaleplon; behaviors emerge within hours of dose ingestion.
differentials.workup: Medication audit; Immediate discontinuation of Z-drugs.

differentials.overlap: Night terrors or sleepwalking triggered by respiratory arousals from deep slow-wave sleep.
differentials.physical_signs: Snoring, witnessed apneas, gasping awakenings that precipitate the confusional arousal.
differentials.workup: In-lab Polysomnography (assessing if arousals follow obstructive hypopneas).

red_flags: Stereotyped brief motor behaviors (< 60 sec) with bicycling leg movements occurring multiple times nightly (frontal epilepsy).
Complex dangerous sleep-driving or cooking after taking zolpidem.
Parasomnias emerging de novo in middle-aged or older adults.

name: Nightmare Disorder
symptoms: Repeated occurrences of extended, extremely dysphoric, and well-remembered dreams that usually involve efforts to avoid threats to survival, security, or physical integrity, occurring during the second half of the major sleep episode (REM sleep), where upon awakening, the individual rapidly becomes oriented and alert.

differentials.overlap: Terrifying, vivid, cinematic nightmares waking the patient nightly.
differentials.physical_signs: Taking lipophilic beta-blockers (which cross the blood-brain barrier); resting sinus bradycardia (HR < 50-60 bpm).
differentials.workup: Medication audit; Trial of switching to hydrophilic beta-blocker (atenolol) or alternative class.

differentials.mimic: REM Sleep Rebound Nightmare Syndrome (F10.239 / F13.239)
differentials.overlap: Severe nightly nightmares, vivid dream enactment following drug cessation.
differentials.physical_signs: Recent abrupt withdrawal from REM-suppressing substances (alcohol, benzodiazepines, SSRIs, barbiturates).
differentials.workup: Substance discontinuation timeline; Polysomnography showing marked increase in REM sleep percentage (> 30-35%).

differentials.mimic: Early Lewy Body Dementia / Parkinson's Nightmares (G31.83 / G20)
differentials.overlap: Terrifying dreams of being attacked, insects, snakes, or intruders, waking in fear.
differentials.physical_signs: Visual hallucinations, mild asymmetric parkinsonism, anosmia, dream enactment.
differentials.workup: DaT-SPECT scan; Neurological examination; Polysomnography.

red_flags: Cinematic nightmares emerging following the initiation of propranolol or metoprolol.
Violent physical dream enactment accompanied by waking nightmares (REM Sleep Behavior Disorder).
Nightmares with resting bradycardia < 50 bpm.

name: REM Sleep Behavior Disorder (RBD)
symptoms: Repeated episodes of arousal during sleep associated with vocalization and/or complex motor behaviors (punching, flailing, kicking, leaping from bed to fight attackers) reflecting dream enactment during REM sleep, confirmed by polysomnographic recording demonstrating *REM sleep without atonia* (loss of normal muscle paralysis).

differentials.mimic: Prodromal Alpha-Synucleinopathy (Parkinson's / DLB / MSA) (G20 / G31.83 / G23.8)
differentials.overlap: Violent dream enactment behaviors; over 80-90% of idiopathic RBD patients convert to Parkinson's, Dementia with Lewy Bodies, or Multiple System Atrophy within 10-15 years.
differentials.physical_signs: Subtle signs: loss of smell (anosmia), chronic constipation, subtle resting hand tremor, reduced arm swing, orthostatic hypotension, subtle cogwheel rigidity.
differentials.workup: Polysomnography with extended limb EMG channels (confirming REM sleep without atonia); University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT); DaT-SPECT scan; Orthostatic vitals.

differentials.overlap: Dream enactment, kicking, punching during sleep following SSRI, SNRI, or TCA therapy.
differentials.physical_signs: Chronologically linked to initiation or dose escalation of venlafaxine, sertraline, or mirtazapine in younger individuals.
differentials.workup: Medication audit; Polysomnography; Trial of dose reduction or switch to bupropion (which does not exacerbate RWA).

differentials.overlap: Nocturnal thrashing, flailing, vocalizations, violent movements.
differentials.physical_signs: Occurs in NREM sleep (not REM), stereotypic motor pattern, brief duration (< 60 sec), preserved REM atonia on PSG.
differentials.workup: Continuous Video-PSG with full 32-channel EEG montage.

red_flags: Dream enactment behavior in an adult > 50 years old (requires neurological evaluation for prodromal Parkinson's / Lewy body disease).
Anosmia (loss of smell) and chronic constipation accompanying nocturnal dream enactment.
Physical bed-partner injury from violent punches, kicks, or jumping out of bed during nightmares.

name: Restless Legs Syndrome (Willis-Ekbom Disease)
symptoms: An urge to move the legs, usually accompanied by or in response to uncomfortable and unpleasant sensations in the legs, characterized by all of: (1) Begins or worsens during periods of rest or inactivity, (2) Partially or totally relieved by movement (walking, stretching), (3) Exclusively occurs or is worse in the evening or night, occurring >= 3 times/week for >= 3 months.

differentials.mimic: Severe Iron Deficiency without Anemia (D50.9 / E61.1)
differentials.overlap: Severe uncomfortable crawling sensations in legs at night, motor urge to move.
differentials.physical_signs: Normal hemoglobin on CBC, but central brain iron stores are depleted (brain iron deficiency impairs striatal dopamine transport).
differentials.workup: Fasting Serum Ferritin (ferritin < 50-75 ng/mL is a major trigger for RLS and demands oral or IV iron replacement); Serum Iron and TIBC (transferrin saturation < 20%).

differentials.overlap: Burning, tingling, crawling sensations in feet and lower legs at night.
differentials.physical_signs: Symptoms are painful (burning dysesthesias) rather than a motor urge; sensations do *not* resolve with movement and are often worsened by walking; loss of pinprick/temperature on exam.
differentials.workup: EMG / Nerve Conduction Studies; Skin punch biopsy for Intraepidermal Nerve Fiber Density (IENFD).

differentials.overlap: Heavy, aching, uncomfortable legs in the evening, restless movement of legs.
differentials.physical_signs: Bilateral lower extremity pitting edema, varicose veins, stasis dermatitis, hyperpigmentation around ankles; relieved by leg elevation (RLS is not relieved by elevation alone).
differentials.workup: Lower extremity venous duplex ultrasound.

differentials.overlap: Severe restlessness, inability to keep legs still, pacing.
differentials.physical_signs: Inner generalized subjective restlessness involving the whole body, not localized to calves/legs; lack of circadian evening worsening; occurs after starting dopamine antagonists or SSRIs.
differentials.workup: Barnes Akathisia Rating Scale (BARS); Medication audit.

red_flags: Serum ferritin < 50 ng/mL in any patient presenting with restless legs (oral/IV iron replacement is first-line).
Symptoms fail to improve with movement and feature burning numbness (indicates small fiber neuropathy).
Bilateral ankle edema and stasis dermatitis relieved by leg elevation (venous insufficiency).

name: Substance/Medication-Induced Sleep Disorder
symptoms: A prominent and severe disturbance in sleep (insomnia, daytime sleepiness, parasomnia, or mixed) developing during or soon after substance intoxication or withdrawal or after exposure to a medication.

differentials.mimic: Alcohol-Induced Sleep Fragmentation & REM Suppression (F10.182 / F10.282)
differentials.overlap: Using alcohol as a sleep aid, followed by middle-of-the-night awakenings, sweating, vivid dreams.
differentials.physical_signs: Alcohol shortens sleep latency but severely disrupts second-half sleep architecture (REM rebound, sympathetic arousal, tachycardia).
differentials.workup: Alcohol consumption timeline; Blood alcohol concentration; Polysomnography.

differentials.overlap: Profound insomnia, vivid nightmares, early morning awakenings.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting bradycardia, hypotension, rebound severe hypertension if centrally acting alpha-2 agonists (clonidine) are missed.
differentials.workup: Medication audit; Blood pressure monitoring; Resting ECG.

differentials.overlap: Difficulty falling asleep, restless sleep, light unrefreshing sleep.
differentials.physical_signs: Taking caffeinated beverages, energy drinks, or pre-workout supplements in afternoon/evening; slow caffeine metabolizers (CYP1A2 polymorphisms).
differentials.workup: Dietary caffeine audit; 2-week caffeine elimination trial.

red_flags: Rebound severe hypertension and panic upon missing evening clonidine doses.
Consuming alcohol nightly for sleep leading to 3:00 AM awakenings with diaphoresis and tremors.
Afternoon intake of pre-workout powders containing unlisted stimulant analogues.

name: Unspecified Sleep-Wake Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a sleep-wake disorder predominate but there is insufficient information to make a specific diagnosis.

differentials.overlap: Bizarre nocturnal behaviors, stridor during sleep, severe insomnia, sleep-disordered breathing, gait ataxia.
differentials.physical_signs: Prominent nocturnal inspiratory vocal cord stridor, chorea, supranuclear gaze palsy, bulbar dysfunction.
differentials.workup: Serum and CSF Anti-IgLON5 antibodies; Overnight Polysomnography (profound destruction of NREM and REM sleep architecture); HLA-DRB1*10:01 typing.

differentials.overlap: Total intractable progressive insomnia, loss of circadian rhythm, panic, hallucinations.
differentials.physical_signs: Autonomic storm (hyperhidrosis, pyrexia, tachycardia, hypertension), dysarthria, myoclonus, ataxia, rapid fatal progression over 7-18 months.
differentials.workup: PRNP gene sequencing (D178N mutation with 129M polymorphism); Polysomnography (total loss of sleep spindles and slow-wave sleep); FDG-PET (severe thalamic hypometabolism).

differentials.overlap: Waking repeatedly at 3:00-4:00 AM with chest tightness, cough, anxiety.
differentials.physical_signs: Expiratory wheezing, prolonged expiratory phase, nocturnal cough.
differentials.workup: Overnight peak expiratory flow (PEF) monitoring (demonstrating diurnal variation > 20%); Spirometry.

red_flags: Prominent inspiratory stridor during sleep with progressive gait ataxia and bulbar palsy (Anti-IgLON5 disease).
Total unremitting loss of ability to sleep with autonomic hyperactivity and myoclonus (Fatal Familial Insomnia).
Diurnal variation in peak expiratory flow > 20% (nocturnal asthma).

name: Delayed Ejaculation
symptoms: Marked delay in ejaculation or marked infrequency or absence of ejaculation on almost all or all occasions of partnered sexual activity, persisting for >= 6 months, causing significant distress.

differentials.mimic: SSRI / SNRI-Induced Anorgasmia and Delayed Ejaculation (T43.205A)
differentials.overlap: Inability to achieve ejaculation or orgasm during partnered sex or masturbation.
differentials.physical_signs: Chronologically linked to initiation of sertraline, paroxetine, escitalopram, fluoxetine, or venlafaxine; normal physical exam.
differentials.workup: Medication audit; Trial of dose reduction, adjunctive bupropion, or switch to non-serotonergic agent.

differentials.overlap: Delayed ejaculation, retrograde ejaculation (semen directed into bladder), erectile dysfunction.
differentials.physical_signs: Decreased sensation in feet (stocking-glove neuropathy), loss of ankle reflexes, orthostatic hypotension.
differentials.workup: Post-ejaculatory urinalysis (demonstrating abundant spermatozoa in urine confirms retrograde ejaculation); HbA1c.

differentials.overlap: Loss of ejaculatory drive, delayed climax, decreased sexual desire.
differentials.physical_signs: Testicular atrophy, gynecomastia, loss of facial hair, galactorrhea.
differentials.workup: Serum total and free testosterone (8:00 AM); Serum prolactin; LH / FSH.

red_flags: Presence of spermatozoa in urine following sexual climax (confirms retrograde ejaculation from autonomic neuropathy or prostate surgery).
Severe delayed ejaculation emerging after starting serotonergic antidepressants.
Bilateral testicular atrophy and gynecomastia (hypogonadism / prolactinoma).

name: Erectile Disorder
symptoms: Marked difficulty in obtaining an erection during sexual activity, marked difficulty in maintaining an erection until completion, or marked decrease in erectile rigidity, occurring on almost all occasions of sexual activity for >= 6 months.

differentials.mimic: Atherosclerotic Vascular Disease / Pelvic Arterial Insufficiency (I70.209)
differentials.overlap: Progressive inability to obtain or maintain erectile rigidity; ED is an early herald of occult systemic CAD.
differentials.physical_signs: Diminished femoral/pedal pulses, femoral bruits, buttock claudication (Leriche syndrome), hypertension, metabolic syndrome.
differentials.workup: Penile Doppler Ultrasound with intracavernosal prostaglandin injection (peak systolic velocity < 30 cm/s confirms arteriogenic ED); Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI); Fasting lipid panel; Coronary calcium scan.

differentials.overlap: Decreased morning erections, reduced libido, fatigue, erectile failure.
differentials.physical_signs: Small, soft testes (< 15-20 mL), gynecomastia, loss of body hair, decreased muscle mass.
differentials.workup: Morning total testosterone (< 300 ng/dL on 2 separate 8:00 AM draws); Free testosterone; LH / FSH (differentiating primary vs secondary hypogonadism).

differentials.overlap: Acute or subacute loss of erectile function, numbness during intercourse.
differentials.physical_signs: Saddle anesthesia (numbness over perineum, buttocks, inner thighs), reduced anal sphincter tone, urinary retention, bilateral sciatica.
differentials.workup: Urgent Lumbosacral Spine MRI; Neurological examination.

differentials.overlap: Erectile failure starting after initiation of blood pressure medications.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting bradycardia, normal nocturnal penile tumescence.
differentials.workup: Medication audit; Trial of ARB (e.g., losartan, which has neutral/pro-erectile profile).

red_flags: Saddle anesthesia, urinary retention, and loss of anal sphincter tone (Cauda Equina emergency).
Bilateral buttock claudication, absent femoral pulses, and ED (Leriche aortic bifurcation syndrome).
Morning total testosterone < 200 ng/dL on repeat morning testing.

name: Female Orgasmic Disorder
