symptoms: Marked delay in, marked infrequency of, or absence of orgasm, or markedly reduced intensity of orgasmic sensations on almost all occasions of sexual activity, persisting for >= 6 months, causing significant distress.

differentials.overlap: Sudden total loss of ability to achieve orgasm or severe delay in reaching climax.
differentials.physical_signs: Normal sexual arousal and lubrication present, but orgasmic plateau cannot be breached; begins within days of starting serotonergic medication.
differentials.workup: Pharmacotherapy audit; Dose reduction, weekend drug holidays, or switch to bupropion/vilazodone.

differentials.mimic: Pudendal Nerve Neuropathy / Sacral Nerve Injury (G57.80)
differentials.overlap: Loss of orgasmic sensation, genital numbness, burning vulvar pain.
differentials.physical_signs: Loss of sensation to light touch and pinprick over clitoris and labia minora, unilateral or bilateral; history of difficult vaginal delivery or pelvic surgery.
differentials.workup: Pudendal nerve terminal motor latency (PNTML); Pelvic MRI; Quantitative sensory testing.

differentials.overlap: Decreased orgasmic sensitivity, dryness, painful intercourse.
differentials.physical_signs: Pale, thin, dry vaginal mucosa, loss of vaginal rugae, clitoral atrophy, introital stenosis.
differentials.workup: Serum estradiol; Vaginal maturation index; Trial of local vaginal estrogen cream.

red_flags: Complete numbness of the clitoris and labia following pelvic surgery or childbirth (pudendal nerve injury).
Sudden emergence of complete anorgasmia following SSRI initiation.
Severe vulvovaginal atrophy with mucosal petechiae on speculum examination.

name: Female Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder
symptoms: Lack of, or significantly reduced, sexual interest/arousal, manifested by >= 3 of: absent/reduced interest in sexual activity, absent/reduced erotic thoughts/fantasies, absent/reduced initiation of sexual activity, absent/reduced excitement/pleasure during sex, absent/reduced sexual interest in response to erotic cues, absent/reduced genital or non-genital sensations, lasting >= 6 months.

differentials.overlap: Total extinction of sexual desire, absent lubrication, amenorrhea, depression.
differentials.physical_signs: Galactorrhea (milky discharge on nipple expression), bitemporal visual field deficits, headaches.
differentials.workup: Fasting morning serum prolactin (> 25 ng/mL; prolactinoma often > 100-200); Pituitary MRI with contrast.

differentials.overlap: Profound loss of libido, fatigue, weight gain, low mood, poor lubrication.
differentials.physical_signs: Delayed reflex relaxation, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, cold intolerance, goiter.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (> 4.5 mIU/L); Free T4 (< 0.8 ng/dL); Anti-TPO antibodies.

differentials.overlap: Avoidance of sexual activity, lack of lubrication, severe dyspareunia.
differentials.physical_signs: Vaginal pallor, friability, loss of rugae, petechiae, introital narrowing.
differentials.workup: Vaginal pH (> 5.0 indicates hypoestrogenism); Clinical pelvic examination.

differentials.overlap: Dramatic collapse in libido, blunted erotic desire following surgical removal of ovaries.
differentials.physical_signs: Surgical scars from bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy; loss of pubic/axillary hair.
differentials.workup: Serum total and free testosterone; DHEA-S (markedly subnormal).

red_flags: Bilateral spontaneous galactorrhea and headaches (demands prolactin level and pituitary MRI).
Complete collapse of sexual desire immediately following bilateral oophorectomy (androgen deficiency).
Vaginal pH > 5.0 with severe mucosal pallor and introital narrowing (GSM).

name: Genito-Pelvic Pain/Penetration Disorder
symptoms: Persistent or recurrent difficulties with >= 1 of: vaginal penetration during intercourse, marked vulvovaginal or pelvic pain during vaginal intercourse or penetration attempts, marked fear or anxiety about vulvovaginal or pelvic pain in anticipation of/during penetration, or marked tensing/tightening of the pelvic floor muscles during penetration attempts, lasting >= 6 months.

differentials.overlap: Severe burning, stinging, or knife-like pain at the vaginal entrance upon attempted penetration.
differentials.physical_signs: Positive Cotton-Swab (Q-tip) Test: severe localized sharp pain elicited by gentle touch at 4:00 to 8:00 positions of the vestibular mucosa; erythema.
differentials.workup: Cotton-swab vestibular mapping; Rule out active candida, trichomonas, herpes simplex, and human papillomavirus.

differentials.overlap: Inability to tolerate penetration, intense dyspareunia, introital burning.
differentials.physical_signs: Porcelain-white atrophic plaques in a 'figure-of-eight' distribution around vulva and perianal region; resorption of labia minora; buried clitoral hood (phimosis); fissuring.
differentials.workup: Vulvar punch biopsy (epidermal atrophy, hyperkeratosis, dermal band of hyalinization); High-potency topical corticosteroid therapy.

differentials.overlap: Deep pelvic dyspareunia (pain on deep thrusting), chronic pelvic pain, dread of sex.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe dysmenorrhea, dyschezia (pain with defecation), palpable tender nodules on uterosacral ligaments or rectovaginal septum.
differentials.workup: Transvaginal Ultrasound with bowel prep; Pelvic MRI; Diagnostic laparoscopy.

differentials.mimic: Hypertonic Pelvic Floor Muscle Dysfunction (Levator Ani Spasm) (M62.838)
differentials.overlap: Involuntary vaginal muscle spasm preventing penetration, severe pain.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe tenderness to palpation of puborectalis, iliococcygeus, and obturator internus muscles on gentle single-digit internal pelvic exam.
differentials.workup: Pelvic floor physical therapy assessment; Biofeedback manometry.

red_flags: Porcelain-white atrophic vulvar plaques with architectural resorption (Lichen Sclerosus, requires biopsy to rule out squamous cell carcinoma).
Severe pain localized specifically to gentle Q-tip touch at the vestibular glands (Vestibulodynia).
Pain on deep thrusting accompanied by severe dysmenorrhea and pain with bowel movements (deep endometriosis).

name: Male Hypoactive Sexual Desire Disorder
symptoms: Persistently or recurrently deficient (or absent) sexual or erotic thoughts or fantasies and desire for sexual activity, taking into account factors that affect sexual functioning such as age and sociocultural context, persisting for >= 6 months, causing clinically significant distress.

differentials.overlap: Complete absence of sexual desire, loss of spontaneous morning erections, chronic fatigue.
differentials.physical_signs: Testicular volume < 15-20 mL, gynecomastia, loss of facial/body hair, visceral obesity.
differentials.workup: Morning serum total testosterone (< 300 ng/dL on 2 separate 8 AM draws); Free testosterone; Serum LH and FSH (elevated in primary testicular failure; low/normal in pituitary/hypothalamic failure).

differentials.overlap: Total suppression of libido, erectile failure, severe anhedonia.
differentials.physical_signs: Galactorrhea (rare in men but diagnostic), bitemporal visual field cuts (macroadenoma), gynecomastia.
differentials.workup: Fasting serum prolactin (> 20 ng/mL; macroadenoma typically > 100-200 ng/mL); Pituitary MRI with contrast.

differentials.overlap: Loss of libido, sluggish cognition, psychomotor slowing, chronic exhaustion.
differentials.physical_signs: Delayed reflex relaxation, periorbital puffiness, cold intolerance, bradycardia, dry skin.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (> 4.5 mIU/L); Free T4 (< 0.8 ng/dL).

differentials.overlap: Total loss of sexual desire, daytime exhaustion, morning headaches, low testosterone.
differentials.physical_signs: BMI > 30, neck circumference > 17 inches, loud snoring, witnessed apneas.
differentials.workup: Polysomnography (AHI >= 15-30 events/hr); Morning testosterone.

red_flags: Morning total testosterone < 200 ng/dL with loss of morning erections.
Bitemporal hemianopia or galactorrhea in a man with absent libido (pituitary macroadenoma).
Delayed deep tendon reflex relaxation and cold intolerance (hypothyroidism).

name: Premature (Early) Ejaculation
symptoms: A persistent or recurrent pattern of ejaculation occurring during partnered sexual activity within approximately 1 minute following vaginal penetration and before the individual wishes it, occurring on almost all occasions for >= 6 months, causing significant distress.

differentials.overlap: Sudden onset of premature ejaculation in a man with previously normal latency.
differentials.physical_signs: Perineal, penile, or suprapubic aching, dysuria, pain with ejaculation, tender boggy prostate on digital rectal exam.
differentials.workup: Meares-Stamey four-glass test or two-glass pre- and post-massage test (urine culture and expressed prostatic secretion microscopy demonstrating leukocytosis > 10 WBC/HPF); Transrectal ultrasound.

differentials.overlap: Acquired severe premature ejaculation, psychomotor restlessness, palpitations.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting sinus tachycardia, fine hand tremor, warm moist skin, hyperreflexia, weight loss.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (suppressed < 0.01 mIU/L); Free T4 and Free T3 (elevated).

differentials.overlap: Extreme penile hypersensitivity leading to instantaneous ejaculation on minimal touch.
differentials.physical_signs: Hyperesthesia over glans penis, hyperactive bulbocavernosus reflex.
differentials.workup: Biothesiometry (measuring penile sensory threshold); Pudendal nerve latency.

red_flags: Pain during or immediately following ejaculation with tender prostate on exam (prostatitis).
Suppressed TSH with fine resting hand tremor and tachycardia (hyperthyroidism).
Sudden acquisition of premature ejaculation in an adult with prior lifelong normal ejaculatory latency.

name: Substance/Medication-Induced Sexual Dysfunction
symptoms: A clinically significant disturbance in sexual function (desire, arousal, orgasm, erection) developing during or soon after substance intoxication or withdrawal or after exposure to a medication.

differentials.overlap: Delayed ejaculation, anorgasmia, erectile dysfunction, decreased libido in 40-70% of patients.
differentials.physical_signs: Normal pre-medication sexual function; starts within days/weeks of paroxetine, sertraline, citalopram, venlafaxine.
differentials.workup: Medication audit; Arizona Sexual Experiences Scale (ASEX); Trial of bupropion or phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors.

differentials.overlap: Persistent severe erectile dysfunction, loss of libido, penile numbness, anhedonia persisting months/years after drug cessation.
differentials.physical_signs: Loss of morning erections, reduced semen volume, penile flaccidity.
differentials.workup: Medication history confirming finasteride or dutasteride use for alopecia or BPH; Serum DHT (dihydrotestosterone) and total testosterone.

differentials.mimic: Chronic Alcohol / Opioid Induced Hypogonadism (F10.281 / F11.281)
differentials.overlap: Severe erectile failure, loss of libido, delayed ejaculation.
differentials.physical_signs: Gynecomastia, testicular atrophy, palmar erythema, miosis (pinpoint pupils on opioids).
differentials.workup: Morning serum total testosterone (markedly suppressed); Liver panel; Urine tox screen.

red_flags: Severe persistent sexual dysfunction following finasteride use.
Suppression of serum testosterone in a patient taking chronic prescription opioids (opioid-induced androgen deficiency).
Temporal correlation with starting an SSRI or SNRI antidepressant.

name: Other Specified & Unspecified Sexual Dysfunction
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a sexual dysfunction predominate but do not meet full criteria, including Persistent Genital Arousal Disorder (PGAD) (unwanted, intrusive, distressing sensations of genital arousal without conscious subjective sexual desire).

differentials.overlap: Persistent, relentless, painful genital arousal, clitoral/penile engorgement, restless legs, dyspareunia.
differentials.physical_signs: Deep sacral pain exacerbated by sitting, paresthesias in S2-S4 dermatomes, hyperesthesia of clitoris/perineum.
differentials.workup: High-resolution Sacral Spine MRI (visualizing fluid-filled cystic dilatations of sacral nerve root sleeves in S2-S4).

differentials.overlap: Pelvic fullness, genital throbbing, deep dyspareunia, post-coital aching.
differentials.physical_signs: Vulvar and perineal varicosities, lower extremity varicose veins, tenderness over ovarian points.
differentials.workup: Transvaginal color Doppler ultrasound; Pelvic venography demonstrating ovarian vein incompetence and dilated pelvic venous plexus (> 5-6 mm).

differentials.mimic: Paroxysmal Genital Arousal / Temporal Lobe Epilepsy (G40.209)
differentials.overlap: Sudden paroxysmal surges of intense genital tingling or involuntary orgasm-like sensations.
differentials.physical_signs: Brief stereotypic duration (< 60-90 seconds), aura, automatisms, postictal confusion.
differentials.workup: Video-EEG monitoring; Brain MRI.

red_flags: Sacral back pain exacerbated by sitting with persistent unprovoked genital arousal (Tarlov cyst on sacral MRI).
Paroxysmal brief genital sensations lasting < 90 seconds (focal epilepsy).
Visible vulvar or perineal varicose veins (pelvic congestion syndrome).

name: Gender Dysphoria in Children
symptoms: A marked incongruence between one's experienced/expressed gender and assigned gender, of at least 6 months' duration, manifested by >= 6 criteria (strong desire to be of the other gender, strong insistence that one is the other gender, strong preference for cross-gender roles, toys, playmates, and strong dislike of one's sexual anatomy).

differentials.mimic: Differences of Sex Development (DSD) / Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia (CAH) (E25.0)
differentials.overlap: Ambiguous genitalia, male gender identification in 46,XX individuals, virilization.
differentials.physical_signs: Clitoromegaly, labial fusion, hyperpigmentation, salt-wasting crises in infancy (hypotension, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia).
differentials.workup: Chromosomal Karyotyping (46,XX vs 46,XY); Serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone (markedly elevated in 21-hydroxylase deficiency); CYP21A2 gene sequencing; Pelvic ultrasound (presence of uterus/ovaries).

differentials.overlap: Female gender identity in a 46,XY individual with discordance discovered at puberty.
differentials.physical_signs: Phenotypically normal female external genitalia, blind-ending vagina, absent uterus and fallopian tubes, inguinal masses (undescended testes), primary amenorrhea.
differentials.workup: Karyotype (46,XY); Pelvic ultrasound (absent uterus); Serum testosterone in normal male range; AR gene mutation analysis.

differentials.overlap: High co-occurrence of gender diversity and rigid insistence on non-conforming gender expressions.
differentials.physical_signs: Presence of social communication deficits, restricted interests, sensory sensitivities.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive multidisciplinary evaluation; ADOS-2.

red_flags: Ambiguous genitalia or hypospadias in a child (demands immediate DSD workup and karyotype).
History of neonatal adrenal salt-wasting crises (hypotension, hyperkalemia in CAH).
Primary amenorrhea with inguinal masses in an adolescent female (Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome).

name: Gender Dysphoria in Adolescents and Adults
icd11: HA60 (Gender incongruence of adolescence and adulthood)
symptoms: A marked incongruence between one's experienced/expressed gender and assigned gender, of at least 6 months' duration, manifested by >= 2 criteria (marked incongruence with primary/secondary sex characteristics, strong desire to be rid of them, strong desire for sex characteristics of the other gender, strong conviction that one has typical feelings/reactions of the other gender), causing significant distress.

differentials.overlap: Atypical gender identity exploration, distress regarding male secondary sex characteristics, gynecomastia.
differentials.physical_signs: Tall stature with eunuchoid proportions (long legs), small firm testes (< 4 mL), gynecomastia, sparse facial/body hair, primary hypogonadism.
differentials.workup: Chromosomal Karyotype (47,XXY); Elevated LH and FSH with low total testosterone; Bone density scan (DEXA).

differentials.overlap: Distress over bodily development, delayed puberty, primary amenorrhea.
differentials.physical_signs: Short stature, webbed neck (cystic hygroma), low posterior hairline, shield chest with widely spaced nipples, bicuspid aortic valve / coarctation of aorta.
differentials.workup: Chromosomal Karyotype (45,X); Echocardiogram; Renal ultrasound; Pelvic ultrasound.

differentials.overlap: Sudden late-onset emergence of cross-gender desires, hypersexuality, paraphilias.
differentials.physical_signs: Seizures, visual field defects, endocrine abnormalities, headaches; absence of lifelong gender incongruence.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with and without gadolinium; EEG.

differentials.overlap: Intense disgust with genitalia, desire to surgically alter sex organs.
differentials.physical_signs: Preoccupation is centered on perceived 'ugliness', asymmetry, or defect of genitalia rather than incongruence with internal gender identity.
differentials.workup: BDD Diagnostic Interview; Structured clinical evaluation.

red_flags: Small firm testes (< 4 mL), gynecomastia, and tall eunuchoid proportions (Klinefelter 47,XXY).
Short stature, webbed neck, and cardiac murmur (Turner 45,X).
Sudden late-onset emergence of gender distress following a stroke, traumatic brain injury, or seizure disorder.

name: Other Specified & Unspecified Gender Dysphoria
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of gender dysphoria predominate but do not meet full criteria (e.g., transient or non-binary gender incongruence without distress; insufficient information).

differentials.overlap: Raised as female, then experiences sudden rapid virilization and male gender identity at puberty ('guevedoces').
differentials.physical_signs: Severe virilization at puberty (phallic enlargement, deepening of voice, muscular development), lack of breast development, descended testes.
differentials.workup: SRD5A2 gene sequencing; Serum testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (T/DHT) ratio (elevated > 20:1 after hCG stimulation).

differentials.overlap: Intense, agonizing intrusive thoughts questioning one's gender ('What if I am actually the other gender?').
differentials.physical_signs: Thoughts are ego-dystonic and cause intense panic/dread (not authentic desire); accompanied by hours of mental checking, analyzing childhood memories, and reassurance seeking.
differentials.workup: Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS); Structured OCD assessment.

differentials.overlap: Asymmetrical gonadal development, ambiguous physical features, gender exploration.
differentials.physical_signs: Ovotestis, asymmetrical genitalia, mixed secondary sexual characteristics.
differentials.workup: Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH) on multiple tissues (blood, skin fibroblasts, gonadal tissue).

red_flags: Severe virilization at puberty in a child raised female (5-alpha reductase 2 deficiency).
Intrusive obsessions about gender accompanied by compulsive reassurance seeking and panic (OCD).
Mixed gonadal histology on imaging.

name: Oppositional Defiant Disorder (ODD)
symptoms: A pattern of angry/irritable mood, argumentative/defiant behavior, or vindictiveness lasting at least 6 months, manifested by >= 4 symptoms across: (1) Angry/Irritable Mood (loses temper, touchy, angry/resentful), (2) Argumentative/Defiant Behavior (argues with authority, defies rules, deliberately annoys others, blames others), (3) Vindictiveness, exhibited with at least one individual who is not a sibling.

differentials.overlap: Defiant behavior, explosive anger, refusal to follow instructions, emotional lability.
differentials.physical_signs: Tonsillar/adenoidal hypertrophy, mouth breathing, loud snoring with gasps, nocturnal enuresis, morning grogginess.
differentials.workup: Pediatric Polysomnography (AHI >= 1 event/hr); ENT examination.

differentials.overlap: Ignoring teacher/parent commands, failure to follow rules, perceived as 'willful defiance'.
differentials.physical_signs: Child fails to respond when spoken to from behind or in noisy rooms, normal compliance when visual contact is made.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive Audiometric Evaluation; Pure-tone audiogram.

differentials.overlap: Aggression, defiance, impulsivity, irritability, academic failure.
differentials.physical_signs: Microcytic anemia, pallor, Burton line on gingival margins, pica history, living in pre-1978 home.
differentials.workup: Whole blood lead level (BLL >= 3.5 mcg/dL); Peripheral smear (basophilic stippling).

differentials.overlap: Sudden explosion of extreme oppositional defiance, rage outbursts, emotional lability.
differentials.physical_signs: Overnight onset, accompanying vocal/motor tics, handwriting deterioration, choreiform movements, post-strep infection.
differentials.workup: Throat culture; ASO / Anti-DNase B titers; Pediatric autoimmune panel.

red_flags: Severe tonsillar hypertrophy, loud snoring, and nocturnal gasping (OSA).
Failure to hear commands in noisy environments with normal compliance during face-to-face contact (hearing deficit).
Elevated blood lead level >= 3.5 mcg/dL.
Sudden overnight emergence of rage outbursts accompanied by tics (PANDAS/PANS).

name: Intermittent Explosive Disorder (IED)
symptoms: Recurrent behavioral outbursts representing a failure to control aggressive impulses, manifested by either: (1) Verbal aggression or physical aggression toward property, animals, or individuals occurring twice weekly for 3 months (not resulting in damage/injury), or (2) Three behavioral outbursts involving damage or destruction of property and/or physical assault involving injury within a 12-month period, where aggression is grossly out of proportion to provocation, impulsive, and causes distress.

differentials.mimic: Episodic Dyscontrol Syndrome / Temporal Lobe Epilepsy (G40.209)
differentials.overlap: Sudden, unprovoked violent rage outbursts, destructive behavior, screaming.
differentials.physical_signs: Aura preceding rage (epigastric rising, metallic taste), stereotyped automatisms, glassy unseeing stare during rage, complete amnesia or exhaustion/sleep immediately following outburst.
differentials.workup: Prolonged Video-EEG monitoring; High-resolution 3T Brain MRI (epilepsy protocol).

differentials.overlap: Explosive rage, disinhibition, violent outbursts, emotional volatility.
differentials.physical_signs: Anosmia (loss of smell), executive cognitive deficits, history of head trauma with loss of consciousness.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) demonstrating orbitofrontal / inferior frontal contusions.

differentials.overlap: Episodes of sudden, violent combative agitation, confusion, sweating, rage.
differentials.physical_signs: Whipple triad: diaphoresis, tachycardia, verified low glucose (< 55 mg/dL), prompt resolution with sugar.
differentials.workup: Supervised 72-hour fast; Fasting insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin; Continuous glucose monitor.

differentials.overlap: Unprovoked explosive physical aggression, violent assaults, grandiosity.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe cystic acne, gynecomastia, testicular atrophy, supraphysiologic musculature, hypertension.
differentials.workup: Serum testosterone (supraphysiologic); Suppressed LH/FSH (< 0.5 mIU/mL); Elevated hematocrit.

red_flags: Amnesia for the violent outburst accompanied by sudden sleepiness/snoring immediately after (epileptic rage).
Anosmia and history of frontal head injury (orbitofrontal encephalopathy).
Diaphoresis and tachycardia during rage that resolves completely within 10 minutes of drinking juice (hypoglycemia).
Cystic acne, gynecomastia, and testicular atrophy in a heavily muscled patient.

name: Conduct Disorder (Childhood & Adolescent Onset)
symptoms: A repetitive and persistent pattern of behavior in which the basic rights of others or major age-appropriate societal norms or rules are violated, manifested by >= 3 criteria in past 12 months across: (1) Aggression to people and animals (bullying, fighting, weapon use, physical cruelty, forced sexual activity), (2) Destruction of property (fire setting, vandalism), (3) Deceitfulness or theft, (4) Serious violations of rules (truancy, running away).

differentials.overlap: Antisocial behavior, stealing, lying, explosive violence, deteriorating school performance in adolescents.
differentials.physical_signs: Kayser-Fleischer rings on slit-lamp, wing-beating tremor, dystonia, dysarthria, hepatosplenomegaly.
differentials.workup: Slit-lamp exam; Serum ceruloplasmin (< 20 mg/dL); 24-hour urine copper (> 100 mcg/24h); Liver enzymes.

differentials.overlap: Severe aggression, behavioral deterioration, cruelty, defiance, academic collapse.
differentials.physical_signs: Prominent parkinsonian rigidity, bradykinesia, dystonia, seizures (unlike choreic adult form), family history of Huntington's.
differentials.workup: Targeted HTT gene genetic testing (CAG repeats >= 60 in juvenile form); Brain MRI (caudate atrophy).

differentials.overlap: Severe rule violations, lack of conscience, cruelty, inability to learn from punishment.
differentials.physical_signs: Smooth philtrum, thin upper lip, short palpebral fissures, microcephaly.
differentials.workup: 4-Digit Diagnostic Code; Brain MRI; Documented maternal alcohol exposure.

differentials.overlap: Sudden emergence of violent behavior, defiance, aggression, school failure in young boys.
differentials.physical_signs: Cutaneous hyperpigmentation (adrenal failure), gait ataxia, vision loss, hearing loss, rapid dementia.
differentials.workup: Plasma Very Long-Chain Fatty Acids (VLCFA: elevated C26:0); Brain MRI (parieto-occipital demyelination); ABCD1 sequencing.

red_flags: Kayser-Fleischer corneal rings, tremor, or elevated liver enzymes (Wilson's disease).
Rapid cognitive decline, visual loss, and ataxia following new-onset aggression in a boy (Adrenoleukodystrophy).
Prominent rigidity, bradykinesia, and seizures in an adolescent with behavioral decline (Juvenile Huntington's).
Classic facial dysmorphic features of prenatal alcohol exposure.

name: Antisocial Personality Disorder (Diagnostic Interface)
symptoms: A pervasive pattern of disregard for and violation of the rights of others occurring since age 15, indicated by >= 3 of: failure to conform to lawful behaviors, deceitfulness (lying, conning), impulsivity, irritability and aggressiveness (frequent fights/assaults), reckless disregard for safety, consistent irresponsibility, lack of remorse, in an individual at least 18 years old with evidence of Conduct Disorder before age 15.

differentials.overlap: Total lack of remorse, sociopathic rule-breaking, shoplifting, financial scamming, complete loss of empathy.
differentials.physical_signs: Onset in middle age (45-65) in an individual with *previously exemplary moral/ethical conduct*; primitive frontal release signs (grasp/snout), hyperorality.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (bilateral asymmetric frontal/anterior temporal atrophy); FDG-PET scan; Comprehensive neuropsychological testing.

differentials.mimic: Acquired Sociopathy (Ventromedial Prefrontal Brain Injury) (F07.0 / S06.9X9A)
differentials.overlap: Reckless disregard for safety, deceitfulness, impulsivity, callous lack of concern for others.
differentials.physical_signs: Anosmia, impaired decision-making on Iowa Gambling Task, documented history of orbitofrontal trauma or ruptured ACoA aneurysm.
differentials.workup: High-resolution Brain MRI (orbitofrontal/ventromedial prefrontal cortex destruction); Neuropsychological testing.

differentials.mimic: Bilateral Frontal Lobe Neoplasm (e.g., Butterfly Glioma / Meningioma) (C71.1 / D32.0)
differentials.overlap: Sudden emergence of criminal behavior, grand theft, aggression, disinhibition in a previously law-abiding adult.
differentials.physical_signs: Papilledema on fundoscopy, frontal release signs, urinary incontinence, apathy alternating with euphoria.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with and without gadolinium.

red_flags: De novo antisocial behavior emerging in an adult over 40 with no childhood history of conduct disorder.
Anosmia and frontal release signs (grasp reflex) on neurological exam.
Papilledema on fundoscopy indicating elevated intracranial pressure.

name: Pyromania
symptoms: Deliberate and purposeful fire setting on more than one occasion, accompanied by tension or affective arousal before the act, fascination with/curiosity about fire and its situational contexts, and pleasure, gratification, or relief when setting fires or witnessing/participating in their aftermath, not done for monetary gain, revenge, or political ideology.

differentials.overlap: Repetitive dangerous fire setting, lighting fires inside the house, lack of concern for danger.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe memory impairment, disorientation, agnosia, apraxia; fires are set out of confusion, forgetting stove is on, or perseverative motor actions rather than primary pyromania.
differentials.workup: MoCA cognitive testing; Brain MRI (generalized cerebral or frontal atrophy).

differentials.overlap: Lighting matches or fires in a trance-like state without awareness.
differentials.physical_signs: Complex partial seizure automatisms, unresponsiveness during fire lighting, amnesia for the act, lip smacking.
differentials.workup: Prolonged Video-EEG; Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Setting fires resulting in major destruction.
differentials.physical_signs: Fire setting is driven by command auditory hallucinations or bizarre persecutory/delusional beliefs (e.g. purifying demons); absence of primary pyromaniac fire fascination.
differentials.workup: Psychiatric clinical interview; Evaluation of delusional content.

red_flags: Fire setting driven by command auditory hallucinations or religious purification delusions (psychosis).
Fire setting occurring in an amnestic confusional state in an older adult (dementia).
Trance-like state with lip smacking during fire manipulation (epilepsy).

name: Kleptomania
symptoms: Recurrent failure to resist impulses to steal objects that are not needed for personal use or for their monetary value, accompanied by an increasing sense of tension immediately before committing the theft, and pleasure, gratification, or relief at the time of committing the theft, not committed to express anger or vengeance and not in response to a delusion.

differentials.overlap: Compulsive shoplifting of worthless items (candy, trinkets), lack of embarrassment when caught.
differentials.physical_signs: Age of onset 45-65, social disinhibition, loss of empathy, hyperorality, primitive reflexes (grasp/snout).
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (frontal and temporal lobe atrophy); FDG-PET scan; Standardized executive cognitive testing.

differentials.mimic: Dopamine Agonist Induced Impulse Control Disorder (T42.8X5A)
differentials.overlap: Compulsive stealing, shoplifting, pathological gambling, hypersexuality, punding.
differentials.physical_signs: Underlying Parkinson's disease or restless legs syndrome; taking pramipexole, ropinirole, or levodopa.
differentials.workup: Medication audit; QUIP-RS scale; Resolution upon dopamine agonist dose reduction.

differentials.overlap: Inability to inhibit impulses to take objects in plain sight (utilization behavior), stealing.
differentials.physical_signs: Utilization behavior (compulsively using or pocketing objects placed in front of them), anosmia, executive dysfunction.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (orbitofrontal / ventromedial prefrontal damage).

red_flags: New-onset shoplifting in an adult over 50 with no prior criminal history (demands brain MRI for frontotemporal dementia).
Compulsive stealing developing after starting pramipexole or ropinirole (dopamine agonist toxicity).
Utilization behavior (compulsive automatic grasping and pocketing of examiner's pens/tools).

name: Other Specified Disruptive, Impulse-Control Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a disruptive, impulse-control, and conduct disorder predominate but do not meet full criteria (e.g., recurrent behavioral outbursts with insufficient frequency).

differentials.overlap: Severe cyclical rage outbursts, aggression, property damage occurring exclusively in the late luteal phase.
differentials.physical_signs: Complete follicular phase euthymia and compliance; physical symptoms (breast tenderness, bloating).
differentials.workup: Prospective daily symptom logging (DRSP) across 2 consecutive menstrual cycles.

differentials.overlap: Violent, aggressive, combative outbursts upon being awakened from sleep.
differentials.physical_signs: Disorientation, slurred speech, combative resistance to awakening; normal daytime behavioral control.
differentials.workup: Overnight Polysomnography (ruling out OSA and NREM parasomnia).

differentials.overlap: Episodic reckless impulsivity, belligerence, impaired judgment.
differentials.physical_signs: Perioral rash ('glue-sniffer's eczema'), chemical breath odor, paint stains on clothing, transient ataxia.
differentials.workup: Blood/urine solvent screening; BMP (hypokalemia, distal renal tubular acidosis).

red_flags: Outbursts occur exclusively upon being awakened from deep sleep (confusional arousals).
Severe cyclic aggression that completely vanishes within 2 days of menses onset (PMDD).
Perioral rash and chemical breath odor (volatile solvent abuse).

name: Unspecified Disruptive, Impulse-Control Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a disruptive, impulse-control, and conduct disorder predominate but there is insufficient information to make a specific diagnosis.

differentials.overlap: Violent destructive behavior, unprovoked assaults, severe agitation.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe tachycardia, hypertension, diaphoresis, hyperthermia, mydriasis, delirium.
differentials.workup: Expanded GC-MS toxicology screen; Serum CPK (rhabdomyolysis); 12-lead ECG.

differentials.overlap: Sudden behavioral volatility, combativeness, disinhibition, confusion.
differentials.physical_signs: Fever, seizures, autonomic instability, memory loss.
differentials.workup: CSF autoimmune encephalopathy panel; Brain MRI with contrast.

differentials.overlap: Bizarre combative behavior, violent resistance to assistance, confusion.
differentials.physical_signs: Diaphoresis, tachycardia, pale clammy skin, immediate recovery with IV dextrose.
differentials.workup: Immediate bedside capillary blood glucose measurement.

red_flags: Violent agitation with diaphoresis, tachycardia, and blood glucose < 50 mg/dL (hypoglycemia).
Severe hyperthermia (> 39.0 C / 102 F) and tachycardia in an aggressively agitated patient (toxic delirium).
Fever and new-onset seizures accompanying behavioral violence (encephalitis).

name: Alcohol Use Disorder & Induced Syndromes
symptoms: A problematic pattern of alcohol use leading to clinically significant impairment or distress, manifested by >= 2 criteria in a 12-month period across: impaired control, social impairment, risky use, tolerance, and withdrawal.

differentials.overlap: Confusion, slurred speech, ataxia, drowsiness, behavioral disinhibition, often attributed purely to acute intoxication.
differentials.physical_signs: Asterixis (flapping tremor on wrist dorsiflexion), fetor hepaticus (sweet musty breath odor), spider angiomas, palmar erythema, jaundice, caput medusae, ascites.
differentials.workup: Venous or arterial blood ammonia (elevated, drawn on ice); Total bilirubin, albumin, PT/INR (> 1.5); Abdominal ultrasound / Doppler of portal vein.

differentials.overlap: Confusion, ataxia, severe memory loss, confabulation, drowsiness.
differentials.physical_signs: Horizontal nystagmus, bilateral sixth nerve (lateral rectus) palsy, conjugate gaze palsies, wide-based ataxia; chronic alcohol use history.
differentials.workup: Immediate empiric IV Thiamine (500 mg TID) BEFORE any IV glucose infusion; Whole blood thiamine diphosphate; Brain MRI (mamillary body / medial thalamic hyperintensities).

differentials.overlap: Progressive confusion, apathy, fluctuating somnolence, unsteady gait in chronic alcohol misuse.
differentials.physical_signs: Asymmetric deep tendon reflexes, pronator drift, mild contralateral hemiparesis, pupillary asymmetry, history of falls.
differentials.workup: Non-contrast Brain CT (crescent-shaped extra-axial collection crossing suture lines); Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Agitation, confusion, nausea, vomiting, tremulousness.
differentials.physical_signs: Tachypnea (Kussmaul breathing), dehydration, fruity acetone breath, tachycardia, diaphoresis.
differentials.workup: Serum beta-hydroxybutyrate (markedly elevated); Arterial blood gas (high anion gap metabolic acidosis); Blood glucose.

red_flags: Asterixis (flapping tremor) and sweet musty breath odor in a confused patient (hepatic encephalopathy).
Ataxia, nystagmus, and gaze palsies in an alcoholic patient (urgent IV thiamine emergency for Wernicke's).
Focal neurological deficits or pupillary asymmetry following a fall (chronic subdural hematoma).
Severe metabolic acidosis with elevated beta-hydroxybutyrate (Alcoholic Ketoacidosis).

name: Caffeine Intoxication & Caffeine Withdrawal
symptoms: Intoxication: Recent consumption of caffeine (usually > 250 mg) with >= 5 of: restlessness, nervousness, excitement, insomnia, flushed face, diuresis, GI disturbance, muscle twitching, rambling speech, tachycardia/arrhythmia, inexhaustibility, psychomotor agitation. Withdrawal: Abrupt cessation followed within 24h by headache, marked fatigue, dysphoric mood, difficulty concentrating, flu-like symptoms.

differentials.overlap: Severe paroxysmal panic, pounding palpitations, tremulousness, diaphoresis, headache.
differentials.physical_signs: Paroxysmal hypertension (> 180-220 mmHg systolic), marked skin pallor, absence of high dietary caffeine intake.
differentials.workup: Plasma free metanephrines/normetanephrines; 24-hr urine fractionated metanephrines.

differentials.overlap: Sudden racing heartbeat, lightheadedness, chest tightness, anxiety.
differentials.physical_signs: Regular tachycardia (150-220 bpm) with abrupt start and termination, responsive to vagal maneuvers.
differentials.workup: 12-lead ECG; Continuous ambulatory Holter monitor.

differentials.overlap: Nervousness, fine tremor, insomnia, palpitations, heat intolerance, weight loss.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting sinus tachycardia, lid lag, exophthalmos, diffuse goiter with vascular bruit.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (< 0.01 mIU/L); Free T4 and Free T3; TSI antibodies.

red_flags: Paroxysmal blood pressure spikes > 180 mmHg with headache and pallor (pheochromocytoma).
Sustained heart rate > 150 bpm with sudden onset/offset (cardiac arrhythmia).
Suppressed TSH with fine resting hand tremor and diffuse goiter.

name: Cannabis Use Disorder & Induced Syndromes
symptoms: A problematic pattern of cannabis use leading to clinically significant impairment or distress, manifested by >= 2 criteria in a 12-month period, including cannabis-induced psychotic disorder (prominent delusions/hallucinations) and cannabis hyperemesis syndrome.

differentials.overlap: Recurrent episodes of intractable nausea and severe vomiting.
differentials.physical_signs: Personal or family history of migraine; episodes occur in discrete cycles with normal health in between; *absence* of cannabis use; absence of compulsive hot bathing behavior.
differentials.workup: Upper endoscopy; Brain MRI; Abdominal CT.

differentials.overlap: Paranoid delusions, auditory hallucinations, thought disorganization in a young cannabis user.
differentials.physical_signs: Psychotic symptoms persist beyond 4 weeks after total verified cessation of cannabis use (substance-induced psychosis typically remits within days to weeks of drug clearance).
differentials.workup: Serial Urine Drug Screens (monitoring THC clearance over 30-45 days); Comprehensive psychiatric evaluation.

differentials.overlap: Acute behavioral agitation, bizarre delusions, paranoia, insomnia in a young person presumed to have 'smoked bad weed'.
differentials.physical_signs: Orofacial dyskinesias, choreoathetosis, autonomic lability, hypoventilation, negative urine drug screen.
differentials.workup: CSF and serum anti-GluN1 NMDA receptor antibodies; Pelvic ultrasound; Video-EEG.

red_flags: Compulsive hot bathing/showering for hours daily providing temporary relief from vomiting (Cannabis Hyperemesis Syndrome).
Persistence of delusions/hallucinations > 4 weeks after confirmed negative urine drug screens (indicates primary schizophrenia).
Involuntary facial dyskinesias or hyperthermia in an agitated young person (autoimmune encephalitis).

name: Phencyclidine & Hallucinogen Use Disorders
symptoms: Problematic use of hallucinogens (LSD, psilocybin, MDMA) or phencyclidine (PCP), with intoxication characterized by perceptual alterations, depersonalization, derealization, illusions, synesthesias, or violent combative agitation, and Hallucinogen Persisting Perception Disorder (HPPD / flashbacks).

differentials.overlap: Continuous, unremitting dynamic tiny flickering dots across entire visual field, trailing images (palinopsia), photophobia.
differentials.physical_signs: Completely normal ophthalmologic and brain MRI examinations; symptoms present continuously 24/7 without prior hallucinogen exposure; accompanied by bilateral tinnitus.
differentials.workup: Visual fields; Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT); Brain MRI; Neuro-ophthalmology evaluation.

differentials.overlap: Visual hallucinations (picking at clothes), agitation, delirium, muttering.
differentials.physical_signs: 'Hot as a hare, blind as a bat, dry as a bone, red as a beet, mad as a hatter': anhidrosis, flushed skin, urinary retention, mydriasis, tachycardia; PCP features rotary nystagmus, diaphoresis, and hypertension.
differentials.workup: Toxidrome physical exam; Bladder scan (> 500 mL retention in anticholinergic); Urine drug screen.

differentials.overlap: Episodic visual hallucinations (colored flashing circles, palinopsia, micropsia/macropsia).
differentials.physical_signs: Visual hallucinations are brief (< 1-3 minutes), paroxysmal, stereotyped, followed by eye deviation, vomiting, or headache.
differentials.workup: Routine / Video-EEG with occipital leads; Brain MRI (occipital cortical dysplasia or vascular malformation).

red_flags: Rotary or vertical nystagmus with marked analgesia to pain and violent combativeness (pathognomonic for PCP intoxication).
Urinary retention, total anhidrosis, and absent bowel sounds (anticholinergic toxidrome).
Brief paroxysmal colored visual circles lasting < 2 minutes with eye turning (occipital lobe epilepsy).

name: Inhalant Use Disorder & Toxic Encephalopathy
symptoms: Problematic use of volatile hydrocarbons (glue, gasoline, spray paint, lighter fluid, nitrous oxide) leading to intoxication (dizziness, nystagmus, incoordination, slurred speech, lethargy, tremor, psychomotor retardation, euphoria) and chronic white matter neurotoxicity.

differentials.mimic: Subacute Combined Degeneration from Nitrous Oxide ('Whippets') (E53.8 / G32.0)
differentials.overlap: Severe sensory ataxia, difficulty walking, burning paresthesias, spastic paraparesis, cognitive blunting.
differentials.physical_signs: Loss of vibration and proprioception in lower extremities, positive Romberg sign, hyperreflexia, extensor plantars (Babinski), caused by irreversible oxidation of the cobalt core of Vitamin B12 by N2O.
differentials.workup: Serum Methylmalonic Acid (MMA markedly elevated > 1000 nmol/L); Serum Homocysteine (markedly elevated); Serum B12 (often falsely normal!); Cervical Spine MRI (inverted 'V-sign' / dorsal column hyperintensity).

differentials.mimic: Toluene-Induced Distal Renal Tubular Acidosis (Type 1 RTA) (N25.8 / T52.1X1A)
differentials.overlap: Profound muscular weakness, quadriparesis, confusion, cardiac arrhythmias in chronic glue/paint sniffers.
differentials.physical_signs: 'Glue-sniffer's rash' (eczema/erythema around nose and mouth), chemical breath odor, hypokalemic paralysis.
differentials.workup: Serum Potassium (severe hypokalemia < 2.0-2.5 mEq/L); Arterial blood gas (normal anion gap hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis); Urine pH (> 5.5 despite systemic acidosis); Urinary hippuric acid.

differentials.mimic: Toluene Leukoencephalopathy / White Matter Dementia (T52.1X1A / F02.80)
differentials.overlap: Severe progressive cognitive decline, apathy, cerebellar ataxia, dysarthria, tremor in chronic solvent abusers.
differentials.physical_signs: Cerebellar signs (dysmetria, intention tremor), hyperreflexia, spasticity, anosmia.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (striking, diffuse, symmetric T2/FLAIR hyperintensity of cerebral and cerebellar white matter with loss of grey-white differentiation).

red_flags: Severe hypokalemic paralysis with chemical breath odor and perioral rash (Toluene-induced Type 1 RTA).
Severe sensory ataxia and dorsal column loss in a young person abusing nitrous oxide whippets (elevated MMA).
Diffuse white matter hyperintensity on Brain MRI in a young inhalant abuser.

name: Opioid Use Disorder & Overdose/Withdrawal
symptoms: Problematic pattern of opioid use (heroin, oxycodone, fentanyl, methadone) leading to clinically significant impairment. Overdose: classic opioid toxidrome (coma, pinpoint miosis, respiratory depression). Withdrawal: dysphoria, nausea/vomiting, muscle aches, lacrimation, rhinorrhea, pupillary dilation, piloerection, sweating, diarrhea, yawning, fever, insomnia.

differentials.overlap: Coma, pinpoint pupils, respiratory failure, flaccid quadriplegia mimicking acute opioid overdose.
differentials.physical_signs: Pinpoint pupils (due to sympathetic pathway disruption in pons) that do NOT dilate in response to IV naloxone; severe hyperthermia, decerebrate posturing, absent horizontal dolls-eye reflex.
differentials.workup: Immediate IV Naloxone (0.4-2.0 mg) trial (lack of response strongly suggests pontine lesion); Urgent Non-contrast Head CT (demonstrating hyperdense hemorrhage in central pons).

differentials.overlap: Fever, diaphoresis, myalgias, nausea, vomiting, agitation resembling severe opioid withdrawal.
differentials.physical_signs: Nuchal rigidity (stiff neck), positive Kernig and Brudzinski signs, petechial or purpuric rash, altered mental status with confusion (opioid withdrawal preserves clear sensorium).
differentials.workup: Lumbar puncture (CSF pleocytosis > 1000 WBC/uL, elevated protein, low glucose); Blood cultures; CBC.

differentials.overlap: Severe sedation, coma, bradycardia, hypotension; partially resistant to naloxone.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe necrotic cutaneous ulcers/abscesses at non-injection sites (arms, legs, torso), severe bradycardia, profound hypotension.
differentials.workup: Urine/blood GC-MS toxicology for xylazine (alpha-2 adrenergic agonist); Supportive hemodynamic management.

red_flags: Pinpoint pupils and coma that fail to reverse after 4-10 mg of IV naloxone (pontine hemorrhage).
Severe necrotic non-healing skin ulcers in a fentanyl user (Xylazine contamination).
Nuchal rigidity, petechial purpura, and confusion in a patient presumed to be in withdrawal (bacterial meningitis).

name: Sedative, Hypnotic, or Anxiolytic Use Disorder
symptoms: Problematic pattern of benzodiazepine, barbiturate, or Z-drug use leading to impairment. Withdrawal: autonomic hyperactivity (tachycardia, diaphoresis, hypertension), coarse hand tremor, insomnia, nausea, transient visual/tactile hallucinations, psychomotor agitation, anxiety, and grand mal withdrawal seizures.

differentials.overlap: Gross coarse hand tremor, tachycardia, diaphoresis, hallucinations, seizures.
differentials.physical_signs: Identical GABAergic withdrawal toxidrome Footprint; elevated blood alcohol level or history of recent alcohol cessation.
differentials.workup: CIWA-Ar scoring; Blood alcohol concentration; BMP (hypomagnesemia, hypokalemia); Liver enzymes.

differentials.overlap: Severe agitation, delirium, extreme tachycardia (> 140 bpm), diaphoresis, tremulousness, hyperthermia.
differentials.physical_signs: Goiter, exophthalmos, atrial fibrillation, high-output heart failure, systolic hypertension.
differentials.workup: Burch-Wartofsky Point Scale (> 45 indicates thyroid storm); Serum TSH (< 0.01 mIU/L); Free T4 and Free T3.

differentials.overlap: Agitation, autonomic instability, diaphoresis, hyperthermia, tremor.
differentials.physical_signs: Spontaneous clonus, inducible ocular clonus, hyperreflexia pronounced in lower extremities (benzodiazepine withdrawal features tremor and hyperreflexia without clonus).
differentials.workup: Hunter Serotonin Toxicity Criteria; Serum CPK; Medication audit.

red_flags: Grand mal seizures emerging 2-7 days after stopping alprazolam, clonazepam, or diazepam (benzodiazepine withdrawal emergency).
Severe hyperthermia > 40 C (104 F) with atrial fibrillation and thyroid enlargement (thyroid storm).
Spontaneous lower extremity clonus and ocular flutter following serotonergic medication changes.

name: Stimulant (Cocaine / Amphetamine) Use Disorder
symptoms: Problematic pattern of amphetamine-type substance, cocaine, or other stimulant use leading to impairment. Intoxication: tachycardia/bradycardia, pupillary dilation, elevated/lowered BP, perspiration/chills, nausea, weight loss, psychomotor agitation, muscular weakness, respiratory depression, chest pain, cardiac arrhythmias, confusion, seizures, dystonia, coma.

differentials.mimic: Acute Coronary Vasospasm / Myocardial Infarction (I21.9 / I20.1)
differentials.overlap: Severe substernal chest pressure, diaphoresis, shortness of breath, palpitations, catastrophic dread.
differentials.physical_signs: Tachycardia, diaphoresis, hypertension, pallor; cocaine directly inhibits norepinephrine reuptake and promotes coronary vasoconstriction and platelet aggregation.
differentials.workup: 12-lead ECG (ST elevations, ST depressions, T-wave inversions); Serial high-sensitivity cardiac troponin; Coronary angiography (avoid beta-blockers due to unopposed alpha-1 vasoconstriction).

differentials.mimic: Acute Subarachnoid Hemorrhage / Intracranial Hemorrhage (I60.9 / I61.9)
differentials.overlap: Sudden catastrophic headache, vomiting, confusion, agitation, severe hypertension.
differentials.physical_signs: 'Thunderclap' headache peaking within 60 seconds, neck stiffness, photophobia, focal neurological deficits, preretinal subhyaloid hemorrhages.
differentials.workup: Urgent Non-contrast Head CT (hyperdensity in basal cisterns); Lumbar puncture if CT is negative > 6 hrs (xanthochromia on spectrophotometry); CT Angiography.

differentials.mimic: Acute Aortic Dissection (Type A or B) (I71.00)
differentials.overlap: Severe tearing chest and back pain, diaphoresis, panic, hypertension.
differentials.physical_signs: Tearing pain radiating to interscapular back, pulse deficit (asymmetric radial or femoral pulses > 20 mmHg BP difference between arms), new aortic regurgitation murmur.
differentials.workup: CT Angiography of Chest and Abdomen; Transesophageal Echocardiogram (TEE).

red_flags: Sudden thunderclap headache peaking in < 60 seconds with hypertension (subarachnoid hemorrhage).
Tearing chest pain radiating to interscapular back with asymmetric arm blood pressures (aortic dissection).
Substernal chest pressure with ST-elevation in a young stimulant user (cocaine-induced MI; avoid non-selective beta-blockers).

name: Tobacco Use Disorder & Nicotine Withdrawal
symptoms: Problematic pattern of tobacco/nicotine use. Withdrawal: Abrupt cessation followed within 24h by >= 4 of: irritability/frustration/anger, anxiety, difficulty concentrating, increased appetite, restlessness, depressed mood, insomnia.

differentials.overlap: Irritability, anxiety, shakiness, increased hunger, difficulty concentrating.
differentials.physical_signs: Diaphoresis, tachycardia, symptoms occur 2-4 hours postprandially and resolve rapidly with food.
differentials.workup: Capillary blood glucose during symptoms (< 55-70 mg/dL); Fasting insulin.

differentials.overlap: Severe restlessness, difficulty concentrating, impatience, impulsivity upon stopping smoking.
differentials.physical_signs: Lifelong history of inattention and motor restlessness; nicotine was used as self-medication for dopamine enhancement.
differentials.workup: Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS); Developmental history.

differentials.overlap: Chronic cough, dyspnea, fatigue, irritability.
differentials.physical_signs: Persistent cough with sputum production for >= 3 months in 2 consecutive years, wheezing.
differentials.workup: Spirometry (post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC < 0.70 confirms airflow limitation).

red_flags: Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC < 0.70 in a long-term smoker (COPD).
Significant diaphoresis, confusion, and blood glucose < 55 mg/dL.
Hemoptysis or unexplained weight loss in a chronic tobacco user (occult bronchogenic carcinoma).

name: Gambling Disorder (Pathological Gambling)
symptoms: Persistent and recurrent problematic gambling behavior leading to clinically significant impairment or distress, manifested by >= 4 criteria in a 12-month period: needing to gamble with increasing amounts of money to achieve excitement, restless/irritable when attempting to cut down, repeated unsuccessful efforts to control gambling, preoccupation with gambling, gambling when distressed, chasing losses, lying, jeopardizing relationships/jobs, relying on others for money.

differentials.overlap: Sudden, devastating emergence of catastrophic compulsive gambling, risking life savings, betting online for 18 hours/day.
differentials.physical_signs: Underlying Parkinson's disease or restless legs syndrome; taking pramipexole, ropinirole, or rotigotine; absence of prior gambling history.
differentials.workup: Medication audit calculating daily Levodopa Equivalent Dose (LEDD); QUIP-RS scale; Resolution or dramatic improvement upon tapering dopamine agonist.

differentials.overlap: Reckless, catastrophic financial spending, casino gambling, grandiosity.
differentials.physical_signs: Gambling occurs *exclusively* during discrete manic episodes accompanied by decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, and flight of ideas.
differentials.workup: Young Mania Rating Scale (YMRS); Mood timeline.

differentials.overlap: Reckless financial decisions, gambling away retirement funds, loss of judgment in adults aged 50-65.
differentials.physical_signs: Apathy, loss of empathy, social disinhibition, hyperorality, executive dysfunction on testing.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (frontal lobe atrophy); Neuropsychological testing.

red_flags: Devastating new-onset gambling behavior in a patient taking pramipexole or ropinirole (dopamine agonist toxicity).
Gambling occurs strictly during manic surges of boundless energy and sleeplessness.
New reckless financial gambling in an adult over 50 accompanied by personality changes (FTD).

name: Other (or Unknown) Substance-Related Disorders
symptoms: Problematic use of substances not covered in the standard categories (e.g., synthetic designer drugs, anabolic steroids, nitrous oxide, kratom, phenibut, anticholinergics), leading to intoxication, withdrawal, or substance-induced psychiatric syndromes.

differentials.overlap: Euphoria, analgesia, followed by severe opioid-like withdrawal (rhinorrhea, lacrimation, severe myalgias, diarrhea, insomnia).
differentials.physical_signs: Miosis on high doses, tremors, anorexia, weight loss, dark facial pigmentation (kratom melanosis).
differentials.workup: Specific liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) for mitragynine and 7-hydroxymitragynine (standard hospital UDS is negative!).

differentials.overlap: Severe rebound panic, severe insomnia, visual hallucinations, agitated delirium, tremors, autonomic storm.
differentials.physical_signs: Marked tachycardia, systolic hypertension, diaphoresis, hyperreflexia, psychosis; withdrawal closely resembles baclofen or severe alcohol withdrawal.
differentials.workup: Medication/nootropic audit (over-the-counter online nootropics); Management with high-dose baclofen or benzodiazepines.

differentials.overlap: Dissociative state, hallucinations, ataxia, euphoria, slurred speech.
differentials.physical_signs: Mydriasis, nystagmus, tachycardia, hypertension, diaphoresis, hyperreflexia; may cause false-positive PCP on routine immunoassay.
differentials.workup: Serum/urine GC-MS for dextromethorphan and dextrorphan; Screening for concurrent acetaminophen toxicity (in combination cold syrups).

red_flags: Severe opioid withdrawal symptoms with a totally negative standard hospital urine drug screen (kratom / mitragynine).
Severe agitated delirium and autonomic storm following cessation of an online 'nootropic' supplement (phenibut).
False-positive PCP result on urine drug screen in an adolescent abusing OTC cough syrup (dextromethorphan).

name: Non-Substance Addictive Disorders (Gaming / Compulsive Buying)
symptoms: A pattern of persistent or recurrent behavioral engagement (e.g., video gaming, compulsive shopping/buying) characterized by impaired control over the behavior, increasing priority given to the behavior over other life interests and daily activities, and continuation or escalation despite negative consequences.

differentials.overlap: Compulsive buying of dozens of identical unneeded items, maxing out credit cards, compulsive repetitive computer tinkering.
differentials.physical_signs: Underlying Parkinson's disease or RLS; taking pramipexole, ropinirole; complete lack of financial restraint.
differentials.workup: Medication audit; QUIP-RS scale; Dopamine agonist dose reduction.

differentials.mimic: Autism Spectrum Disorder (Intense Restrictive Video Game Interest) (F84.0)
differentials.overlap: Spending 12-16 hours daily playing video games, extreme distress if gaming is interrupted.
differentials.physical_signs: Gaming serves as a circumscribed special interest and sanctuary from social communication deficits, rather than addiction; presence of sensory sensitivities, literal communication.
differentials.workup: ADOS-2; Multidisciplinary developmental evaluation.

differentials.overlap: Massive catastrophic shopping sprees, purchasing luxury goods, buying cars.
differentials.physical_signs: Spending occurs in discrete manic episodes accompanied by euphoria, flight of ideas, decreased need for sleep.
differentials.workup: YMRS; Mood episode history.

red_flags: Catastrophic compulsive shopping emerging after starting pramipexole or ropinirole.
Gaming used as an escape from unaddressed classroom sensory overload or bullying in an autistic youth.
Buying sprees occurring exclusively during uninhibited sleepless manic episodes.

name: Synthetic Cannabinoid Intoxication Spectrum
symptoms: Exposure to full synthetic cannabinoid receptor agonists ('Spice', 'K2') characterized by severe acute psychosis, violent agitation, hallucinations, catatonia, seizures, tachycardia, hyperthermia, acute kidney injury, and sudden death (substantially more potent and toxic than natural THC).

differentials.overlap: Acute psychotic agitation, bizarre catatonic posturing, autonomic instability, seizures in young adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Orofacial dyskinesias, choreoathetosis, hypoventilation, negative routine urine tox.
differentials.workup: CSF and serum anti-GluN1 NMDA receptor antibodies; Continuous video-EEG.

differentials.overlap: Severe psychomotor agitation, paranoia, tachycardia, hypertension, diaphoresis, hyperthermia.
differentials.physical_signs: Mydriasis, tremors, bruxism, rhabdomyolysis.
differentials.workup: Urine Drug Screen; Specialized synthetic cannabinoid LC-MS/MS; Serum CPK; CMP (acute renal failure).

differentials.overlap: Agitation, bizarre behavior, hallucinations, fever, seizures.
differentials.physical_signs: Fever, neck stiffness, temporal lobe seizures, focal neurological deficits.
differentials.workup: Lumbar puncture (CSF HSV PCR); Brain MRI with contrast.

red_flags: Acute kidney injury with unexplained severe rhabdomyolysis (CPK > 10,000-50,000 U/L) in an agitated young person.
Negative standard urine drug screen in a patient with florid acute psychotic agitation and seizures (synthetic cannabinoids do not trigger THC immunoassays).
Severe hyperthermia > 39.5 C (103 F) and autonomic collapse.

name: Synthetic Cathinone ('Bath Salts') Toxic Psychosis
symptoms: Exposure to synthetic cathinones (MDPV, alpha-PVP / 'Flakka', mephedrone) producing excited delirium syndrome: extreme paranoid psychosis, superhuman strength, violent combativeness, nakedness (stripping clothes due to hyperthermia), profound agitation, hallucinations, and high risk of sudden cardiac arrest.

differentials.overlap: Hyperthermia, severe autonomic storm, diaphoresis, confusion, elevated CPK.
differentials.physical_signs: NMS features severe generalized 'lead-pipe' rigidity with *hypokinesia/catatonic stupor*; synthetic cathinone excited delirium features extreme hyperkinesia and violent thrashing.
differentials.workup: Serum Creatine Kinase (CK); Complete Blood Count; Urine myoglobin.

differentials.overlap: Agitation, hyperthermia, diaphoresis, tachycardia, delirium.
differentials.physical_signs: Spontaneous clonus, ocular flutter, hyperreflexia marked in legs, bilateral extensor plantars.
differentials.workup: Hunter criteria evaluation; Comprehensive tox screen.

differentials.overlap: Extreme agitation, delirium, fever (> 38.5 C), tachycardia (> 140 bpm), vomiting.
differentials.physical_signs: Goiter, exophthalmos, high-output heart failure; absence of acute drug exposure history.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (< 0.01 mIU/L); Free T4; Burch-Wartofsky score.

red_flags: Excited delirium: violent agitation, stripping off clothing, imperviousness to pain, hyperthermia (high risk of fatal ventricular dysrhythmia).
Serum CPK > 20,000 U/L indicating massive rhabdomyolysis and myoglobinuric acute renal failure.
Severe hyperthermia > 40.5 C (105 F) requiring immediate physical cooling immersion.

name: Fentanyl & Novel Synthetic Opioid Overdose Mimics
symptoms: Exposure to illicit fentanyl analogues (carfentanil, acetylfentanyl, nitazenes) producing lightning-fast respiratory arrest ('wooden chest syndrome' - severe fentanyl-induced chest wall rigidity preventing ventilation), pinpoint pupils, cyanosis, and coma.

differentials.overlap: Immediate total inability to ventilate, severe hypoxia, cyanosis, apnea.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe, rock-hard rigidity of intercostal and abdominal muscles preventing bag-valve-mask ventilation; occurs within seconds of IV injection; patient cannot be ventilated despite clear airway.
differentials.workup: Immediate administration of high-dose IV Naloxone (2-4 mg) AND immediate neuromuscular blockade (succinylcholine/rocuronium) with endotracheal intubation by emergency personnel.

differentials.mimic: Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion / Pontine Infarction (I63.9)
differentials.overlap: Coma, quadriplegia, pinpoint pupils, respiratory depression.
differentials.physical_signs: Negative response to naloxone, absent horizontal vestibulo-ocular reflexes, decerebrate posturing, hyperthermia.
differentials.workup: Urgent CT Angiography of head and neck (basilar artery filling defect); Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Profound apnea, coma, refractory to standard 0.4 mg naloxone doses.
differentials.physical_signs: Standard hospital fentanyl immunoassay strips are *negative*; requires massive repeated naloxone doses (4-10 mg) due to extreme receptor potency.
differentials.workup: Specialized reference lab LC-MS/MS testing; Continuous naloxone infusion.

red_flags: Inability to squeeze bag-valve-mask due to wooden rigidity of chest wall following injection (Wooden Chest Syndrome).
Coma with pinpoint pupils that is completely unresponsive to 10 mg of IV naloxone (basilar artery thrombosis).
Re-narcotization (patient wakes with naloxone, then relapses into fatal coma 30-45 minutes later as naloxone wears off while long-acting synthetic opioids persist).

name: Anabolic-Androgenic Steroid Use Disorder
symptoms: Problematic pattern of anabolic steroid use (testosterone, nandrolone, oxandrolone, trenbolone) despite severe physical, psychological, and social consequences, characterized by escalating megadosing ('stacking', 'pyramiding'), extreme body image dysphoria ('muscle dysmorphia' / bigorexia), explosive rage ('roid rage'), and severe suicidal depression upon withdrawal.

differentials.overlap: Hypertension, mood lability, irritability, muscle changes, purple striae.
differentials.physical_signs: Central truncal obesity with thin wasted limbs (steroids produce massive generalized muscular hypertrophy, not wasting), buffalo hump, moon facies.
differentials.workup: 24-hour urinary free cortisol; Dexamethasone suppression test.

differentials.overlap: Markedly elevated hematocrit (> 52-54%), facial plethora, headache, pruritus.
differentials.physical_signs: Splenomegaly, aquagenic pruritus (intense itching after warm shower); absence of supraphysiologic musculature.
differentials.workup: Peripheral blood JAK2 V617F mutation analysis; Serum erythropoietin (EPO, suppressed in PV; normal/low in AAS abuse).

differentials.overlap: Profound major depression, total erectile dysfunction, severe fatigue, suicidality following cycle cessation.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe bilateral testicular atrophy (< 10 mL), gynecomastia, loss of strength; hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis shutdown.
differentials.workup: Serum total and free testosterone (profoundly subnormal < 50-100 ng/dL); Undetectable LH and FSH (< 0.2 mIU/mL).

red_flags: Severe bilateral testicular atrophy and gynecomastia in a heavily muscled athlete.
Profound suicidal depression accompanied by undetectable LH and FSH following steroid cycle cessation.
Hematocrit > 54% with elevated blood pressure (high risk of thrombotic stroke and myocardial infarction).

name: Delirium (Hyperactive, Hypoactive, Mixed)
symptoms: A disturbance in attention (reduced ability to direct, focus, sustain, and shift attention) and awareness (reduced orientation to the environment), developing over a short period of time (hours to days), representing an acute change from baseline, fluctuating in severity during the day, accompanied by cognitive disturbance (memory, disorientation, language, perceptual distortion), directly caused by a physiological medical condition, substance intoxication/withdrawal, or multiple etiologies.

differentials.overlap: Acute fluctuating inattention, confusion, lethargy, or agitation.
differentials.physical_signs: Fever (> 38.0 C) or hypothermia (< 36.0 C), tachypnea (> 20 breaths/min), tachycardia (> 90 bpm), warm vasodilated skin or cold mottled extremities, hypotension (qSOFA >= 2).
differentials.workup: CBC with diff (leukocytosis or leukopenia with left shift > 10% bands); Blood cultures x 2; Urinalysis and urine culture; Serum lactate (> 2 mmol/L); Chest X-ray; Procalcitonin.

differentials.overlap: Fluctuating confusion, mutism, stupor, or wandering agitation in older adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Subtle rhythmic eyelid myoclonus, minor facial twitching, perseverative automatic gestures, lack of response to vocal cues.
differentials.workup: Urgent Continuous Video-EEG monitoring (demonstrating continuous rhythmic generalized or focal epileptiform spike-and-wave discharges); Resolution upon IV lorazepam/levetiracetam.

differentials.mimic: Acute Uremic or Hepatic Encephalopathy (N18.6 / K76.82)
differentials.overlap: Lethargy, confusion, hallucinations, sleep-wake reversal.
differentials.physical_signs: Asterixis (flapping tremor), multifocal myoclonus, uremic frost, fetor hepaticus, jaundice, ascites.
differentials.workup: Serum BUN (> 80-100 mg/dL) and Creatinine; Venous blood ammonia (elevated on ice); Liver panel; Arterial blood gas.

differentials.overlap: Agitated delirium, visual hallucinations (picking at invisible threads / liliputian hallucinations), incoherent speech.
differentials.physical_signs: Dilated pupils, flushed skin, dry axillae and mucous membranes, resting tachycardia, urinary retention with palpable bladder globe, absent bowel sounds.
differentials.workup: Bladder ultrasound scan (> 500 mL retention); Medication audit calculating Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB) score; Response to physostigmine in refractory cases.

differentials.overlap: Acute confusion, combativeness, hallucinations, progressing to stupor.
differentials.physical_signs: Profuse diaphoresis, tachycardia, dilated pupils, hypothermia, history of insulin or sulfonylurea therapy.
differentials.workup: Immediate point-of-care capillary blood glucose measurement (< 55 mg/dL diagnostic); Immediate IV D50W administration.

red_flags: Point-of-care capillary glucose < 55 mg/dL (immediate IV dextrose required).
Fever, tachypnea, tachycardia, and elevated serum lactate (sepsis resuscitation protocol).
Subtle rhythmic eyelid twitching in an unresponsive patient (urgent EEG for NCSE).
Palpable distended bladder with dilated pupils and dry skin (anticholinergic urinary retention).

name: Other Specified & Unspecified Delirium
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of delirium predominate but do not meet full criteria, or information is inadequate to determine etiology.

differentials.overlap: Confusion, disorientation, headache, nausea, lethargy in winter months.
differentials.physical_signs: Retinal hemorrhages, confusion, multiple cohabitants or family members ill simultaneously.
differentials.workup: Venous or arterial carboxyhemoglobin (COHb > 5-10%); 12-lead ECG; 100% normobaric or hyperbaric oxygen.

differentials.mimic: Acute Non-Dominant Parietal Stroke (Right MCA Infarction) (I63.9)
differentials.overlap: Acute agitated confusion, disorientation, bizarre affect.
differentials.physical_signs: Left hemispatial neglect, left visual field cut (hemianopia), anosognosia, subtle left facial weakness.
differentials.workup: Urgent Non-contrast Head CT + CT Angiography; Brain MRI (DWI restricted diffusion).

differentials.overlap: Progressive confusion, delirium, lethargy, seizures.
differentials.physical_signs: Hyporeflexia, gait instability, nausea, seizures when serum Na drops rapidly < 120 mEq/L.
differentials.workup: Basic Metabolic Panel (serum sodium < 120-125 mEq/L); Serum and urine osmolality.

red_flags: Multiple household members with acute confusion and headache (Carbon Monoxide poisoning).
Left hemispatial neglect or failure to acknowledge left side of space (acute right parietal stroke).
Serum sodium < 120 mEq/L with seizure activity (hypertonic 3% saline protocol).

name: Major/Mild Neurocognitive Disorder: Alzheimer's Disease
symptoms: Insidious onset and gradual progressive impairment in one or more cognitive domains (typically learning and memory, followed by executive function, language, and visuospatial ability), meeting criteria for Major NCD (interferes with independence in everyday activities) or Mild NCD (does not interfere with independence).

differentials.overlap: Progressive cognitive impairment, executive slowing, memory deficits in older adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Hakim-Adams Triad: (1) Magnetic gait ataxia (shuffling, wide-based, feet glued to floor, difficulty turning), (2) Early urinary urge incontinence, (3) Cognitive decline; gait disorder *precedes* cognitive decline (opposite of Alzheimer's).
differentials.workup: Brain MRI/CT (ventriculomegaly out of proportion to sulcal enlargement, Evans index > 0.30, narrow callosal angle); High-volume lumbar puncture tap test (removal of 30-50 mL CSF) demonstrating objective improvement in gait speed within 2-4 hours.

differentials.overlap: Progressive memory decline, executive dysfunction, apathy, confusion, depression.
differentials.physical_signs: Loss of vibratory sense and proprioception in lower extremities, positive Romberg test, hyperreflexia and Babinski sign, atrophic glossitis, lemon-yellow skin pallor.
differentials.workup: Serum Vitamin B12 (< 200 pg/mL); Serum Methylmalonic Acid (MMA > 400 nmol/L); Serum Homocysteine; CBC (macrocytosis, MCV > 100 fL).

differentials.overlap: Reversible dementia, cognitive slowing, severe memory impairment, psychomotor slowing.
differentials.physical_signs: Delayed reflex relaxation (Woltman sign), coarse dry skin, cold intolerance, periorbital puffiness, bradycardia.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (> 10-20 mIU/L); Free T4 (< 0.7 ng/dL); Anti-TPO antibodies.

differentials.overlap: Subacute cognitive decline, memory impairment, apathy, somnolence in elderly.
differentials.physical_signs: Fluctuating alertness, mild asymmetric weakness, history of minor falls weeks prior.
differentials.workup: Non-contrast Head CT / Brain MRI (crescent extra-axial fluid collection with mass effect).

differentials.overlap: Severe complaints of memory loss, poor concentration, functional impairment.
differentials.physical_signs: Patient highlights and laments memory deficits ('I can't remember anything'; AD patients minimize deficits), gives up easily on testing ('I don't know'), intact recognition memory on testing.
differentials.workup: Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS); MoCA cognitive testing; Trial of antidepressant therapy restores cognitive function.

red_flags: Magnetic shuffling gait and urinary incontinence occurring *before* or concurrently with mild cognitive decline (NPH).
Loss of vibration and position sense in feet with positive Romberg sign (Vitamin B12 deficiency).
Delayed deep tendon reflex relaxation with elevated TSH > 20 mIU/L (Hypothyroidism).
Patient actively complains of severe memory loss while scoring normally on objective recognition testing (Depressive Pseudodementia).

name: Major/Mild NCD: Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration
symptoms: Insidious onset and gradual progression of either: (1) Behavioral variant: >= 3 of: behavioral disinhibition, apathy/inertia, loss of sympathy/empathy, perseverative/stereotyped/compulsive behavior, hyperorality/dietary changes, executive dysfunction with relative preservation of memory/visuospatial skills; OR (2) Language variant (Primary Progressive Aphasia): prominent decline in language abilities.

differentials.overlap: Profound personality change, behavioral disinhibition, apathy, loss of social judgment.
differentials.physical_signs: Foster Kennedy syndrome (ipsilateral optic atrophy + contralateral papilledema + ipsilateral anosmia), frontal release signs, morning headaches.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with and without gadolinium (visualizing large extra-axial enhancing subfrontal mass compressing frontal lobes); Fundoscopic exam.

differentials.overlap: Social disinhibition, hypersexuality, reckless financial spending, grandiosity, restlessness.
differentials.physical_signs: Preserved executive cognitive architecture on neuropsychological testing; episodic course (FTD is insidiously progressive without remission).
differentials.workup: Neuropsychological assessment (demonstrating severe frontal executive deficits in FTD); Brain MRI (frontal lobe atrophy in FTD vs normal MRI in primary mania).

differentials.overlap: Frontal behavioral changes, disinhibition, cognitive decline, psychosis.
differentials.physical_signs: Vertical Supranuclear Gaze Palsy (inability to look down voluntarily), gelastic cataplexy, ataxia, splenomegaly.
differentials.workup: Vertical saccade examination; Plasma oxysterols; NPC1/NPC2 sequencing.

red_flags: Anosmia, papilledema, or unilateral optic atrophy in an adult with personality disinhibition (subfrontal meningioma).
Vertical gaze palsy (patient cannot follow visual target down) (Niemann-Pick C or Progressive Supranuclear Palsy).
Primitive frontal release reflexes (snout, grasp, palmomental reflexes) in a middle-aged adult.

name: Major/Mild NCD with Lewy Bodies
symptoms: Core diagnostic features: (1) Fluctuating cognition with pronounced variations in attention and alertness, (2) Recurrent well-formed and detailed visual hallucinations, (3) REM sleep behavior disorder (dream enactment), (4) One or more spontaneous cardinal features of parkinsonism (bradykinesia, rest tremor, rigidity). Indicative biomarker: reduced dopamine transporter uptake in basal ganglia.

differentials.overlap: Parkinsonism, visual hallucinations, cognitive decline, fluctuating attention.
differentials.physical_signs: The 'One-Year Rule': in PDD, well-established motor parkinsonism precedes cognitive decline by at least 1 year (often 5-10 years); in DLB, cognitive impairment occurs before, concurrently with, or within 1 year of parkinsonism.
differentials.workup: Detailed chronological motor and cognitive timeline; DaT-SPECT scan.

differentials.mimic: Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea with Hypnagogic Hallucinations (G47.33)
differentials.overlap: Daytime cognitive fluctuations, drowsiness, vivid dream-like hallucinations.
differentials.physical_signs: Habitual loud snoring, witnessed apneas, absence of spontaneous parkinsonian rigidity or tremor.
differentials.workup: Overnight Polysomnography (AHI >= 15-30 events/hr); Absence of REM sleep without atonia.

differentials.mimic: Severe Antipsychotic-Induced Parkinsonism and Delirium (G21.11 / F05)
differentials.overlap: Acute worsening of parkinsonian rigidity, confusion, hallucinations.
differentials.physical_signs: Extreme neuroleptic sensitivity (DLB patients develop catastrophic rigidity, catatonia, or NMS when exposed even to low-dose first- or second-generation antipsychotics like haloperidol or risperidone).
differentials.workup: Medication audit; Complete avoidance of conventional antipsychotics; Low-dose quetiapine or pimavanserin if essential.

red_flags: Severe, catastrophic worsening of parkinsonism or catatonic collapse upon receiving a low-dose antipsychotic (pathognomonic neuroleptic sensitivity of DLB).
Detailed visual hallucinations of children, animals, or deceased relatives perceived with clarity.
History of acting out violent dreams during sleep years prior to cognitive decline.

name: Major/Mild Vascular Neurocognitive Disorder
icd10: F01.50 (Without Behavioral Disturbance), F01.51 (With Behavioral Disturbance)
symptoms: Cognitive deficits in complex attention and frontal executive function, temporally related to one or more cerebrovascular events, or prominent evidence of extensive subcortical cerebrovascular disease (infarctions, microbleeds, leukoaraiosis) on neuroimaging, with a stepwise or fluctuating decline.

differentials.overlap: Recurrent subcortical strokes, progressive vascular dementia, depression, executive dysfunction in patients aged 35-55.
differentials.physical_signs: History of severe migraines with aura starting in 20s, pseudobulbar palsy, hyperreflexia, absence of conventional cardiovascular risk factors.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (pathognomonic symmetric T2/FLAIR hyperintensities in the anterior temporal lobes and external capsules); NOTCH3 gene testing; Skin biopsy (GOM deposits).

differentials.overlap: Subcortical executive decline, psychomotor slowing, periventricular white matter changes on imaging.
differentials.physical_signs: Prominent magnetic gait ataxia and early urinary incontinence; gait impairment is out of proportion to cognitive deficits.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (Evans index > 0.30, narrow callosal angle); High-volume CSF tap test.
