differentials.overlap: Recurrent ischemic strokes, multi-infarct dementia, cognitive impairment in young adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Livedo reticularis (violaceous lace-like mottling on legs/arms), history of recurrent deep vein thrombosis or miscarriages.
differentials.workup: Lupus Anticoagulant; Anticardiolipin antibodies; Anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I antibodies (persistent positive on 2 draws 12 weeks apart).

red_flags: Anterior temporal lobe and external capsule white matter hyperintensities on MRI (pathognomonic for CADASIL).
Livedo reticularis and history of recurrent miscarriages or venous thrombosis in a young stroke patient (APS).
Stepwise deterioration corresponding to discrete focal neurological stroke episodes.

name: Major/Mild NCD Due to Traumatic Brain Injury
symptoms: Neurocognitive disorder presenting immediately following the occurrence of a traumatic brain injury (head displacement, blast injury) or immediately after recovery of consciousness, persisting past the acute post-injury period, with deficits in complex attention, executive function, learning, and memory.

differentials.overlap: Subacute cognitive decline, progressive somnolence, headache, apathy weeks after head trauma.
differentials.physical_signs: Fluctuating level of consciousness, mild asymmetric hemiparesis, hyperreflexia, pronator drift.
differentials.workup: Non-contrast Brain CT (crescent extra-axial collection); Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Progressive cognitive decline, explosive rage, depression, suicidality, parkinsonism developing years after repetitive head impacts.
differentials.physical_signs: History of repetitive contact sports (football, boxing, hockey) or military blast exposure; executive dysfunction, motor signs (dysarthria, tremor, ataxia).
differentials.workup: Comprehensive neuropsychological testing; 3T Brain MRI (cavum septum pellucidum, generalized atrophy, white matter damage); Neuropathologic criteria.

differentials.overlap: Severe cognitive 'brain fog', fatigue, difficulty reading, irritability, nausea.
differentials.physical_signs: Convergence insufficiency, abnormal smooth pursuit, saccadic dysmetria, motion-provoked dizziness.
differentials.workup: Vestibular-Ocular Motor Screening (VOMS); Comprehensive Neuro-optometric evaluation.

red_flags: Progressive somnolence and asymmetric hemiparesis weeks after head trauma (chronic subdural hematoma).
History of repetitive concussions with progressive behavioral rage, parkinsonism, and memory decay (CTE).
Convergence insufficiency and dizziness on reading following head impact (post-concussion visual-vestibular deficit).

name: Substance/Medication-Induced Major or Mild NCD
symptoms: Neurocognitive deficits that represent a significant decline from a previous level of performance, persisting beyond the usual duration of substance intoxication and acute withdrawal, directly attributable to the neurotoxic effects of substances or medications.

differentials.overlap: Progressive executive dysfunction, memory loss, severe irritability, depression, fatigue.
differentials.physical_signs: Burton line (blue-purple line on gingiva), peripheral motor neuropathy (wrist drop / foot drop), microcytic anemia, abdominal colic.
differentials.workup: Whole blood lead level (BLL > 20-40 mcg/dL); Peripheral blood smear (basophilic stippling); ZPP level.

differentials.overlap: Apathy, severe memory decline, parkinsonism, executive decay occurring weeks after carbon monoxide exposure.
differentials.physical_signs: Delayed post-hypoxic leukoencephalopathy: gait apraxia, masked facies, rigidity, urinary incontinence.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (bilateral symmetrical T2/FLAIR hyperintensity in globus pallidus and subcortical white matter).

differentials.overlap: Progressive cognitive decline, memory impairment, confusion in older adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, blurred vision, taking multiple anticholinergic agents (oxybutynin, diphenhydramine, TCAs, paroxetine).
differentials.workup: Anticholinergic Cognitive Burden (ACB) score calculation; Medication deprescribing trial restores baseline cognitive functioning.

red_flags: Bilateral symmetrical globus pallidus lesions on brain MRI following a furnace malfunction (Carbon Monoxide leukoencephalopathy).
Burton blue line on gums and wrist drop neuropathy (lead toxicity).
Reversal of cognitive impairment upon discontinuing bladder antispasmodics and antihistamines.

name: Major/Mild NCD Due to HIV Infection
symptoms: Subcortical pattern of neurocognitive impairment (prominent psychomotor slowing, executive dysfunction, impaired memory retrieval, apathy, social withdrawal) in an individual documented to have HIV infection, not attributable to opportunistic CNS infections or systemic illness.

differentials.overlap: Subacute cognitive decline, aphasia, visual field loss, hemiparesis in an HIV patient.
differentials.physical_signs: Homonymous hemianopia, focal motor deficits, limb ataxia; rapid progression over weeks (HAND progresses over months/years).
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (asymmetric confluent white matter hyperintensities involving subcortical U-fibers without mass effect or enhancement); CSF JC virus PCR.

differentials.overlap: Confusion, lethargy, headache, cognitive dulling in an immunocompromised host.
differentials.physical_signs: Fever, neck stiffness, papilledema, cranial nerve VI palsy (elevated opening pressure), CD4 < 100 cells/uL.
differentials.workup: Lumbar puncture with Opening Pressure measurement (often > 250-300 mm H2O); CSF Cryptococcal Antigen (CrAg lateral flow assay); India ink preparation; Fungal culture.

differentials.overlap: Confusion, cognitive slowing, seizures, focal neurological signs.
differentials.physical_signs: Hemiparesis, cranial neuropathies, fever, altered consciousness, CD4 < 100 cells/uL.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with contrast (multiple ring-enhancing lesions in basal ganglia with vasogenic edema); Serum Toxoplasma IgG antibody.

red_flags: Markedly elevated CSF opening pressure > 250 mm H2O with positive cryptococcal antigen (cryptococcal meningitis).
Multiple ring-enhancing lesions in basal ganglia on MRI (Cerebral Toxoplasmosis).
Confluent non-enhancing white matter lesions crossing U-fibers with positive CSF JC virus PCR (PML).

name: Major/Mild NCD Due to Prion Disease (CJD)
symptoms: Rapidly progressive neurocognitive impairment typically developing over weeks to a few months, accompanied by at least two of: myoclonus, visual or cerebellar problems, pyramidal or extrapyramidal signs, or akinetic mutism, leading to death within a year of onset.

differentials.overlap: Rapidly progressive dementia, myoclonus, seizures, psychiatric agitation over weeks.
differentials.physical_signs: Faciobrachial dystonic seizures (brief unilateral arm/facial jerks), hyponatremia; highly responsive to immunotherapy (CJD is non-responsive).
differentials.workup: Serum and CSF Autoimmune Encephalopathy antibody panel; CSF RT-QuIC (negative in limbic encephalitis; positive in CJD); Brain MRI (medial temporal T2 hyperintensity).

differentials.overlap: Rapid dementia, tremors, dysarthria, personality dissolution, ataxia.
differentials.physical_signs: Argyll Robertson pupils, tabetic sensory ataxia, hyperreflexia.
differentials.workup: Serum TP-PA / FTA-ABS; CSF-VDRL, cell count, protein; Treatment with IV penicillin G.

differentials.overlap: Rapid cognitive decline, myoclonus, seizures, hallucinations, fluctuating confusion.
differentials.physical_signs: Stimulus-sensitive myoclonus, tremor, ataxia, dramatic response to high-dose corticosteroids.
differentials.workup: Serum Anti-Thyroperoxidase (anti-TPO) antibodies (> 500 IU/mL); CSF protein; Brain MRI.

red_flags: Pathognomonic startle myoclonus (loud hand-clap provokes violent generalized myoclonic jerk).
CSF RT-QuIC positive (> 90% sensitivity, ~100% specificity for prion disease).
Cortical ribboning and basal ganglia hyperintensity ('hockey-stick sign') on Diffusion-Weighted MRI.
Periodic sharp-wave complexes (PSWC) at 1 Hz on routine EEG.

name: Major/Mild NCD Due to Parkinson's Disease
symptoms: Neurocognitive impairment developing in the context of established Parkinson's disease, where motor parkinsonism has been present for at least 1 year prior to the onset of cognitive decline, featuring executive dysfunction, impaired memory retrieval, visual hallucinations, and apathy.

differentials.overlap: Parkinsonism, early falls, cognitive slowing, executive dysfunction, personality changes.
differentials.physical_signs: Vertical Supranuclear Gaze Palsy (inability to look voluntarily downward), early prominent postural instability with backward falls, 'hummingbird sign' / 'penguin sign' on midbrain MRI, axial rigidity greater than limb rigidity, lack of resting tremor and poor levodopa response.
differentials.workup: Neurological examination of vertical saccades; Brain MRI (midbrain atrophy with thinning of midbrain tegmentum; midbrain-to-pons ratio < 0.20).

differentials.overlap: Parkinsonism, cognitive slowing, motor impairment.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe early autonomic failure (profound orthostatic hypotension, neurogenic bladder incontinence, erectile failure), cerebellar ataxia, 'hot cross bun sign' on pontine MRI, poor levodopa response.
differentials.workup: Autonomic reflex testing; Tilt table test; Brain MRI (pontine T2 cross sign); Post-void residual bladder scan.

differentials.overlap: Parkinsonian-like gait disturbance, executive cognitive decline, apathy.
differentials.physical_signs: Magnetic shuffling gait, early urinary incontinence, ventriculomegaly out of proportion to sulcal enlargement.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI; CSF tap test.

red_flags: Vertical Supranuclear Gaze Palsy (failure of downward saccades) with early backward falls (PSP).
Severe early orthostatic drop > 30 mmHg with urinary incontinence (Multiple System Atrophy).
Lack of resting tremor and total absence of response to high-dose carbidopa-levodopa.

name: Major/Mild NCD Due to Huntington's Disease
symptoms: Neurocognitive impairment in an individual with diagnosed Huntington's disease or at risk based on family history or genetic testing, characterized by subcortical executive dysfunction, processing slowing, apathy, irritability, and choreiform movement disorder.

differentials.overlap: Choreoathetosis, dystonia, tremor, progressive cognitive decline, psychiatric irritability.
differentials.physical_signs: Kayser-Fleischer rings on slit-lamp, wing-beating tremor, hepatosplenomegaly, young onset (< 35 years old).
differentials.workup: Slit-lamp exam; Serum ceruloplasmin (< 20 mg/dL); 24-hr urine copper (> 100 mcg/24h); ATP7B gene testing.

differentials.mimic: Huntington's Disease-Like Syndromes (HDL1, HDL2, C9orf72) (G10 / G31.89)
differentials.overlap: Phenotypically identical chorea, progressive dementia, and psychiatric symptoms with negative HTT gene testing.
differentials.physical_signs: Acanthocytes on peripheral blood smear (chorea-acanthocytosis), seizures, peripheral neuropathy.
differentials.workup: HTT gene negative; JPH3 (HDL2), PRNP (HDL1), and C9orf72 repeat expansion testing; Peripheral blood smear (acanthocytes).

differentials.overlap: Involuntary choreic movements, emotional lability, obsessive symptoms.
differentials.physical_signs: Acute onset in children/adolescents following strep pharyngitis; milkmaid's grip, darting tongue, carditis.
differentials.workup: ASO and Anti-DNase B titers; Echocardiogram; Self-limiting over 3-6 months.

red_flags: Kayser-Fleischer corneal rings on slit-lamp (Wilson's disease).
Acanthocytes on fresh peripheral blood smear (Chorea-Acanthocytosis / Neuroacanthocytosis).
Targeted HTT gene testing showing >= 36 CAG repeats (confirms Huntington's disease).

name: Major/Mild NCD Due to Another Medical Condition
icd10: F02.80 (Without Behavioral Disturbance), F02.81 (With Behavioral Disturbance)
symptoms: Neurocognitive impairment directly attributable to the physiological consequences of another medical condition not covered in the specific categories (e.g., Multiple Sclerosis, systemic lupus erythematosus, neurosarcoidosis, celiac disease).

differentials.mimic: Multiple Sclerosis (Secondary Progressive MS Cognitive Impairment) (G35)
differentials.overlap: Prominent information processing slowing, executive decline, memory retrieval deficits, depression.
differentials.physical_signs: Spastic paraparesis, internuclear ophthalmoplegia, hyperreflexia, positive Babinski signs, neurogenic bladder.
differentials.workup: Brain and Spinal Cord MRI with gadolinium (Dawson fingers, high T2 lesion load, brain volume loss / atrophy); Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT).

differentials.overlap: Subacute cognitive decline, apathy, headache, cranial neuropathies, hypothalamic dysfunction.
differentials.physical_signs: Facial nerve palsy (CN VII), uveitis, parotid enlargement, erythema nodosum, lupus pernio.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with contrast (nodular leptomeningeal enhancement at skull base); Chest CT (bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy); Serum ACE.

differentials.overlap: Cognitive 'brain fog', executive impairment, psychosis, major depression.
differentials.physical_signs: Malar rash, photosensitivity, non-deforming polyarthritis, oral ulcers, serositis.
differentials.workup: ANA; Anti-dsDNA; Anti-Sm; Complement C3/C4 (depressed in active flare); Brain MRI.

red_flags: Nodular leptomeningeal contrast enhancement at the skull base with facial nerve palsy (Neurosarcoidosis).
Information processing speed collapse on SDMT with demyelinating periventricular lesions (Multiple Sclerosis).
Depressed complement levels (C3/C4) and high-titer anti-dsDNA with cognitive decline (Lupus cerebritis).

name: Major/Mild NCD Due to Multiple Etiologies
symptoms: Neurocognitive impairment characterized by the simultaneous presence of more than one underlying neuropathological or medical process (e.g., Mixed Dementia: Alzheimer's Disease combined with Vascular Neurocognitive Disorder).

differentials.overlap: Gradual memory decline combined with sudden stepwise executive deteriorations and gait slowing.
differentials.physical_signs: Focal pyramidal signs (unilateral hyperreflexia, pronator drift), hypertension, cardiovascular disease.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (concomitant hippocampal volume loss AND extensive deep white matter ischemic hyperintensities / lacunar infarcts).

differentials.mimic: Mixed Alzheimer's & Dementia with Lewy Bodies (G30.9 / G31.83)
differentials.overlap: Severe memory impairment combined with visual hallucinations and parkinsonian rigidity.
differentials.physical_signs: Cogwheel rigidity, resting tremor, dream enactment, neuroleptic sensitivity.
differentials.workup: DaT-SPECT scan; Amyloid/tau PET or CSF biomarkers (A-beta-42/tau ratio); Polysomnography.

differentials.mimic: Dementia Complicated by Occult Metabolic Derangement (F03.90 / E03.9)
differentials.overlap: Rapid worsening of stable chronic dementia following an acute medical change.
differentials.physical_signs: Signs of dehydration, delayed reflexes, constipation, polypharmacy.
differentials.workup: CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, Urinalysis (frequently uncovers occult UTI or severe hypothyroidism exacerbating baseline dementia).

red_flags: Concomitant severe hippocampal atrophy AND extensive subcortical lacunar infarcts on MRI.
Rapid catastrophic worsening of baseline chronic dementia over days (demands search for occult infection, metabolic shift, or stroke).
Severe neuroleptic sensitivity in an Alzheimer's patient.

name: Unspecified Neurocognitive Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a neurocognitive disorder predominate but there is insufficient information to make a specific diagnosis (e.g., in acute emergency room admissions).

differentials.overlap: Progressive dementia, personality dissolution, memory loss, emotional lability.
differentials.physical_signs: Argyll Robertson pupils, dysarthric slurred speech, tremor of tongue/hands, sensory ataxia.
differentials.workup: Serum syphilis treponemal antibody screen (TP-PA/FTA-ABS); Lumbar puncture with CSF-VDRL, cell count, and protein.

differentials.overlap: Cognitive slowing, memory loss, lethargy, apathy, depression.
differentials.physical_signs: Hypotonia, hyporeflexia, bone aches, abdominal pain, severe constipation.
differentials.workup: Serum total and ionized calcium (> 10.5 mg/dL); Intact PTH; 24-hr urine calcium.

differentials.mimic: Chronic Heavy Metal Toxicity (Lead, Mercury, Arsenic) (T56.0X1A - T57.0X1A)
differentials.overlap: Dementia, behavioral changes, memory loss, ataxia, peripheral neuropathy.
differentials.physical_signs: Burton line on gums (lead), erethism and intention tremor (mercury), Mees' lines on nails (arsenic), peripheral neuropathy.
differentials.workup: Heavy metals blood and 24-hour urine panel (lead, mercury, arsenic, cadmium).

red_flags: Argyll Robertson pupils (unreactive to direct light with preserved accommodation).
Elevated serum calcium > 11.0 mg/dL with cognitive dulling.
Mees' transverse white lines on fingernails or severe peripheral neuropathy.

name: Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus Cognitive Syndrome
symptoms: A specific subcortical neurocognitive disorder characterized by psychomotor slowing, apathy, executive dysfunction, and memory retrieval deficits, occurring in the context of the classic Hakim-Adams triad (gait ataxia, urinary incontinence, dementia).

differentials.overlap: Memory decline, executive impairment, slow walking in older adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Alzheimer's features early cortical amnestic memory loss with normal arm-swing and normal gait mechanics early; NPH features prominent magnetic gait (feet glued to floor) *preceding* cognitive slowing.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (disproportionately enlarged subarachnoid-space hydrocephalus [DESH], ventriculomegaly with tight high-convexity sulci); CSF tap test.

differentials.overlap: Gait disturbance, urinary urge incontinence, subcortical dementia.
differentials.physical_signs: Pseudobulbar palsy, hyperreflexia, extensive diffuse bilateral white matter ischemic rarefaction on imaging.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (confluent periventricular and deep white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensity sparing subcortical U-fibers); Negative CSF tap test.

differentials.mimic: Parkinson's Disease (Postural Instability Gait Difficulty - PIGD) (G20)
differentials.overlap: Shuffling gait, freezing of gait, executive cognitive decline.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting tremor, cogwheel rigidity, micrographic handwriting, good response to levodopa; NPH patients have wide-based magnetic gait without pill-rolling tremor.
differentials.workup: DaT-SPECT scan (reduced in PD; normal in NPH); Brain MRI.

red_flags: Magnetic gait: feet appear glued to floor with hesitation on turning and normal leg strength when seated (pathognomonic for NPH).
Disproportionately Enlarged Subarachnoid-Space Hydrocephalus (DESH) on coronal MRI.
Dramatic objective improvement in walking speed and step height within 2-4 hours of a 30-50 mL lumbar puncture CSF drainage.

name: Limbic-Predominant Age-Related TDP-43 Encephalopathy
symptoms: An amnestic neurocognitive disorder in individuals aged 80 and older that clinically mimics Alzheimer's disease (progressive memory loss, executive decline) but is pathologically driven by TDP-43 proteinopathy rather than amyloid-beta, characterized by a slower rate of progression.

differentials.overlap: Amnestic memory deficits, word-finding difficulties, executive impairment in the very old.
differentials.physical_signs: Clinically identical presentation; rate of functional decline in LATE is significantly slower than typical Alzheimer's; occurs predominantly in persons >= 80 years old.
differentials.workup: Amyloid PET scan or Plasma p-tau217 (often negative or low in pure LATE; elevated in Alzheimer's); 3T Brain MRI (disproportionate severe hippocampal sclerosis and amygdalar atrophy out of proportion to neocortical atrophy).

differentials.overlap: Progressive cognitive decline, transient focal neurological episodes ('amyloid spells') in elderly.
differentials.physical_signs: Lobar intracerebral hemorrhages, cortical superficial siderosis.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with T2* Gradient-Echo / SWI (multiple strictly lobar microbleeds, sparing basal ganglia).

differentials.mimic: Occult Vitamin B12 / Folate Malnutrition in Nonagenarians (E53.8)
differentials.overlap: Progressive memory loss, apathy, cognitive slowing, frailty.
differentials.physical_signs: Sensory ataxia, absent ankle reflexes, atrophic glossitis.
differentials.workup: Serum B12, MMA, RBC Folate; Complete blood count.

red_flags: Severe isolated hippocampal atrophy on MRI with negative amyloid/tau biomarkers in an 85-year-old patient (classic for LATE).
Multiple cortical/lobar microbleeds on susceptibility-weighted MRI (Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy).
Significantly slower cognitive progression than expected for typical Alzheimer's disease.

name: Transient Global Amnesia
symptoms: Sudden onset of severe anterograde and retrograde amnesia, accompanied by repetitive questioning, with preserved personal identity, intact higher cognitive functions, and absence of focal neurological signs, resolving completely within 24 hours.

differentials.overlap: Amnestic episodes, confusion, difficulty recalling recent events.
differentials.physical_signs: Episodes typically last < 1 hour (TGA lasts 4-12 hours), recur frequently (often multiple times per year; TGA rarely recurs in > 5-10%), occur upon waking; accompanied by subtle automatisms.
differentials.workup: Prolonged Sleep-deprived Video-EEG (demonstrating temporal epileptiform sharp waves); Brain MRI.

differentials.mimic: Posterior Cerebral Artery (PCA) Stroke / Hippocampal Infarct (I63.9)
differentials.overlap: Sudden memory loss, disorientation.
differentials.physical_signs: Contralateral homonymous hemianopia (visual field cut), visual agnosia, alexia without agraphia; deficits do *not* resolve within 24 hours.
differentials.workup: Urgent Brain MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI showing acute occipital/thalamic/hippocampal infarction); CT Angiography.

differentials.overlap: Inability to recall autobiographical information following severe stress.
differentials.physical_signs: Loss of personal identity (patient does not know their own name; TGA patients always know who they are), absence of perseverative questioning, wandering.
differentials.workup: Structured clinical interview; Psychological assessment.

red_flags: Loss of personal identity (patient does not know their name - indicates Dissociative Amnesia, NOT TGA).
Visual field cut (hemianopia) accompanying acute memory loss (PCA stroke).
Recurrent episodes of morning amnesia lasting < 45 minutes (Transient Epileptic Amnesia).

name: Alcohol-Induced Major NCD / Korsakoff Syndrome
symptoms: A persisting neurocognitive impairment characterized by profound anterograde amnesia (inability to form new declarative memories) and severe retrograde amnesia, accompanied by spontaneous confabulation (fabricating plausible memories to fill memory voids) and lack of insight, occurring in the context of chronic alcohol dependence and thiamine deficiency.

differentials.mimic: Third Ventricle Colloid Cyst / Fornix Damage (G91.8 / D33.0)
differentials.overlap: Severe anterograde memory failure, confabulation, inability to form new memories.
differentials.physical_signs: Episodic paroxysmal severe headaches relieved by lying down, drop attacks, sudden obstructive hydrocephalus.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with contrast (demonstrating smooth round hyperdense cyst at the foramen of Monro compressing the columns of the fornix).

differentials.overlap: Profound anterograde amnesia, emotional blunting, confabulation.
differentials.physical_signs: History of acute febrile encephalopathy, temporal lobe seizures, dysphasia.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (bilateral extensive necrosis and gliosis of mesial temporal lobes and hippocampi); CSF HSV PCR history.

differentials.mimic: Bilateral Anterior Thalamic Infarction (Artery of Percheron Stroke) (I63.9)
differentials.overlap: Sudden onset of profound anterograde amnesia, apathy, confabulation, vertical gaze palsy.
differentials.physical_signs: Vertical gaze paresis, fluctuating somnolence, acute onset.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with DWI (bilateral symmetrical paramedian and anterior thalamic infarctions).

red_flags: Positional headaches and drop attacks with acute memory failure (Third Ventricle Colloid Cyst emergency).
Vertical gaze paresis with sudden bilateral thalamic memory loss (Artery of Percheron infarction).
Ataxia, nystagmus, and gaze palsies in any malnourished alcoholic patient (urgent IV thiamine to prevent progression to permanent Korsakoff syndrome).

name: Paranoid Personality Disorder
symptoms: A pervasive distrust and suspiciousness of others such that their motives are interpreted as malevolent, beginning by early adulthood and present in a variety of contexts (suspects others are exploiting/harming/deceiving them, preoccupied with doubts about loyalty, reluctant to confide, reads hidden demeaning meanings into benign events, bears persistent grudges, perceives attacks on character).

differentials.overlap: Paranoid ideation, suspiciousness, extreme irritability, interpersonal hostility preceding motor signs.
differentials.physical_signs: Subtle choreic twitches of fingers/toes, motor impersistence (tongue), slowing of saccadic eye movements, family history of autosomal dominant movement disorder.
differentials.workup: Targeted HTT gene genetic testing (CAG repeat expansion >= 36); Brain MRI (bilateral caudate head atrophy).

differentials.overlap: Persecutory beliefs, irritability, emotional volatility, sleep disturbance.
differentials.physical_signs: Moon facies, buffalo hump, central obesity with thin extremities, wide purple abdominal striae, proximal muscle weakness.
differentials.workup: 24-hour urinary free cortisol (> 3x ULN); 1 mg overnight Dexamethasone suppression test; Pituitary/adrenal imaging.

differentials.overlap: Suspiciousness that others are whispering or talking behind one's back, social withdrawal, hostile defensiveness.
differentials.physical_signs: Difficulty understanding speech in noise, leaning forward, high-frequency hearing loss on audiometry; paranoia resolves with hearing aids.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive Pure-Tone and Speech Audiometry; Audiology evaluation.

red_flags: Motor impersistence of the tongue or subtle finger chorea (Huntington's disease).
Cushingoid physical habitus: purple abdominal striae, buffalo hump, proximal myopathy.
Suspiciousness that vanishes when properly fitted with hearing aids.

name: Schizoid Personality Disorder
symptoms: A pervasive pattern of detachment from social relationships and a restricted range of expression of emotions in interpersonal settings, beginning by early adulthood (neither desires nor enjoys close relationships, almost always chooses solitary activities, little interest in sexual experiences, takes pleasure in few activities, lacks close friends, indifferent to praise/criticism, emotional coldness/flattened affect).

differentials.overlap: Social detachment, solitary preferences, apparent indifference to peer relationships, flat affect.
differentials.physical_signs: Presence of restricted repetitive behaviors, motor mannerisms, insistence on sameness, sensory hypersensitivities, and developmental history of early childhood communication challenges (absent in schizoid PD).
differentials.workup: ADOS-2; Comprehensive developmental and neurodevelopmental assessment.

differentials.mimic: Subfrontal / Apathy Syndrome / Prefrontal Tumor (D32.0 / C71.1)
differentials.overlap: Emotional flattening, social isolation, apathy, abulia, lack of social drive.
differentials.physical_signs: Frontal release signs (grasp, snout), anosmia, papilledema, executive cognitive deficits.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with and without gadolinium; Comprehensive neuropsychological battery.

differentials.overlap: Profound social withdrawal, lethargy, flattened emotional responsiveness, lack of interest in sex.
differentials.physical_signs: Delayed reflex relaxation, dry coarse skin, periorbital puffiness, cold intolerance, bradycardia.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (> 10 mIU/L); Free T4 (< 0.7 ng/dL); Anti-TPO antibodies.

red_flags: Sensory sensitivities to textures/sounds and restricted motor mannerisms (Autism Spectrum).
Anosmia or papilledema accompanying new-onset social detachment in an adult (subfrontal neoplasm).
Marked delayed reflex relaxation and severe cold intolerance.

name: Schizotypal Personality Disorder (Diagnostic Interface)
symptoms: A pervasive pattern of social and interpersonal deficits marked by acute discomfort with close relationships, cognitive/perceptual distortions, and behavioral eccentricities. DIAGNOSTIC INTERFACE & CROSS-REFERENCE NOTE: Under international nosology (ICD-10 F21 / ICD-11 6A22) and DSM-5-TR, Schizotypal disorder occupies a recognized genetic and phenotypic interface between schizophrenia spectrum conditions and personality pathology. For the complete foundational multidisciplinary differential matrix, laboratory triage, and systemic mimics, refer directly to primary Entry 021 in Chapter 02. The targeted differentials below focus specifically on organic etiologies encountered during personality disorder assessments.

differentials.mimic: Temporal Lobe Epilepsy (Interictal Personality / Geschwind Syndrome) (G40.209)
differentials.overlap: Deeply idiosyncratic mystical/religious preoccupations, hypergraphia (excessive writing), circumstantial speech, viscosity.
differentials.physical_signs: Stereotyped auras (epigastric sensations, olfactory hallucinations), brief absence-like stare, postictal confusion.
differentials.workup: Prolonged Video-EEG monitoring; High-resolution Brain MRI (hippocampal sclerosis).

differentials.overlap: Odd beliefs, social awkwardness, eccentric thinking, cognitive vulnerabilities, high risk of psychosis.
differentials.physical_signs: Hypernasal speech (velopharyngeal insufficiency), history of repaired cleft palate, congenital heart defect, hooded eyelids, bulbous nasal tip.
differentials.workup: Chromosomal Microarray (CMA) or 22q11.2 FISH; Serum calcium and PTH.

differentials.overlap: Magical thinking, odd spiritual beliefs, bodily illusions, social eccentricity.
differentials.physical_signs: Pupillary dilation, track marks, frequent drug paraphernalia.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive Urine Drug Screen (LC-MS panel including synthetic phenethylamines/tryptamines).

red_flags: Hypernasal speech resonance and history of congenital heart surgery (22q11.2 deletion).
Brief paroxysmal olfactory auras or lip smacking preceding mystical ideation (temporal lobe epilepsy).
Sudden late-onset eccentricities in an adult over 40.

name: Antisocial Personality Disorder
symptoms: A pervasive pattern of disregard for and violation of the rights of others occurring since age 15, indicated by >= 3 of: failure to conform to lawful behaviors, deceitfulness (lying, conning), impulsivity, irritability and aggressiveness (frequent fights/assaults), reckless disregard for safety, consistent irresponsibility, lack of remorse, in an individual at least 18 years old with evidence of Conduct Disorder before age 15.

differentials.overlap: Callous sociopathic rule-breaking, shoplifting, financial swindles, total loss of remorse in adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Onset at age 45-65 in an adult with *previously exemplary moral/ethical history*; primitive frontal release signs (grasp/snout), hyperorality.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (bilateral asymmetric frontal/anterior temporal atrophy); FDG-PET scan; Executive cognitive testing.

differentials.mimic: Orbitofrontal Traumatic Brain Injury (Acquired Sociopathy) (F07.0 / S06.9X9A)
differentials.overlap: Reckless disregard for safety, deceitfulness, lack of empathy, explosive aggression.
differentials.physical_signs: Anosmia, impaired decision-making on Iowa Gambling Task, history of traumatic brain injury or ruptured ACoA aneurysm.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with SWI (orbitofrontal / ventromedial prefrontal contusions).

differentials.overlap: Severe impulsivity, behavioral non-compliance, emotional volatility, learning difficulties.
differentials.physical_signs: Tall stature (> 95th percentile), severe nodulocystic acne, mild facial asymmetry, intention tremor, macrocephaly.
differentials.workup: Chromosomal Karyotyping (47,XYY).

red_flags: De novo sociopathic conduct emerging in an adult > 45 years old with no prior criminal or conduct record (FTD).
Anosmia and frontal release signs (grasp reflex) following head injury (acquired sociopathy).
Tall stature, severe cystic acne, and tremor in a youth with aggressive behavioral difficulties (47,XYY).

name: Borderline Personality Disorder
symptoms: A pervasive pattern of instability of interpersonal relationships, self-image, and affects, and marked impulsivity, beginning by early adulthood and present in a variety of contexts, indicated by >= 5 of: frantic efforts to avoid abandonment, unstable/intense relationships (splitting), identity disturbance, impulsivity in >= 2 self-damaging areas, recurrent suicidal behavior/gestures/self-mutilation, affective instability (intense episodic dysphoria/irritability), chronic feelings of emptiness, inappropriate intense anger, transient stress-related paranoid ideation or severe dissociation.

differentials.mimic: Temporal Lobe Epilepsy (Limbic Kindling / Affective Lability) (G40.209)
differentials.overlap: Intense rapid emotional volatility, episodic explosive rage, micro-psychotic episodes, severe dissociation.
differentials.physical_signs: Stereotyped rising epigastric auras, lip-smacking automatisms, postictal confusion, brief episode duration (< 2-3 minutes).
differentials.workup: Prolonged Continuous Video-EEG monitoring with anterior temporal leads; 3T Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Sudden emotional dysregulation, affective volatility, impulsivity, paranoid ideation, memory loss in young females.
differentials.physical_signs: Faciobrachial dystonic seizures, hyponatremia, sleep disturbance, rapid deterioration.
differentials.workup: Serum and CSF Autoimmune Encephalopathy antibody panel; Brain MRI with contrast.

differentials.overlap: Cyclic severe emotional lability, explosive anger, self-harm urges, intense rejection sensitivity.
differentials.physical_signs: Symptoms occur strictly during the final 7-10 days of the luteal phase and completely vanish within days of menses onset, leaving follicular euthymia.
differentials.workup: Prospective Daily Record of Severity of Problems (DRSP) across 2 consecutive cycles.

differentials.overlap: Severe emotional volatility, behavioral disinhibition, rage outbursts, impulsivity in young adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Kayser-Fleischer rings on slit-lamp, wing-beating tremor, dystonia, dysarthria, hepatosplenomegaly.
differentials.workup: Slit-lamp exam; Serum ceruloplasmin (< 20 mg/dL); 24-hr urine copper (> 100 mcg/24h).

red_flags: Paroxysmal brief epigastric auras or lip smacking preceding acute dissociative/rage states (temporal lobe epilepsy).
Kayser-Fleischer corneal rings, tremor, or abnormal liver function in a young emotionally volatile patient (Wilson's disease).
Emotional dysregulation that completely resolves during the post-menstrual follicular week (pure PMDD).
Involuntary facial/arm twitching in a young female with acute emotional collapse (LGI1 encephalitis).

name: Histrionic Personality Disorder
symptoms: A pervasive pattern of excessive emotionality and attention seeking, beginning by early adulthood and present in a variety of contexts, indicated by >= 5 of: uncomfortable when not center of attention, inappropriately sexually seductive/provocative, rapidly shifting/shallow emotions, uses physical appearance to draw attention, impressionistic speech lacking detail, dramatic/theatrical expression, suggestible, considers relationships more intimate than they are.

differentials.overlap: Inappropriate theatricality, disinhibition, facetiousness ('Witzelsucht' - inappropriate joking), dramatic affect in older adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Papilledema, anosmia, primitive frontal release reflexes, focal neurological signs; onset late in life.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with and without gadolinium; Comprehensive neurological evaluation.

differentials.overlap: High psychomotor energy, emotional theatrics, dramatic rapid speech, emotional lability.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting sinus tachycardia, fine hand tremor, warm moist skin, goiter, lid lag, weight loss.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (< 0.01 mIU/L); Free T4 and Free T3; Thyroid antibodies.

differentials.overlap: Flamboyant dress, flirtatious seductive behavior, dramatic speech, boundless energy.
differentials.physical_signs: Episodic course with distinct onset and offset; accompanied by decreased need for sleep and racing thoughts.
differentials.workup: Young Mania Rating Scale; Mood timeline.

red_flags: Late-onset theatrical disinhibition and inappropriate punning/joking ('Witzelsucht') in an older adult (frontal lobe tumor).
Resting tachycardia > 100 bpm and fine hand tremor (hyperthyroidism).
Theatrical flamboyance occurring strictly during distinct sleepless hypomanic episodes.

name: Narcissistic Personality Disorder
symptoms: A pervasive pattern of grandiosity (in fantasy or behavior), need for admiration, and lack of empathy, beginning by early adulthood and present in a variety of contexts, indicated by >= 5 of: grandiose sense of self-importance, preoccupied with fantasies of unlimited success/power/brilliance, believes they are 'special' and unique, requires excessive admiration, sense of entitlement, interpersonally exploitative, lacks empathy, envious of others, arrogant/haughty behaviors or attitudes.

differentials.overlap: Grandiose delusions, belief in special powers/connections, arrogance, entitlement.
differentials.physical_signs: Episodic course; accompanied by decreased need for sleep (sleeping 2 hrs/night without fatigue), pressured speech, racing thoughts; NPD grandiosity is lifelong, stable, and lacks acute sleep reduction.
differentials.workup: Young Mania Rating Scale; Mood episode longitudinal history.

differentials.mimic: Paretic Neurosyphilis (General Paresis of the Insane) (A52.17)
differentials.overlap: Grandiose megalomania, entitlement, extravagant financial schemes, arrogance in adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Argyll Robertson pupils (unreactive to light with preserved accommodation), dysarthric speech, tremor of tongue/hands, sensory ataxia.
differentials.workup: Serum treponemal antibody testing (TP-PA/FTA-ABS); Lumbar puncture (CSF-VDRL, pleocytosis, elevated protein).

differentials.overlap: Grandiosity, entitlement, arrogance, hypervigilance, interpersonal exploitation.
differentials.physical_signs: Mydriasis, tachycardia, hypertension, track marks, nasal mucosal erosion/perforation.
differentials.workup: Urine Drug Screen; Comprehensive toxicology panel.

red_flags: Argyll Robertson pupils and slurred dysarthric speech accompanying grandiose megalomania (Neurosyphilis).
Grandiosity accompanied by sudden reduction in sleep to < 3 hours nightly without fatigue (Bipolar Mania).
Nasal septal perforation and pupillary dilation in an arrogant patient (chronic cocaine misuse).

name: Avoidant Personality Disorder
symptoms: A pervasive pattern of social inhibition, feelings of inadequacy, and hypersensitivity to negative evaluation, beginning by early adulthood and present in a variety of contexts, indicated by >= 4 of: avoids occupational activities involving interpersonal contact due to fear of criticism/rejection, unwilling to get involved unless certain of being liked, restraint in intimate relationships due to fear of shame, preoccupied with being criticized/rejected, inhibited in new interpersonal situations, views self as socially inept/inferior, reluctant to take personal risks.

differentials.overlap: Intense fear of negative evaluation, avoidance of social interactions, social distress.
differentials.physical_signs: Significant diagnostic overlap; Social Anxiety focuses on fear of embarrassment during specific social performances; Avoidant PD represents a pervasive, deeply internalized global identity of personal inferiority and inadequacy.
differentials.workup: Structured Clinical Interview (SCID-5-PD); Social Phobia and Anxiety Inventory (SPAI).

differentials.overlap: Social withdrawal, avoidance of social groups, feeling 'different' or defective.
differentials.physical_signs: History of developmental social communication deficits, literal comprehension, sensory hypersensitivities, exhaustion from 'social masking'.
differentials.workup: ADOS-2; Comprehensive developmental evaluation.

differentials.mimic: Progressive Hearing Loss with Social Withdrawal (H90.3)
differentials.overlap: Reluctance to engage in social conversations, avoidance of group gatherings, feeling inept.
differentials.physical_signs: Difficulty hearing in noisy restaurants, failure to understand group conversations, leaning forward.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive Pure-Tone Audiometry; Speech-in-noise testing.

red_flags: Lifelong sensory aversions and communication challenges dating to early childhood (masked Autism Spectrum).
Social avoidance driven primarily by inability to hear speech in background noise (audiometric loss).
Absence of autonomic panic during solitary activities.

name: Dependent Personality Disorder
symptoms: A pervasive and excessive need to be taken care of that leads to submissive and clinging behavior and fears of separation, beginning by early adulthood and present in a variety of contexts, indicated by >= 5 of: difficulty making everyday decisions without advice/reassurance, needs others to assume responsibility, difficulty expressing disagreement due to fear of loss of support, difficulty initiating projects alone, goes to excessive lengths to obtain nurturance, feels helpless when alone, urgently seeks another relationship when one ends, unrealistically preoccupied with fears of being left to care for self.

differentials.mimic: Mild Intellectual Disability / Executive Function Deficit (F70 / F88)
differentials.overlap: Inability to manage independent living, needing others to make decisions, submissive reliance.
differentials.physical_signs: Objective standardized IQ < 70-75, adaptive functional deficits across conceptual and practical domains; reliance stems from true cognitive incapacity rather than psychological dependency.
differentials.workup: Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale (WAIS-IV); Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales.

differentials.overlap: Profound fatigue, lack of initiative, apathy, helplessness, total reliance on spouse.
differentials.physical_signs: Hypotension, cutaneous hyperpigmentation or pallor, loss of axillary/pubic hair, extreme weakness.
differentials.workup: Morning serum cortisol (< 3 mcg/dL); Cosyntropin stimulation test; Pituitary hormone panel.

differentials.mimic: Early Subtle Apathy Syndrome / Frontal Abulia (G31.89)
differentials.overlap: Total passivity, inability to initiate daily activities without spousal prompting.
differentials.physical_signs: Decreased spontaneous speech, prolonged latency in answering questions, motor impersistence.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI; Standardized executive cognitive testing.

red_flags: Objective IQ score < 70 on standardized neuropsychological testing (Intellectual Disability).
Severe orthostatic hypotension with morning cortisol < 3 mcg/dL (adrenal insufficiency).
Frontal abulia with loss of spontaneous initiative on neurological examination.

name: Obsessive-Compulsive Personality Disorder (OCPD)
symptoms: A pervasive pattern of preoccupation with orderliness, perfectionism, and mental and interpersonal control, at the expense of flexibility, openness, and efficiency, beginning by early adulthood, indicated by >= 4 of: preoccupied with details/rules/lists to the extent that the major point of the activity is lost, perfectionism that interferes with task completion, excessively devoted to work/productivity to the exclusion of leisure/friendships, overconscientious and inflexible about morality/ethics/values, unable to discard worn-out objects, reluctant to delegate, miserly spending style, rigidity and stubbornness (*ego-syntonic*).

differentials.overlap: Preoccupation with order, rules, checking, cleanliness, symmetry.
differentials.physical_signs: OCD features true intrusive, agonizing, distressing obsessions and repetitive neutralizing compulsions that are *ego-dystonic* (the patient hates the thoughts and wants them gone); OCPD features rigid, perfectionistic personality traits that are *ego-syntonic* (the patient believes their way is the correct, superior, and moral way).
differentials.workup: Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS); SCID-5-PD.

differentials.overlap: Inflexible adherence to routines, rigid morality, perfectionism, intense detail focus.
differentials.physical_signs: Presence of nonverbal social communication deficits, literal language interpretation, sensory hypersensitivities, circumscribed special interests.
differentials.workup: ADOS-2; Multidisciplinary developmental assessment.

differentials.mimic: Behavioral Variant Frontotemporal Dementia (Early Rigid Stereotypy) (G31.09)
differentials.overlap: Rigid adherence to clock-watching, rigid schedules, hoarding, inflexible rituals in late middle age.
differentials.physical_signs: Social disinhibition, loss of empathy, hyperorality, primitive frontal reflexes; onset aged 50-65 in an individual with prior normal flexibility.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (frontal lobe atrophy); FDG-PET scan.

red_flags: Rigid, agonizing intrusive obsessions that the patient recognizes as irrational and unwanted (OCD).
Sensory sensitivities to sounds/textures with social communication deficits (Autism Spectrum).
New-onset extreme behavioral rigidity and clock-watching emerging in an adult over 50 (bvFTD).

name: Personality Change Due to Another Medical Condition
symptoms: A persistent personality disturbance that represents a change from the individual's previous characteristic personality pattern, directly attributable to the direct physiological consequences of another medical condition (e.g., frontal lobe lesion, traumatic brain injury, stroke, seizure disorder).

differentials.overlap: Apathy, abulia, loss of initiative, disinhibition, inappropriate joking ('Witzelsucht'), coarse language.
differentials.physical_signs: Papilledema, Foster Kennedy syndrome (ipsilateral optic atrophy + contralateral papilledema + anosmia), frontal release signs (grasp reflex), incontinence.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with and without gadolinium; Fundoscopic exam; Cranial nerve testing.

differentials.overlap: Dramatic personality deterioration, emotional volatility, disinhibition, rage outbursts in young adults.
differentials.physical_signs: Kayser-Fleischer rings on slit-lamp, wing-beating tremor, dystonia, dysarthria, hepatomegaly.
differentials.workup: Slit-lamp exam; Serum ceruloplasmin (< 20 mg/dL); 24-hr urine copper (> 100 mcg/24h); ATP7B gene testing.

differentials.overlap: Profound erosion of social conduct, apathy, loss of empathy, hyperorality.
differentials.physical_signs: Primitive reflexes (snout, root, grasp), striking lack of concern for family distress.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI; FDG-PET scan; Executive cognitive testing.

differentials.overlap: Deepening of religious/philosophical interests, hypergraphia, emotional viscosity, hyposexuality.
differentials.physical_signs: Epigastric auras, lip-smacking automatisms, postictal confusion.
differentials.workup: Prolonged Video-EEG; 3T Brain MRI.

red_flags: Anosmia, papilledema, or unilateral optic atrophy in an adult with sudden personality change (frontal tumor).
Kayser-Fleischer corneal rings or tremor in an adolescent with behavioral breakdown (Wilson's disease).
Primitive grasp reflex or snout reflex on physical examination.

name: Other Specified & Unspecified Personality Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a personality disorder predominate but do not meet full criteria for any specific personality disorder (e.g., mixed personality features), or information is inadequate to specify.

differentials.overlap: Severe irritability, emotional lability, depression, personality changes.
differentials.physical_signs: Moon facies, buffalo hump, central obesity, purple striae (> 1 cm), proximal myopathy.
differentials.workup: 24-hour urinary free cortisol (> 3x ULN); 1 mg Dexamethasone suppression test.

differentials.overlap: Personality changes, irritability, cognitive slowing, chronic fatigue, depressive mood.
differentials.physical_signs: History of tick bite or erythema migrans, peripheral facial palsy, large joint arthritis.
differentials.workup: Serum two-tier Lyme serology (ELISA + Western blot); CSF-to-serum Borrelia antibody index.

differentials.mimic: Cerebral Small Vessel Disease / Lacunar Infarctions (I67.82)
differentials.overlap: Apathy, irritability, emotional lability in older adults with vascular risk factors.
differentials.physical_signs: Pseudobulbar affect (pathologic laughing/crying), hyperreflexia, pronator drift.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (deep white matter leukoaraiosis and lacunar infarcts).

red_flags: Cushingoid habitus with proximal muscle weakness (Cushing's syndrome).
Pathological laughing or crying (pseudobulbar affect) following cerebrovascular disease.
Facial nerve palsy and swollen knee joints with personality changes (Lyme neuroborreliosis).

name: Voyeuristic Disorder
symptoms: Over a period of at least 6 months, recurrent and intense sexual arousal from observing an unsuspecting person who is naked, in the process of disrobing, or engaging in sexual activity, manifested by fantasies, urges, or behaviors, acted upon with a non-consenting person or causing clinically significant distress.

differentials.overlap: Inappropriate sexual peeping, window watching, disinhibition emerging in middle age.
differentials.physical_signs: Onset at age 50-65 in an individual with no prior paraphilic history; primitive frontal release signs (grasp/snout), apathy, hyperorality.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (frontal/temporal atrophy); FDG-PET scan; Executive cognitive testing.

differentials.overlap: Indiscriminate hypersexuality, examining inappropriate objects/people, loss of social fear.
differentials.physical_signs: Visual agnosia (psychic blindness), placidity, putting inedible objects in mouth; following herpes encephalitis or traumatic brain injury.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (bilateral anterior temporal lobe / amygdalar necrosis or encephalomalacia).

differentials.overlap: Compulsive voyeurism, internet pornography obsession, sexual preoccupation.
differentials.physical_signs: Underlying Parkinson's disease or RLS; taking pramipexole, ropinirole; resolves upon drug taper.
differentials.workup: Medication audit; QUIP-RS scale; Dopamine agonist dose reduction.

red_flags: De novo voyeuristic behavior emerging in an adult over 50 with no prior paraphilic history (FTD).
Compulsive sexual browsing and peeping developing after starting pramipexole or ropinirole.
Visual agnosia and hyperorality following herpes encephalitis (Klüver-Bucy syndrome).

name: Exhibitionistic Disorder
symptoms: Over a period of at least 6 months, recurrent and intense sexual arousal from the exposure of one's genitals to an unsuspecting person, manifested by fantasies, urges, or behaviors, acted upon with a non-consenting person or causing significant distress.

differentials.overlap: Disrobing in public, exposing genitals in front of neighbors or store staff.
differentials.physical_signs: Act is carried out with complete nonchalance and lack of sexual arousal or shame (simply feeling hot, wanting to urinate, or total loss of social inhibition); age > 50; primitive frontal reflexes.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (frontal atrophy); Neuropsychological testing.

differentials.overlap: Undressing in public, wandering naked in street, exposing genitalia.
differentials.physical_signs: Occurs in a state of confusion during or immediately after a seizure; accompanied by lip smacking, blank stare, unresponsiveness; absence of sexual pleasure or arousal.
differentials.workup: Prolonged Video-EEG monitoring; Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Public disrobing, sexual exhibitionism, flashing.
differentials.physical_signs: Accompanied by boundless energy, grandiosity, flight of ideas, decreased need for sleep.
differentials.workup: Young Mania Rating Scale; Mood timeline.

red_flags: Disrobing in public occurs during a confusional trance state with lip smacking (ictal automatism).
Public exposure in an older adult without sexual arousal or awareness of social impropriety (FTD).
Disrobing occurs strictly during manic surges of sleeplessness and grandiosity.

name: Frotteuristic Disorder
symptoms: Over a period of at least 6 months, recurrent and intense sexual arousal from touching or rubbing against a non-consenting person, manifested by fantasies, urges, or behaviors, acted upon with a non-consenting person or causing significant distress.

differentials.overlap: Inappropriately touching strangers in public transit, rubbing against people in crowds.
differentials.physical_signs: Age > 50 with no prior history; profound loss of social boundaries, apathy, executive dysfunction on testing.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (bilateral frontal atrophy); FDG-PET scan.

differentials.overlap: Impulsive inappropriate physical contact, touching strangers.
differentials.physical_signs: Anosmia, executive cognitive deficits, documented head injury with loss of consciousness.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with SWI.

differentials.mimic: Severe Autism Spectrum Disorder with Tactile Seeking (F84.0)
differentials.overlap: Touching strangers' clothing or hair in public transit.
differentials.physical_signs: Behavior is driven by sensory tactile seeking (e.g. fascination with silky fabrics or soft fur) rather than sexual arousal; severe social reciprocity deficits.
differentials.workup: ADOS-2; Sensory profile evaluation.

red_flags: Touching strangers' clothing driven strictly by sensory texture seeking without sexual intent (Autism Spectrum).
New-onset inappropriate physical contact in a middle-aged adult with personality changes (FTD).
History of frontal brain trauma preceding disinhibited public touching.

name: Sexual Masochism & Sexual Sadism Disorders
symptoms: Sexual Masochism: Recurrent intense sexual arousal from the act of being humiliated, beaten, bound, or made to suffer (including asphyxiophilia). Sexual Sadism: Recurrent intense sexual arousal from the physical or psychological suffering of another person, acted upon with a non-consenting person or causing distress.

differentials.mimic: Accidental Asphyxial Death (Hypoxyphilia Autoerotic Fatalities) (T71.9 / F65.51)
differentials.overlap: Autoerotic asphyxiation resulting in lethal cerebral hypoxia.
differentials.physical_signs: Ligature marks around neck, complex escape mechanisms that failed, presence of erotic materials at scene, absence of suicide note.
differentials.workup: Forensic autopsy (confirming petechiae, neck ligature marks, absence of toxic suicide levels).

differentials.overlap: Gelastic seizures (paroxysmal laughing), precocious puberty, paraphilic sexual behaviors.
differentials.physical_signs: Stereotyped laughing spells, behavioral disinhibition, endocrine virilization.
differentials.workup: High-resolution Brain MRI (suprasellar hypothalamic hamartoma).

differentials.overlap: Engagement in bondage, dominance, submission, and sadomasochistic erotic themes.
differentials.physical_signs: Activities are completely consensual ('safe, sane, consensual' rules), negotiated with safe words, and cause *zero distress or impairment* (does not meet criteria for a psychiatric disorder).
differentials.workup: Clinical diagnostic interview assessing consent, distress, and impairment.

red_flags: Autoerotic asphyxiation using neck ligatures, plastic bags, or chemical inhalants (extreme risk of fatal cerebral hypoxia).
Gelastic laughing seizures with precocious puberty (hypothalamic hamartoma).
Non-consensual infliction of physical harm or sexual violence.

name: Pedophilic Disorder
symptoms: Over a period of at least 6 months, recurrent and intense sexual arousal from prepubescent children (generally age 13 years or younger), manifested by fantasies, urges, or behaviors, where the individual is at least 16 years old and at least 5 years older than the child, acted upon or causing significant distress.

differentials.overlap: Inappropriate sexual approaches toward children, downloading child pornography in middle age.
differentials.physical_signs: Onset at age 50-65 in an adult with *no prior lifetime history* of pedophilic interests; primitive frontal release reflexes (grasp/snout), apathy, hyperorality, executive collapse.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (bilateral asymmetric frontal/anterior temporal atrophy); FDG-PET scan; Comprehensive neuropsychological evaluation.

differentials.mimic: Right Orbitofrontal / Temporal Neoplasm (e.g., Meningioma) (D32.0 / C71.1)
differentials.overlap: Sudden emergence of pedophilic urges, propositioning minors in an adult.
differentials.physical_signs: Papilledema, anosmia, headaches, memory impairment; surgical resection of tumor leads to complete resolution of pedophilic desires.
differentials.workup: Brain MRI with and without gadolinium.

differentials.mimic: Severe Intellectual Disability with Peer Naivety (F71 / F72)
differentials.overlap: Playing inappropriately with younger children, kissing or touching peers.
differentials.physical_signs: Severe cognitive delay (mental age 6-8 years), developmental naivety; actions represent developmental peer-level play rather than predatory paraphilia.
differentials.workup: Wechsler Adult Intelligence Scale (WAIS-IV); Adaptive functioning assessment.

red_flags: Sudden emergence of pedophilic interests in an adult over 50 with previously normal adult sexuality (demands brain MRI for frontal tumor or FTD).
Papilledema or anosmia on physical examination.
Resolution of paraphilic impulses following surgical removal of a brain tumor.

name: Fetishistic & Transvestic Disorders
symptoms: Fetishistic: Intense sexual arousal from either the use of non-living objects (shoes, rubber, underwear) or a highly specific focus on non-genital body parts. Transvestic: Intense sexual arousal from cross-dressing, occurring in heterosexual or bisexual adolescents/adults, acted upon or causing clinically significant distress.

differentials.overlap: Cross-dressing, wearing clothes of the other gender.
differentials.physical_signs: In Gender Dysphoria, cross-dressing is undertaken to affirm gender identity and reduce dysphoria, *not for sexual arousal or autogynephilic climax*; in Transvestic Disorder, cross-dressing produces direct genital erection/arousal.
differentials.workup: Clinical interview assessing presence of sexual arousal vs authentic gender identity incongruence.

differentials.mimic: Epileptic Paraphilia / Temporal Lobe Focal Seizures (G40.209)
differentials.overlap: Bizarre, stereotyped paraphilic sexual behaviors occurring during seizure activity.
differentials.physical_signs: Stereotyped auras, automatisms, brief duration, postictal confusion.
differentials.workup: Prolonged Video-EEG monitoring; Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Use of fetish objects during consensual intimacy.
differentials.physical_signs: Activities are consensual, cause no personal distress, and do not impair occupational/social functioning (does not meet criteria for a mental disorder).
differentials.workup: Diagnostic assessment confirming absence of distress or impairment.

red_flags: Cross-dressing driven by persistent internal female gender identity rather than sexual arousal (Gender Dysphoria).
Paraphilic behaviors accompanied by ictal automatisms or postictal confusion.
Absence of distress or functional impairment (non-disordered sexual variation).

name: Other Specified & Unspecified Paraphilic Disorder
symptoms: Presentations in which symptoms characteristic of a paraphilic disorder predominate (e.g., telephone scatologia / obscene phone calling, necrophilia, partialism, zoophilia, coprophilia, urophilia) that cause significant distress or impairment.

differentials.overlap: Bizarre, indiscriminate sexual behaviors, attempting to mate with animals or inanimate objects.
differentials.physical_signs: Visual agnosia (psychic blindness), hyperorality (putting everything into mouth), placidity (loss of fear/anger).
differentials.workup: Brain MRI (bilateral anterior temporal lobe / amygdalar necrosis from HSV encephalitis or trauma).

differentials.mimic: Severe Schizophrenia with Bizarre Delusional Sexuality (F20.9)
differentials.overlap: Coprophilia, urophilia, bizarre sexual acts.
differentials.physical_signs: Driven by severe persecutory/mystical delusions or command hallucinations rather than primary erotic paraphilia; disorganized speech, negative symptoms.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive psychiatric evaluation.

differentials.overlap: Emergence of bizarre paraphilic sexual behaviors in a Parkinson's patient.
differentials.physical_signs: Taking high-dose pramipexole or ropinirole; complete remission upon tapering dopamine agonist.
differentials.workup: Medication audit; QUIP-RS scale.

red_flags: Visual agnosia and putting non-food items in mouth following viral encephalitis (Klüver-Bucy syndrome).
Bizarre sexual behaviors driven by active command auditory hallucinations.
Emergence of bizarre sexual obsessions following dopamine agonist dose escalation.

name: Neuroleptic-Induced Parkinsonism
symptoms: Parkinsonian tremor, muscular rigidity, or bradykinesia developing within a few weeks of starting or raising the dose of a neuroleptic medication (dopamine D2 receptor antagonist) or after reducing a medication used to treat extrapyramidal symptoms.

differentials.overlap: Resting tremor, cogwheel rigidity, bradykinesia, masked facies, shuffling gait.
differentials.physical_signs: Idiopathic PD features *asymmetric* motor onset (starts in one hand/arm), prominent 4-6 Hz pill-rolling rest tremor; Neuroleptic parkinsonism is typically *symmetric* from the onset and features more prominent rigidity/bradykinesia than tremor.
differentials.workup: DaT-SPECT scan (abnormal reduced striatal uptake in Idiopathic PD; completely normal striatal presynaptic transporter uptake in drug-induced parkinsonism!).

differentials.mimic: Dementia with Lewy Bodies (Extreme Neuroleptic Sensitivity) (G31.83)
differentials.overlap: Severe, catastrophic parkinsonian rigidity, catatonia, or NMS upon receiving low-dose antipsychotics.
differentials.physical_signs: Pre-existing visual hallucinations, cognitive fluctuations, REM sleep behavior disorder.
differentials.workup: DaT-SPECT scan; Clinical McKeith criteria; Immediate discontinuation of all typical/atypical antipsychotics.

differentials.overlap: Parkinsonian rigidity, tremor, dysarthria in a young psychotic patient.
differentials.physical_signs: Kayser-Fleischer rings on slit-lamp, wing-beating tremor, dystonia, hepatomegaly.
differentials.workup: Slit-lamp exam; Serum ceruloplasmin (< 20 mg/dL); 24-hr urine copper (> 100 mcg/24h).

red_flags: Normal DaT-SPECT scan (definitively confirms drug-induced parkinsonism over idiopathic Parkinson's disease).
Catastrophic motor freezing or catatonia following a single low dose of an antipsychotic (Dementia with Lewy Bodies).
Kayser-Fleischer corneal rings on slit-lamp exam (Wilson's disease).

name: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS)
symptoms: A life-threatening medical emergency developing in association with the use of neuroleptic agents, characterized by: (1) Severe generalized 'lead-pipe' muscle rigidity, (2) Hyperthermia (temperature often > 38.0-40.0 C / 100.4-104 F), (3) Autonomic storm (diaphoresis, resting tachycardia, labile blood pressure, tachypnea, sialorrhea), and (4) Altered mental status (delirium, stupor, mutism, catatonia).

differentials.overlap: Hyperthermia, delirium, autonomic instability, diaphoresis, muscle rigidity.
differentials.physical_signs: Serotonin syndrome features spontaneous clonus, inducible clonus, ocular clonus, tremor, and hyperreflexia (markedly pronounced in lower extremities); NMS features *lead-pipe generalized rigidity without clonus* and hyporeflexia.
differentials.workup: Hunter criteria; Serum CPK; Medication audit (serotonergic vs dopamine antagonist drugs).

differentials.overlap: Severe generalized muscle rigidity, explosive hyperthermia (> 41 C), tachycardia, rhabdomyolysis.
differentials.physical_signs: Triggered within minutes/hours of exposure to volatile halogenated inhalational anesthetics (sevoflurane, desflurane) or succinylcholine; masseter spasm.
differentials.workup: Immediate IV Dantrolene; Arterial blood gas (severe mixed metabolic and respiratory acidosis); RYR1 gene testing.

differentials.overlap: Hyperthermia, extreme rigidity, autonomic storm, mutism.
differentials.physical_signs: Preceded by prolonged prodrome of intense psychotic excitement and motor agitation *before* antipsychotic administration; responds dramatically to IV lorazepam or urgent ECT.
differentials.workup: Bush-Francis Catatonia Rating Scale; Serum CPK; Emergent ECT consultation.

differentials.overlap: High fever, altered sensorium, tachycardia, diaphoresis, leukocytosis.
differentials.physical_signs: Nuchal rigidity (meningismus), petechial rash, absence of lead-pipe generalized limb rigidity.
differentials.workup: Lumbar puncture; Blood cultures; Serum lactate; Procalcitonin.

red_flags: Serum Creatine Kinase (CK) markedly elevated > 1,000 to > 50,000 U/L (rhabdomyolysis and myoglobinuric acute renal failure emergency).
Lead-pipe rigidity with temperature > 38.5 C and autonomic lability (immediate discontinuation of all neuroleptics and ICU admission).
Spontaneous or inducible clonus in lower extremities (demands Hunter criteria evaluation for Serotonin Syndrome).

name: Medication-Induced Acute Dystonia
symptoms: Abnormal, prolonged, painful tonic contractions of muscles (eyes, head, neck, limbs, or trunk) developing within hours or days of starting or raising the dose of a neuroleptic agent or after reducing an antiparkinsonian agent (oculogyric crisis, torticollis, retrocollis, trismus, laryngeal dystonia).

differentials.overlap: Severe painful sustained muscle spasms, trismus ('lockjaw'), arching back.
differentials.physical_signs: Trismus, risus sardonicus (pathognomonic sneering facial spasm), opisthotonos (extreme hyperextension of back), history of dirty wound/puncture, lack of tetanus vaccination; *lack of response* to anticholinergic agents.
differentials.workup: Spatula test (touching posterior pharyngeal wall produces involuntary reflex spasm of masseter / biting spatula); Wound culture; Immediate Tetanus Immune Globulin (TIG).

differentials.overlap: Painful sustained muscle spasms, carpopedal spasms, laryngeal stridor.
differentials.physical_signs: Chvostek sign positive (facial twitching on tapping facial nerve), Trousseau sign positive (carpopedal spasm on BP cuff inflation), prolonged QTc on ECG.
differentials.workup: Serum total calcium (< 8.0 mg/dL) and ionized calcium; Intact PTH; 12-lead ECG.

differentials.overlap: Abnormal head turning, eye deviation, stiffening of arm.
differentials.physical_signs: Brief paroxysmal duration (< 60-90 seconds), clonic jerking, postictal confusion; acute dystonia lasts hours without treatment.
differentials.workup: Routine / Video-EEG; Brain MRI.

differentials.overlap: Fixed abnormal posture of neck, hand, or foot.
differentials.physical_signs: Fixed non-physiologic posture from onset (organic dystonia is mobile early), distractibility, entrainment, absence of neuroleptic exposure.
differentials.workup: Neurological examination assessing distractibility and Hoover sign.

red_flags: Laryngeal dystonia / stridor (acute airway emergency requiring immediate IV diphenhydramine 50 mg or benztropine 2 mg and emergency airway preparation).
Oculogyric crisis (eyes locked in sustained upward gaze) following neuroleptic exposure.
Trismus with risus sardonicus and opisthotonos following a dirty puncture wound (Tetanus).
Positive Chvostek and Trousseau signs with prolonged QTc on ECG (hypocalcemic tetany).

name: Medication-Induced Acute Akathisia
symptoms: Subjective complaints of intense restlessness, accompanied by observed excessive movements (fidgeting of legs, rocking from foot to foot, pacing, inability to sit or stand still), developing within days to weeks of starting or raising the dose of a neuroleptic, antidepressant, or antiemetic agent.

differentials.overlap: Severe motor agitation, pacing, distress, inability to sit still.
differentials.physical_signs: Akathisia is an inner motor restlessness localized to the limbs/body without exacerbation of hallucinations/delusions; misdiagnosing akathisia as 'worsening psychosis' and increasing the antipsychotic dose dramatically worsens akathisia and can provoke violent suicide or homicide.
differentials.workup: Barnes Akathisia Rating Scale (BARS); Trial of Propranolol (10-40 mg) or dose reduction resolves motor pacing.

differentials.overlap: Urge to move legs, pacing, restlessness.
differentials.physical_signs: RLS occurs characteristically at night/in bed and is preceded by uncomfortable paresthesias in the calves; akathisia is present throughout the entire day and is experienced as a generalized motor urge.
differentials.workup: Serum Ferritin; Clinical criteria.

differentials.overlap: Severe restlessness, fidgeting, anxiety, fine tremor, insomnia.
differentials.physical_signs: Resting sinus tachycardia, warm moist skin, goiter, lid lag, weight loss.
differentials.workup: Serum TSH (< 0.01 mIU/L); Free T4 and Free T3.

red_flags: Severe distress, profound pacing, and acute suicidal agitation emerging within days of starting an antipsychotic or SSRI (akathisia-driven suicide risk).
Mistaking akathisia for worsening psychotic agitation (demands immediate BARS assessment; do NOT increase antipsychotic dose!).
Resting tachycardia > 100 bpm and fine hand tremor (hyperthyroidism).

name: Tardive Dyskinesia & Tardive Dystonia
symptoms: Involuntary choreiform, athetoid, or rhythmic stereotyped movements (tongue protrusion, lip smacking, puckering, chewing, grimacing, choreic movements of fingers/toes, pelvic thrusting) or sustained dystonic posturing, developing in association with the use of a neuroleptic medication for at least a few months (or 1 month in patients >= 60 years old).

differentials.overlap: Choreiform movements of face, fingers, trunk, cognitive deficits, psychiatric symptoms.
differentials.physical_signs: Motor impersistence (inability to sustain tongue protrusion on command - 'milkmaid's grip'), saccadic slowing, autosomal dominant family history; chorea affects gait and whole body; TD chorea is stereotypic and classic buccolingual.
differentials.workup: Targeted HTT gene genetic testing (CAG repeats >= 36); Brain MRI (caudate head atrophy).

differentials.overlap: Orofacial dyskinesias, dystonia, tremor, dysarthria in young psychotic patients.
differentials.physical_signs: Kayser-Fleischer rings on slit-lamp, wing-beating tremor, hepatomegaly.
differentials.workup: Slit-lamp exam; Serum ceruloplasmin (< 20 mg/dL); 24-hr urine copper (> 100 mcg/24h).

differentials.overlap: Repetitive chewing and mouth movements in elderly patients.
differentials.physical_signs: Mouth movements vanish when dentures are properly seated or removed; tongue movements do *not* involve true lingual chorea/worm-like writhing.
differentials.workup: Comprehensive dental and oral prosthodontic examination.

differentials.mimic: Spontaneous Orofacial Dyskinesia of the Elderly (Senile Chorea) (G25.5)
differentials.overlap: Masticatory mouth movements in older adults with no neuroleptic history.
differentials.physical_signs: Absence of lifetime neuroleptic or dopamine antagonist exposure; very slow progression.
differentials.workup: Medication audit; Brain MRI.

red_flags: Motor impersistence (inability to keep tongue protruded for 10 seconds) with family history of chorea (Huntington's disease).
Kayser-Fleischer corneal rings or liver cirrhosis stigmata (Wilson's disease).
Worsening of dyskinesia upon neuroleptic withdrawal (withdrawal-emergent dyskinesia).
VMAT2 inhibitor therapy (valbenazine, deutetrabenazine) indicated for verified tardive dyskinesia.

name: Antidepressant Discontinuation Syndrome
symptoms: FINISH syndrome developing within 2-4 days of abrupt cessation or rapid tapering of an antidepressant (especially paroxetine or venlafaxine with short half-lives): (1) Flu-like symptoms (fatigue, myalgias, chills), (2) Insomnia, (3) Nausea, (4) Imbalance (dizziness, vertigo, ataxia), (5) Sensory disturbances (pathognomonic 'brain zaps', electric shock sensations, paresthesias), and (6) Hyperarousal (anxiety, agitation, irritability), resolving rapidly upon reinstatement.

differentials.overlap: Dysphoric mood, tearfulness, irritability, fatigue, insomnia.
differentials.physical_signs: FINISH symptoms emerge within 1-3 days of missing doses and feature physical neuro-sensory symptoms ('brain zaps', electric shock sensations down limbs, vertigo) that are *absent* in primary depression; resolves within hours of taking a missed dose.
differentials.workup: Medication discontinuation timeline; Rechallenge with original antidepressant dose (prompt relief confirms discontinuation syndrome).

differentials.overlap: Severe vertigo, nausea, vomiting, gait unsteadiness.
differentials.physical_signs: Spontaneous horizontal nystagmus with fast phase beating away from affected ear; abnormal head impulse test; absence of 'brain zaps' or electric sensations.
differentials.workup: HINTS examination (Head Impulse, Nystagmus, Test of Skew); Pure-tone audiogram.

differentials.mimic: Acute Viral Influenza / Upper Respiratory Infection (J11.1)
differentials.overlap: Fever, chills, myalgias, fatigue, headache, nausea.
differentials.physical_signs: Fever on thermometer, cough, rhinorrhea, pharyngitis; absence of brain zaps or paresthesias.
differentials.workup: Rapid influenza / COVID-19 PCR swab.

red_flags: Pathognomonic electric shock sensations in the brain or limbs ('brain zaps') triggered by lateral eye movements.
Complete resolution of severe dizziness, nausea, and emotional distress within 2-4 hours of taking a single dose of the discontinued antidepressant.
Abnormal HINTS exam with unidirectional nystagmus (vestibular neuritis).
